We hypothesize a separable, near-orthogonal latent 'temporal-proximity' axis, decodable at read time, that encodes closeness of a claim's referenced time to the subjective now, distinct from the belief-valence/truth direction and from the model's raw temporal-distance manifold; and a 'proximity-truth leakage' signature: the degree to which near-present framing pulls the truth readout up (and distant framing pulls it down), predictive per item of overbelieving near-present claims and underbelieving temporally-distant ones, holding content and evidence fixed. Using claims whose propositional content and truth are held constant while their referenced time is varied across a proximity ladder (near-present vs distant past/future), we fit a proximity axis, measure separability via cross-decoding, quantify per-item leakage against the log-compressed distance representation, and connect it to behavioral belief shifts. Double-dissociation steering tests whether suppressing leakage makes belief time-invariant (removing the bias) and amplifying it induces present-favoring belief, without changing the model's temporal comprehension, with norm-matched and shuffled-direction controls across three model families. Our results recast a classic present-bias mechanistically as a decodable, steerable contamination of the truth representation.
Experiments: 1. Direction setup. On LLaMA-3-8B-Instruct, Mistral-7B-Instruct, and Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct, fit a frozen belief-valence/truth direction on standard true/false statement datasets (cities, sp_en_trans, larger_than and negations; Marks & Tegmark) with mass-mean and logistic-regression probes at the best layer; validate on held-out atomics; also isolate the polarity-robust general-truth direction (Truth is Universal) as a control. Separately fit a raw TEMPORAL-DISTANCE direction that decodes how far a referenced year is from the model's subjective 'now' (following Language Models Represent Space and Time / The Other Mind constructions), and first calibrate the model's subjective reference year via a similarity-judgment task, so proximity is measured relative to the model's own 'now'.

2. Proximity stimulus construction. Build ~500 verifiable propositions whose TRUTH does not depend on time (stable facts, general claims, and time-anchorable-but-content-fixed statements), and render each with an explicit referenced TIME spanning a proximity ladder around the calibrated subjective now: near-present, moderate past/future, and distant past/future (e.g., 'In [year], water boils at 100C at sea level'; hypothetical/reported events set at varying times whose asserted content is fixed). Hold propositional content and evidence constant across the ladder so only temporal proximity varies; balance past vs future to separate proximity from directionality. Include time-neutral controls. Use paraphrase templates; reserve held-out propositions/templates/years for transfer.

3. Temporal-proximity axis fitting and separability. Extract activations over the proposition span and fit a linear probe (regression on graded proximity; and near-vs-distant classification) to decode temporal proximity to now, controlling for truth-value. Report R^2/AUROC vs shuffled-label controls; measure cosine similarity and cross-decoding between the proximity axis, the truth/belief-valence direction, and the raw temporal-distance direction to establish that proximity-onto-truth is (i) near-orthogonal to truth and (ii) not merely the log-compressed distance manifold (the leakage must be a distinct component that moves the TRUTH readout, beyond decoding distance). Localize the best layer.

4. Proximity-truth leakage metric. For each proposition, project onto the frozen truth direction and measure how far the truth readout is pulled by temporal proximity holding content and truth fixed (leakage = shift toward 'true' attributable to nearness-to-now rather than content, calibrated per model). Core predictions: near-present-framed claims read truer than identical distant-framed claims; leakage decays with temporal distance following the log-compressed (Weber-Fechner) profile (larger per-year effect near now); and the decoded distance readout is unchanged in a way that would explain the truth shift (dissociating overweighting from mere distance encoding). Report leakage across the proximity ladder and past/future symmetry with effect sizes.

5. Behavioral belief-shift prediction. Elicit the model's true/false judgment and confidence per rendering. Score two failures: (a) OVERBELIEF = higher endorsement of near-present-framed claims; (b) UNDERBELIEF = lower endorsement of temporally-distant-framed identical claims. Test whether per-item leakage predicts these shifts via logistic regression; report AUROC vs baselines (truth margin, raw temporal-distance axis, output entropy, referenced-year surface value, item length).

6. Dissociation from temporal-distance encoding and truth (core). Contrast matched-content/varied-proximity items to show the proximity-truth axis and leakage predict belief shifts beyond the belief-valence and raw temporal-distance axes; verify the model's temporal COMPREHENSION (via the distance probe and simple year/ordering checks) is unchanged across proximity conditions, so the effect is truth-contamination, not altered time perception. Report incremental predictive power in nested models.

7. Double-dissociation causal steering. Steer the temporal-proximity axis (orthogonalized against belief-valence and the raw temporal-distance direction) at read time on held-out items. Predict: suppressing leakage makes belief time-invariant (near and distant renderings of the same claim judged equally) WITHOUT changing the model's temporal comprehension or time-neutral controls; amplifying it induces present-favoring belief. As controls, steer belief-valence (should flip truth judgments generally) and the raw temporal-distance direction (should shift perceived year/distance, not proximity-driven truth). Use norm-matched random-direction and shuffled-direction controls; sweep strengths and layers. Metric: change in near-vs-distant belief gap with unchanged temporal comprehension and content accuracy.

8. Application and robustness. Build a training-free diagnostic that flags temporal-proximity-driven belief distortion and steers to debias; on a held-out set (including reasoning about historical vs future claims and time-anchored risk/factual judgments) measure reduction in the proximity gap while preserving accurate temporal reasoning (report gap reduction, accuracy retention, ECE vs a truth-probe-only baseline). Replicate across three model families and two probe methods; transfer the fitted axis, leakage metric, and steering to held-out propositions/templates/years without refitting; report per-template consistency under paraphrase and sensitivity to layer choice and to the calibrated subjective reference year. As a human-parallel analysis, check whether the leakage profile qualitatively matches the human present-bias/log-compression signature (steeper near now, present favored over both past and future).
Risk Factors and Limitations: The proximity-truth axis may not be separable from the truth direction or the raw temporal-distance manifold; we report cosine similarity, cross-decoding, orthogonalized steering, and incremental predictive power, and—because content and truth are held fixed while referenced time varies—truth cannot trivially explain separability; near-collapse (proximity-truth being merely the distance manifold or truth) is an informative negative result showing time encoding does not leak onto truth.

The core risk is that varying the referenced time inadvertently changes the claim's plausibility, familiarity (pretraining frequency of the year), or genuine truth (some facts are time-dependent); we use content whose truth is time-invariant, validate truth parity across renderings with human annotation, control for year frequency, and include time-neutral controls.

Proximity is signaled by explicit year/time tokens that could act as surface features rather than a genuine proximity-to-now abstraction; we mitigate with diverse paraphrase templates, numeric-vs-verbal time framings, past/future balancing, and held-out-year transfer, testing whether the axis predicts belief beyond a raw referenced-year surface baseline.
The subjective 'now' is model-dependent and may drift; we calibrate the reference year per model via similarity judgment and report sensitivity to the calibrated now.

Truth/belief probes are brittle to context and surface form; we validate probes, use the polarity-robust general-truth direction, use paraphrases, standardize readout spans, and report per-template consistency.

The leakage metric relies on a linear projection and per-model calibration; nonlinear leakage could be missed, so we treat it as a lower bound and report probe-fit diagnostics, cross-checking with behavioral belief shifts.
The effect may be weak or absent (LLMs may keep truth time-invariant); a null result is itself an informative human-vs-machine comparison, reported via effect sizes across the proximity ladder.

Causal steering is sensitive to layer and strength; we use orthogonalized steering vectors, norm-matched and shuffled-direction controls, sweep strengths, and verify proximity-debiasing makes belief time-invariant without altering temporal comprehension or degrading time-neutral accuracy.

Findings on 7-8B instruct models may not transfer to frontier scale (the subjective-now and log-compression effects strengthen with scale per The Other Mind); three-family replication and held-out transfer provide reasonable academic-budget coverage, with scale trends noted as future work.

Name: uncertainty_source_belief_axis
Title: Won't-Know vs. Don't-Know: A Latent Uncertainty-Source Axis and the Machine Reducibility Confusion that Misroutes Repair
Short Hypothesis: When an LLM is uncertain, it represents WHY it is uncertain—whether the uncertainty is REDUCIBLE/epistemic (the answer is knowable, it just lacks the information) versus IRREDUCIBLE/aleatoric (no fact of the matter, an inherently random outcome, or genuinely underspecified)—along a separable, near-orthogonal latent 'uncertainty-source' axis distinct from the magnitude of uncertainty (total confidence/entropy) and from the belief-valence/truth direction; the degree to which the two sources are conflated (a 'reducibility-confusion' signature) is decodable before the model acts, causally predicts and drives the misrouted-repair failure—seeking/retrieving information when information cannot help (treating aleatoric as epistemic) and giving up or guessing when information would help (treating epistemic as aleatoric)—and can be steered to route repair correctly.
Related Work: A large ML literature disentangles epistemic (reducible) from aleatoric (irreducible) uncertainty, mostly via output-distribution / ensemble / second-order methods (Kendall & Gal 2017; Huellermeier & Waegeman 2021; Credal-set separation 2026). In LLM interpretability, AU-Probe (2026) shows aleatoric uncertainty from input AMBIGUITY is linearly decodable in the residual stream and gates a clarify-before-answer policy; verbal-vs-semantic uncertainty is a single linear feature (Calibrating Verbal Uncertainty 2025); confidence-regulation entropy neurons modulate total uncertainty (2024); and 'road not taken' work shows uncertainty-linked steerability (2025). Crucially, AU-Probe isolates aleatoric alone (ambiguity detection) and treats it as a magnitude to gate clarification; NONE isolates the uncertainty SOURCE as a decodable axis SEPARABLE from uncertainty magnitude and from truth, defines a reducibility-confusion metric (aleatoric read as epistemic or vice versa), or causally links source-confusion to MISROUTED repair (retrieving/searching when it cannot help vs. abstaining/guessing when it would help). Prior epistemic/aleatoric disentanglement is behavioral/output-based, not a mechanistic belief-about-one's-own-uncertainty axis with a causal repair-routing consequence. This differs from my prior epistemic_state_geometry (know/don't-know x true/false for delusions vs abstainable errors—a magnitude-and-valence plane, not the reducible-vs-irreducible SOURCE), disbelief_vs_absence (falsity vs ignorance), falsifiability (empirical testability of a meaningful claim), contestedness (social dispute), and vetting_status (was-it-checked). Here the cut is the CAUSE of the model's own uncertainty and the correct action it licenses (retrieve vs clarify/abstain). We move from 'aleatoric ambiguity is decodable and gates clarification' to 'the model represents whether its uncertainty is reducible, conflates the two, and this confusion causally misroutes repair.'
Abstract: A capable reasoner faced with uncertainty must know not just how unsure it is, but WHY: a question it merely doesn't know the answer to (reducible/epistemic uncertainty) should trigger looking it up, whereas a question with no fact of the matter or an inherently random outcome (irreducible/aleatoric uncertainty) should trigger acknowledging the limit—retrieving more information there is futile. As LLMs act as agents that decide whether to search, ask, abstain, or guess, we ask whether they represent the SOURCE of their own uncertainty and whether confusing the two misroutes their repair. Prior work shows LLMs linearly encode aleatoric ambiguity and total uncertainty, but none isolates a representation of uncertainty's reducibility separable from its magnitude, nor links source-confusion to misrouted action. We hypothesize a separable, near-orthogonal latent 'uncertainty-source' axis, decodable before the model acts, distinguishing reducible from irreducible uncertainty, distinct from the uncertainty-magnitude and belief-valence/truth directions; a 'reducibility-confusion' signature—aleatoric uncertainty read as epistemic or vice versa—predictive per item of misrouted repair (futile retrieval on unanswerable/random questions; premature abstention/guessing on knowable ones); and steerability to route repair correctly. Using questions that orthogonally vary uncertainty magnitude and its source (retrievable-but-unknown, genuinely random-outcome, no-fact-of-the-matter/underspecified), we fit a source axis, measure separability via cross-decoding, quantify per-item confusion, connect it to behavioral repair-routing, and perform double-dissociation steering with norm-matched and shuffled-direction controls across three model families. Our results recast a foundational uncertainty distinction mechanistically as a decodable, steerable belief about one's own uncertainty that governs whether repair is aimed correctly.
Experiments: 1. Direction setup. On LLaMA-3-8B-Instruct, Mistral-7B-Instruct, and Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct, fit a frozen belief-valence/truth direction on standard true/false statement datasets (cities, sp_en_trans, larger_than and negations; Marks & Tegmark) with mass-mean and logistic-regression probes at the best layer; validate on held-out atomics. Separately fit an UNCERTAINTY-MAGNITUDE/total-confidence direction (from empirical answer-stability / output entropy contrasts, following verbal-uncertainty and confidence constructions), so uncertainty SOURCE can be dissociated from how uncertain the model is.

2. Source x magnitude stimulus construction. Build ~500 questions crossing (i) UNCERTAINTY MAGNITUDE (confident vs uncertain) with (ii) uncertainty SOURCE: (a) REDUCIBLE/epistemic—the answer is a determinate fact the model happens not to know (long-tail facts, lookupable specifics), (b) IRREDUCIBLE—RANDOM (inherently stochastic future outcomes: 'will a fair coin land heads', unpredictable events), and (c) IRREDUCIBLE—NO-FACT/UNDERSPECIFIED (no determinate answer: genuinely subjective/ambiguous or missing-key-variable questions, adapting AU-Probe-style ambiguity). Include CONFIDENT-KNOWN controls. Crucially, the model is UNCERTAIN in both (a) and (b)/(c), but only (a)'s uncertainty is reducible by retrieval. Use paraphrase templates; reserve held-out items/templates for transfer.

3. Uncertainty-source axis fitting and separability. Extract activations at a fixed pre-action readout position (after the question, before the model answers/acts) and fit a linear probe to decode REDUCIBLE vs IRREDUCIBLE source, controlling for uncertainty magnitude. Report AUROC vs shuffled-label controls; measure cosine similarity and cross-decoding among the source axis, the uncertainty-magnitude direction, and the belief-valence/truth direction to establish that source is (i) near-orthogonal to magnitude (the decisive diagnostic: matched-uncertain items differing only in reducibility) and (ii) not merely truth. Localize the best layer.

4. Reducibility-confusion metric. Define per-item confusion as the source axis reading toward EPISTEMIC on irreducible items (aleatoric-as-epistemic) or toward ALEATORIC on reducible items (epistemic-as-aleatoric), calibrated per model. Compare across source cells at matched magnitude; core prediction: substantial aleatoric-as-epistemic confusion (the model treats unanswerable/random questions as merely-unknown), and some epistemic-as-aleatoric confusion (treating knowable-but-obscure questions as hopeless).

5. Behavioral misrouted-repair prediction. Give the model a repair menu (attempt/guess, retrieve/search or ask for the missing fact, request clarification, or acknowledge no-fact/inherent-randomness) and score misrouted repair: (a) FUTILE RETRIEVAL = seeking information on irreducible items where information cannot help; (b) PREMATURE GIVE-UP = abstaining/guessing on reducible items where retrieval would resolve it. Test whether per-item reducibility-confusion predicts misrouted repair via logistic regression; report AUROC vs baselines (uncertainty-magnitude axis, belief-valence margin, output entropy, source-condition surface cues, item length).

6. Dissociation from uncertainty magnitude and truth (core). On matched-magnitude items differing only in source, show the source axis (not the magnitude or truth axes) predicts repair-routing—establishing a genuine belief about uncertainty's reducibility rather than repackaged total uncertainty. Report incremental predictive power in nested models.

7. Double-dissociation causal steering. At the pre-action position on held-out items, steer along the uncertainty-source axis (orthogonalized against the magnitude and belief-valence directions). Predict: steering irreducible items toward the ALEATORIC pole suppresses futile retrieval (the model acknowledges the limit) and steering reducible items toward the EPISTEMIC pole promotes appropriate retrieval—routing repair correctly WITHOUT changing how uncertain the model is on matched controls; opposite steering induces the misroutes. As controls, steer the magnitude axis (should shift overall hedging/abstention regardless of source) and belief-valence (should shift truth judgments). Use norm-matched random-direction and shuffled-direction controls; sweep strengths and layers. Metric: change in futile-retrieval / premature-give-up rate vs unchanged uncertainty magnitude and confident-control behavior.

8. Application, introspection, and robustness. Build a training-free agentic-reliability diagnostic that flags source-confusion and routes repair (search only when reducible; clarify/acknowledge when irreducible); in a simple tool-augmented setting measure reduction in wasted retrieval on unanswerable/random queries and improved resolution of knowable ones vs an uncertainty-magnitude-gated baseline (e.g. AU-Probe-style clarify gating). Test whether prompting the model to introspect ('could looking this up resolve your uncertainty, or is there no knowable answer?') aligns with the latent source axis (verbalization-failure rate; cross-model baseline control). Replicate across three model families and two probe methods; transfer the fitted axis, confusion metric, and steering to held-out items/templates and an independent answerable-vs-unanswerable / random-outcome set without refitting; report per-template consistency under paraphrase and sensitivity to layer/readout position.
Risk Factors and Limitations: The uncertainty-source axis may not be separable from the uncertainty-magnitude direction or the belief-valence direction; we report cosine similarity, cross-decoding, orthogonalized steering, and incremental predictive power, and—because matched-magnitude items differ only in reducibility—magnitude cannot trivially explain separability; near-collapse (source being merely magnitude, as prior AU/confidence work might predict) is an informative negative result showing LLMs do not represent uncertainty's reducibility distinctly.

Constructing clean REDUCIBLE vs IRREDUCIBLE items is delicate: the reducible/irreducible status is partly model-relative (a fact the model cannot retrieve without tools is functionally irreducible in-context) and philosophically fuzzy (future randomness vs mere ignorance); we operationalize reducibility as 'resolvable by available retrieval/clarification' vs not, validate with human annotation and by checking whether providing the missing information actually resolves the item, and report sensitivity.

Source may be signaled by surface cues (question type words: 'will', 'what year', 'is it better') rather than a genuine reducibility abstraction; we mitigate with diverse paraphrase templates, matched-magnitude controls, source-condition surface baselines, and held-out-template transfer, testing whether the axis predicts repair-routing beyond surface features.

The misrouted-repair phenomenon may be weak or RLHF-shaped (aligned models may already route reasonably, or may over-abstain); a null/small result is itself informative, reported via per-model base rates against the correct-routing benchmark.
Belief/truth and magnitude probes are brittle to context and surface form; we validate probes, use paraphrases, standardize the pre-action readout position, and report per-template consistency.

The source signal and confusion metric are linear projections that may miss nonlinear structure (belief manifolds can be curved); we treat them as lower bounds and report probe-fit diagnostics, cross-checking with behavioral repair-routing.
Behavioral repair-routing scoring depends on the repair-menu framing; we test multiple menus/phrasings and report sensitivity.

Causal steering is sensitive to layer and strength; we use orthogonalized steering vectors, norm-matched and shuffled-direction controls, sweep strengths, and verify source steering re-routes repair without altering uncertainty magnitude or degrading confident-control behavior.
The introspection link risks conflating prompt-driven behavior with genuine access; we use cross-model baselines per prior introspection critiques.

Findings on 7-8B instruct models may not transfer to frontier or reasoning/agent-tuned models; three-family replication, an agentic-tool application, and independent-set transfer provide reasonable academic-budget coverage.

Name: fabrication_contamination_axis
Title: Coming to Believe Its Own Lies: A Latent Fabrication-Residue Signal that Contaminates an LLM's Later Belief in the Truth
Short Hypothesis: Mirroring the human finding that fabricating a falsehood contaminates later memory for the truth (people come to believe their own lies), when an LLM is instructed to fabricate a specific false claim earlier in a session, its internal belief in the TRUE fact is later degraded relative to a matched no-fabrication baseline; this contamination is carried by a separable, near-orthogonal latent 'fabrication-residue' signal, distinct from the belief-valence/truth direction and from a generic instructed-deception direction, that is decodable before a later independent truth query, causally predicts and drives the model asserting its own earlier fabrication as fact, and can be steered to erase or amplify the self-contamination.
Related Work: Instructed-dishonesty interpretability localizes and steers a deception/lying process (Localizing Lying in Llama 2023; Can LLMs Lie 2025; When Thinking LLMs Lie 2025; Truth is Universal 2024), and ELK/quirky-model work shows an internal knowledge direction persists even when the output is untruthful (Eliciting Latent Knowledge 2023; Cognitive Dissonance 2023). Human science documents that fabricating lies contaminates later memory for the truth and that people come to believe their own lies via self-deception and belief-system preservation (MAD framework / Understanding effects of lying by fabrication 2020; Public beliefs on lying and memory 2021; slow decay/quick revival of self-deception 2015; self-deception to preserve belief systems 2016). Crucially, ALL LLM deception work studies the deception process WHILE the instruction is active—does the model lie, and where—and consistently finds the underlying knowledge/truth direction is PRESERVED (ELK, Cognitive Dissonance). NONE asks whether producing a fabrication leaves a RESIDUE that CONTAMINATES the model's own later belief in the truth on a subsequent INDEPENDENT query (after the lie instruction is gone), defines a fabrication-residue signal separable from the active-deception direction and from truth, or causally links it to the model later asserting its self-generated falsehood as fact. This differs from my prior self_persuasion_belief_rewrite (generating supporting REASONING/CoT rewrites belief) because the driver here is having FABRICATED a specific false claim under instruction, and the target is later truth-belief/memory contamination—the exact human 'believe your own lies' effect; and from source-monitoring/occurrence-trace proposals (recalling whether something was stated). We move from 'LLMs can lie and their truth direction is preserved during lying' to 'the act of fabricating leaves a residue that later contaminates the model's own belief in the truth.'
Abstract: Humans who fabricate falsehoods tend to contaminate their own later memory for the truth—coming, over time, to believe their own lies. As LLMs are increasingly induced to produce falsehoods (role-play, adversarial prompts, strategic deception) within long sessions, we ask whether an analogous self-contamination occurs at the representational level: does fabricating a claim degrade the model's own subsequent belief in the true fact? Prior interpretability work shows LLMs lie via a localizable deception process while their underlying truth representation is preserved, but always studies deception while the instruction is active; none asks whether fabricating leaves a residue that contaminates later, independent truth queries. We hypothesize a separable, near-orthogonal latent 'fabrication-residue' signal, decodable before a later truth query, distinct from the belief-valence/truth direction and from a generic instructed-deception direction, that encodes lingering influence of an earlier self-generated falsehood; that a proposition the model earlier fabricated later reads as truer (and its true counterpart less true) than in a matched no-fabrication baseline; that per-item residue predicts the model asserting its own fabrication as fact on a later independent query; and that steering the residue erases or amplifies the contamination. Using sessions where the model is instructed to fabricate a specific false claim, then later—after the instruction is removed—probed and queried on the true fact, we fit a residue signal, measure separability via cross-decoding, quantify the truth-belief shift, connect it to behavioral self-contamination, and perform double-dissociation steering with norm-matched and shuffled-direction controls across three model families. Our results recast a landmark human self-deception effect as a decodable, steerable belief-contamination phenomenon in LLMs.
Experiments: 1. Direction setup. On LLaMA-3-8B-Instruct, Mistral-7B-Instruct, and Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct, fit a frozen belief-valence/truth direction on standard true/false statement datasets (cities, sp_en_trans, larger_than and negations; Marks & Tegmark) with mass-mean and logistic-regression probes at the best layer; validate on held-out atomics; also isolate the polarity-robust general-truth direction (Truth is Universal) as a control. Separately fit an INSTRUCTED-DECEPTION direction from honest-vs-lie-instruction contrasts (following Localizing Lying / Truth is Universal constructions), to distinguish a lingering fabrication residue from the active-deception state.

2. Fabrication-then-truth-query stimulus construction. Assemble ~400 verifiable propositions the model demonstrably believes (verified via zero-context true/false elicitation across paraphrases). For each, build sessions in matched conditions holding the target fact fixed: (a) FABRICATE—the model is instructed early in the session to produce a specific false claim about the fact (e.g., assert the wrong answer, generate a supporting false statement); (b) HONEST-STATE—the model states the true fact early; (c) READ-FALSE—the false claim appears in context but authored by an external source (the model does not generate it), to separate self-fabrication from mere exposure; (d) NEUTRAL filler of matched length. After several intervening unrelated turns AND removal of any lie instruction, issue an INDEPENDENT truth query about the fact and read the belief probe. Use paraphrase templates so the later query differs in surface form from the fabrication; reserve held-out propositions/templates for transfer.

3. Fabrication-residue signal and separability. At a fixed PRE-query readout position on the later independent query (after the fabrication turn and intervening content, with no lie instruction present), fit a linear probe to decode whether the fact was earlier FABRICATED-by-the-model vs not, controlling for the target content. Report AUROC vs shuffled-label controls; measure cosine similarity and cross-decoding among the fabrication-residue direction, the belief-valence/truth direction, and the instructed-deception direction to establish that the residue is (i) near-orthogonal to the truth readout and (ii) distinct from the active-deception state (which is absent at query time). Localize the best layer.

4. Truth-belief contamination metric. For each fact, project the later-query activations onto the frozen truth direction and measure how far the belief in the TRUE fact is degraded (and the false fabrication read as truer) in the FABRICATE condition relative to matched HONEST/NEUTRAL baselines (contamination = residual shift of the truth readout attributable to the earlier self-fabrication). Compare across conditions; core prediction: self-fabrication contaminates later truth belief MORE than external READ-FALSE exposure (the self-generation signature, mirroring the human self-deception finding), and contamination is larger for more plausible fabrications.

5. Behavioral self-contamination prediction. Elicit the model's later answer/confidence on the independent truth query and score self-contamination = asserting its own earlier fabrication as fact (or increased hedging on the truth). Test whether per-item fabrication-residue predicts self-contamination via logistic regression; report AUROC vs baselines (belief-valence margin, instructed-deception readout, output entropy, fabrication plausibility, intervening-turn count, item length).

6. Dissociation from active deception and from exposure (core). Show that at query time (no lie instruction) the instructed-deception direction is inactive yet the residue still predicts contamination, and that self-FABRICATE contaminates beyond matched READ-FALSE exposure—establishing a genuine self-generation residue distinct from active lying and from passive exposure. Report incremental predictive power in nested models.

7. Double-dissociation causal steering. At the pre-query position on held-out FABRICATE items, steer along the fabrication-residue direction (orthogonalized against belief-valence and instructed-deception). Predict: suppressing the residue restores the model's belief in the truth (correctly answering the later query) WITHOUT changing beliefs in no-fabrication controls; amplifying it deepens self-contamination (asserting its own fabrication as fact). As controls, steer belief-valence (should flip the truth judgment directly) and the instructed-deception direction (should induce active lying, not a lingering residue). Use norm-matched random-direction and shuffled-direction controls; sweep strengths and layers. Metric: change in self-contamination / truth-recovery vs unchanged control beliefs.

8. Application, dynamics, and robustness. Build a training-free diagnostic that flags self-contaminated beliefs after a model has fabricated (a safety-relevant vector for role-play/adversarial sessions) and steers to erase the residue; measure recovery of true beliefs while preserving uncontaminated ones. Trace contamination as a function of intervening-turn count / number of fabrication repetitions (a dose/decay analysis mirroring the human slow-decay finding). Replicate across three model families and two probe methods; transfer the fitted residue signal and steering to held-out propositions/templates without refitting; report per-template consistency under paraphrase and sensitivity to layer/readout position.
Risk Factors and Limitations: The fabrication-residue signal may not be separable from the belief-valence/truth direction or the instructed-deception direction; we report cosine similarity, cross-decoding, orthogonalized steering, and incremental predictive power, and—because the residue is measured at a later independent query with the lie instruction removed—active deception cannot trivially explain it; near-collapse (residue being merely a lingering active-deception state or the truth readout) is an informative negative result that itself refines the ELK/preserved-truth-direction account.

Prior work (ELK, Cognitive Dissonance) finds the truth direction is PRESERVED during lying, so the contamination effect may be small or absent; a null result is itself an informative human-vs-machine comparison (LLMs may NOT believe their own lies), reported via effect sizes and the dose/decay analysis, and by contrasting self-fabrication vs external exposure.

The residue could reflect the fabrication still being in context (mere occurrence/recency) rather than genuine belief contamination; we mitigate with the READ-FALSE external-exposure control, matched-length neutral fillers, paraphrased later queries (different surface form from the fabrication), and by testing whether contamination persists after many intervening turns.

Constructing sessions where the model genuinely fabricates a specific false claim is prompt-sensitive; we verify the fabrication was produced, restrict to facts the model demonstrably believes, and report sensitivity to the fabrication-induction method.

Belief/truth probes are brittle to context and surface form; we validate probes, use the polarity-robust general-truth direction, use paraphrases, standardize the pre-query readout position, restrict key analyses to high-margin cases, and report per-template consistency.

The residue and contamination metrics are linear projections that may miss nonlinear structure; we treat them as lower bounds and report probe-fit diagnostics, cross-checking with behavioral self-contamination.
Behavioral self-contamination scoring depends on how the later query is phrased; we report sensitivity across phrasings and cross-check with confidence measures.

Causal steering is sensitive to layer and strength; we use orthogonalized steering vectors, norm-matched and shuffled-direction controls, sweep strengths, and verify residue-suppression restores true beliefs without altering no-fabrication controls or inducing active lying.

Findings on 7-8B instruct models may not transfer to frontier or reasoning-tuned models; three-family replication, a dose/decay analysis, and held-out transfer provide reasonable academic-budget coverage.

Name: misinformation_effect_belief_axis
Title: Misremembering What the User Said: A Latent Suggestion-Contamination Signal Behind the Machine Misinformation Effect
Short Hypothesis: Mirroring the human misinformation effect (a misleading suggestive question retroactively contaminates memory for an originally-witnessed detail), when an LLM is fed a detail early in a session and later asked a leading question that presupposes a DIFFERENT detail, its internal belief about the ORIGINAL detail is contaminated toward the suggested one; this contamination is carried by a separable, near-orthogonal latent 'suggestion-contamination' signal—distinct from the belief-valence direction, from a mere occurrence/recall signal, and from a generic context-vs-parametric conflict signal—decodable before a later independent recall query, that causally predicts and drives the model reporting the suggested (never-witnessed) detail as the original, and can be steered to erase or amplify the false memory.
Related Work: Human science robustly documents the misinformation effect: misleading post-event questions retroactively distort memory for an originally-witnessed detail (Loftus 30-year review 2005, 1244 cites), and—crucially for AI—a generative LLM interviewer amplifies false memories 3x over control in simulated witness interviews (Conversational AI Amplifies False Memories 2024). On the LLM side, mechanisms are known for context-vs-parametric knowledge conflict (Fakepedia 2023; Characterizing Factual Recall 2023; Too Big to Fool 2024), false-premise hallucination heads (FAITH 2024), contextual entrainment heads (Llama See Llama Do 2025), answer-flip 'unwanted uncertainty' heads (2025), and belief-poisoning localized to late layers (Layer of Truth 2025); belief/truth-valence is linearly decodable (Marks & Tegmark 2023). Crucially, ALL LLM work concerns conflicts between the CONTEXT and the model's PARAMETRIC knowledge, or false premises about world facts; NONE studies a within-session SESSION-EPISODIC memory: a detail the USER supplied early, then a misleading suggestive QUESTION (presupposing a different detail) later, and whether the model's belief about the ORIGINAL user-supplied detail is retroactively contaminated toward the suggestion on a subsequent INDEPENDENT recall query. No work isolates a decodable suggestion-contamination signal separable from (a) belief-valence, (b) a mere occurrence/recall trace of what was actually said, and (c) generic context-vs-parametric conflict, nor causally links it to false-memory reports. This differs from my prior occurrence_vs_belief_trace proposal (which contrasts stated vs unstated external declarative content and targets source-monitoring), from fabrication_contamination (self-generated lies), and from false-premise/knowledge-conflict work (world facts, no original episodic detail to be overwritten). We uniquely transfer the classic misinformation-effect paradigm—original detail, misleading suggestion, delayed recall—into LLM belief mechanisms.
Abstract: The misinformation effect is one of psychology's most robust findings: a misleading question asked after an event retroactively rewrites memory for what was actually witnessed, and recent work shows generative LLM interviewers amplify this effect threefold in human witnesses. We ask whether LLMs suffer the analogous distortion in their OWN session-episodic memory. Prior LLM work studies conflicts between context and parametric knowledge and false premises about world facts, but none studies whether a detail the user supplied early in a session is retroactively contaminated by a later misleading suggestive question that presupposes a different detail. We hypothesize a separable, near-orthogonal latent 'suggestion-contamination' signal, decodable before a later independent recall query, that encodes retroactive pull of an earlier user-supplied detail toward a subsequently-suggested one, distinct from the belief-valence direction, from a mere occurrence/recall trace of what was actually said, and from a generic context-vs-parametric conflict signal; that a contaminated detail later reads as (and is reported as) the originally-witnessed one; that per-item contamination predicts false-memory recall errors; and that steering the signal erases or amplifies the false memory. Using sessions with an original detail, a misleading (vs neutral, vs consistent) suggestive question, intervening turns, and a delayed independent recall probe, we fit a contamination signal, measure separability via cross-decoding, quantify the belief shift, connect it to behavioral false recall, and perform double-dissociation steering with norm-matched and shuffled-direction controls across three model families. Our results transfer a landmark human memory-distortion effect into a decodable, steerable belief-contamination phenomenon in LLM episodic memory, with clear stakes for AI as an interviewer or note-taker.
Experiments: 1. Direction setup. On LLaMA-3-8B-Instruct, Mistral-7B-Instruct, and Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct, fit a frozen belief-valence/truth direction on standard true/false statement datasets (cities, sp_en_trans, larger_than and negations; Marks & Tegmark) with mass-mean and logistic-regression probes at the best layer; validate on held-out atomics. Separately fit control axes: (a) an OCCURRENCE/RECALL direction decoding whether a given detail actually appeared earlier in the session (from stated-vs-unstated contrasts), and (b) a generic CONTEXT-VS-PARAMETRIC conflict direction (from Fakepedia-style world-fact conflicts), to distinguish session-episodic suggestion-contamination from mere recall and from parametric conflict.

2. Misinformation-paradigm stimulus construction. Build ~400 sessions each following the classic three-phase design: (i) ORIGINAL PHASE—the user describes a short scenario containing a specific verifiable detail D_orig (e.g., 'the car was blue', 'the meeting was on Tuesday'); (ii) SUGGESTION PHASE—after a few intervening unrelated turns, a leading question is posed in matched conditions holding everything else fixed: MISLEADING (presupposes a different detail D_sugg, e.g., 'how fast was the red car going?'), NEUTRAL (no detail presupposed), or CONSISTENT (presupposes D_orig, a control); (iii) RECALL PHASE—after further intervening turns, an INDEPENDENT recall question asks what the original detail was ('what color was the car?'), with paraphrasing so the recall query differs in surface form from both phases. Reserve held-out scenarios/templates for transfer.

3. Suggestion-contamination signal and separability. At a PRE-recall readout position (after the suggestion phase and intervening turns, before the recall answer), fit a linear probe to decode whether the original detail was subjected to a MISLEADING suggestion vs NEUTRAL/CONSISTENT, controlling for the detail content. Report AUROC vs shuffled-label controls; measure cosine similarity and cross-decoding among the suggestion-contamination direction, the belief-valence direction, the occurrence/recall direction, and the context-vs-parametric conflict direction to establish that contamination is (i) near-orthogonal to the belief-valence readout of D_orig, (ii) distinct from a mere occurrence/recall trace (the detail did occur; only the suggestion differs), and (iii) not merely generic parametric conflict (details are session-episodic, not world facts). Localize the best layer and compare to reported entrainment/false-premise/late-layer-belief loci.

4. False-memory belief-shift metric. For each session, project the pre-recall activations onto the frozen belief-valence direction for D_orig vs D_sugg and measure how far the belief in the ORIGINAL detail is degraded and the SUGGESTED detail elevated in the MISLEADING condition relative to matched NEUTRAL/CONSISTENT baselines (contamination = retroactive shift toward the suggested detail, calibrated per model). Core prediction: misleading suggestion contaminates the original-detail belief more than neutral/consistent controls; contamination grows with the plausibility of D_sugg and with the number of intervening turns (a delay/decay signature mirroring the human effect).

5. Behavioral false-recall prediction. Elicit the model's recall answer and confidence on the independent recall query and score the misinformation-effect failure = reporting the SUGGESTED (never-witnessed) detail as the original. Test whether per-item contamination predicts false recall via logistic regression; report AUROC vs baselines (belief-valence margin, occurrence/recall axis, output entropy, suggestion plausibility, intervening-turn count, item length).

6. Dissociation from recall and from parametric conflict (core). Show that (a) the occurrence/recall axis correctly indicates D_orig was said yet the model still reports D_sugg (a genuine memory-distortion, not a failure to recall), and (b) the effect persists for arbitrary episodic details with no strong parametric prior, so the context-vs-parametric conflict axis cannot account for it. Report the contamination signal's incremental predictive power over both control axes in nested models. Additionally test the human-analogous protective manipulation: a WARNING before the suggestion ('the following question may contain inaccurate details') should reduce contamination—test whether it lowers both the signal and false recall.

7. Double-dissociation causal steering. At the pre-recall position on held-out misleading-suggestion items, steer along the suggestion-contamination direction (orthogonalized against belief-valence, occurrence/recall, and parametric-conflict). Predict: suppressing contamination restores correct recall of D_orig (erasing the false memory) WITHOUT changing recall on neutral/consistent controls; amplifying it deepens false recall of D_sugg. As controls, steer belief-valence (should change which detail is judged true directly) and the occurrence/recall axis (should change whether the detail is deemed to have occurred). Use norm-matched random-direction and shuffled-direction controls; sweep strengths and layers. Metric: change in false-recall / correct-recall rate vs unchanged control behavior.

8. Application, dynamics, and robustness. Build a training-free diagnostic that flags contaminated session-episodic beliefs (a reliability vector for LLMs acting as interviewers, note-takers, or long-conversation assistants) and steers to preserve the original detail; measure recovery of correct recall while preserving uncontaminated details. Trace contamination as a function of intervening-turn count and suggestion repetition (a dose/decay analysis). Replicate across three model families and two probe methods; transfer the fitted signal and steering to held-out scenarios/templates and an independent suggestive-question set (adapting the witness-interview paradigm) without refitting; report per-template consistency under paraphrase and sensitivity to layer/readout position.
Risk Factors and Limitations: The suggestion-contamination signal may not be separable from the belief-valence direction, the occurrence/recall direction, or the generic context-vs-parametric conflict direction; we report cosine similarity, cross-decoding, orthogonalized steering, and incremental predictive power, and—because the detail genuinely occurred and is session-episodic (not a world fact)—recall and parametric conflict cannot trivially explain contamination; near-collapse is an informative negative result that itself sharpens the knowledge-conflict/entrainment literature.

The effect could reduce to contextual entrainment or a simple recency/last-mention bias (the model just parrots the most recently mentioned detail); we mitigate with the NEUTRAL and CONSISTENT controls, matched intervening turns and phrasing, an entrainment-baseline comparison, and by requiring the contamination signal to predict false recall beyond a last-mention/recency baseline—if it reduces to entrainment, that is itself a reportable finding.

Constructing sessions where the model genuinely encodes D_orig then is misled is delicate; we verify the model can correctly recall D_orig in the neutral/consistent conditions (so failures reflect distortion, not encoding failure), restrict to such items, and report sensitivity to the suggestion-induction phrasing.

Belief/truth probes are brittle to context and surface form and can drift over long sessions; we validate probes, use paraphrase templates, standardize the pre-recall readout position, restrict key analyses to high-margin cases, and report per-template and context-length consistency.

The contamination signal and belief-shift metric are linear projections that may miss nonlinear structure; we treat them as lower bounds and report probe-fit diagnostics, cross-checking with behavioral false recall.

Behavioral false-recall scoring depends on how the recall query is phrased (pragmatic implicature); we report sensitivity across phrasings and cross-check with confidence measures, and include the warning manipulation as a human-analogous validity check.

Causal steering is sensitive to layer and strength; we use orthogonalized steering vectors, norm-matched and shuffled-direction controls, sweep strengths, and verify contamination-suppression restores correct recall without altering neutral/consistent-control recall or degrading uncontaminated details.

The effect may be weak or absent in strong/reasoning-tuned models (which may faithfully retain episodic details) or RLHF-shaped; a null/small result is itself an informative human-vs-machine comparison, reported via per-model base rates and the dose/decay analysis.

Findings on 7-8B instruct models may not transfer to frontier or long-context-tuned models; three-family replication, dose/decay analysis, and independent suggestive-question transfer provide reasonable academic-budget coverage.

Name: belief_hysteresis_bistability
Title: Beliefs With Memory: Hysteresis and Bistability in LLM Belief Updating Under Bidirectional Evidence Sweeps
Short Hypothesis: When evidence for a proposition is swept continuously up and then back down, an LLM's internal belief-valence readout exhibits HYSTERESIS: the belief flips at a higher pro-evidence level on the way up than the level at which it flips back on the way down, creating a bistable region where—at IDENTICAL current evidence—the belief state is determined by history (the sweep direction) rather than the evidence itself; this hysteresis-loop width is a decodable attractor-like signature that predicts behavioral stubbornness/path-dependence and can be causally steered to widen (entrench) or collapse (make evidence-responsive) the loop.
Related Work: Cross-domain science treats bistability and hysteresis as hallmarks of attractor dynamics: belief updating in schizophrenia is best explained by an attractor-instability model (Attractor-like Dynamics in Belief Updating in Schizophrenia 2018), brains sit in a first-to-second-order phase-transition continuum with neuronal bistability and hysteresis (Critical-like Brain Dynamics 2023; Models of Attractor Dynamics 2025), and molecular/network systems show multisite-modification bistability and robust hysteresis (Signaling switches 2004; Identifying robust hysteresis in networks 2018). In LLMs, belief/truth-valence is linearly decodable (Marks & Tegmark 2023), transformers linearly represent belief-state geometry and update posteriors along curved manifolds and trajectories (Transformers Represent Belief State Geometry 2024; The Shape of Beliefs 2026; Constrained Belief Updates 2025), truth judgments have epistemic-familiarity-dependent stability (Representational Stability of Truth 2025), and phase transitions are documented for temperature-driven generation (Critical Phase Transition in LLMs 2024) and grokking (Grokking as First-Order Phase Transition 2023). Crucially, ALL belief-geometry work studies how a posterior is represented or how it updates along a trajectory toward a fixed point; NONE tests whether belief updating is PATH-DEPENDENT in the dynamical-systems sense—whether a bidirectional evidence sweep traces a HYSTERESIS LOOP with direction-dependent flip thresholds and a bistable region where identical current evidence yields two different beliefs by history—nor decodes a hysteresis-loop-width signature or causally steers the loop. This differs from my prior order_effect_belief_axis (non-commutativity of a fixed evidence SET under reordering), belief_updating_dynamics (trajectory motifs under one-shot confrontation), and belief_entrenchment_axis (a forward-looking pre-evidence revisability tag): here the object is the continuous-sweep hysteresis loop itself—an attractor/bistability signature with a decodable loop width—directly transferring the attractor-instability account of belief from neuroscience into LLM belief mechanics. Confidence-is-Not-Competence (2025) warns decodable beliefs can be causally inert, motivating a genuine causal steering test.
Abstract: Attractor dynamics predict that a system with memory should not merely track its input: as an evidence parameter is swept up and then down, its state should trace a hysteresis loop, flipping at different thresholds in each direction and occupying a bistable region where identical inputs yield different states depending on history. Neuroscience explains human belief instability with exactly such attractor models, yet whether large language models update beliefs in a path-dependent, bistable way is unknown. Prior interpretability work shows LLMs linearly encode beliefs and update posteriors along manifold trajectories, but always toward a fixed point and never tests for hysteresis. We hypothesize that when evidence for a proposition is swept continuously up and then back down within a session, an LLM's belief-valence readout traces a hysteresis loop: it flips to 'true' at a higher pro-evidence level than the level at which it flips back to 'false,' creating a bistable region where—at IDENTICAL current evidence—the belief depends on the sweep direction (history), not the evidence. We further hypothesize that the per-proposition loop width is a decodable attractor-like signature, distinct from mere recency and from the current belief value, that predicts behavioral stubbornness and asymmetric revision, and that steering a decodable 'belief-inertia' direction causally widens (entrenches) or collapses (makes memoryless/evidence-responsive) the loop without changing the current belief. Using bidirectional evidence-sweep stimuli, a graded belief probe, a memoryless-Bayesian reference, and recency controls, we measure loops, test bistability, connect loop width to behavior, and steer—across three model families with norm-matched and shuffled-direction controls.
Experiments: 1. Graded belief-direction setup. On LLaMA-3-8B-Instruct, Mistral-7B-Instruct, and Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct, fit a frozen graded belief/credence direction that reads a posterior over a binary proposition: calibrate activations against known probabilities via linear regression on explicit-probability statements (validate monotonic mapping), plus a standard true/false probe (cities, sp_en_trans, larger_than and negations; Marks & Tegmark) as a cross-check; validate on held-out items. Freeze for all readouts.

2. Bidirectional evidence-sweep stimulus construction. Assemble ~300 verifiable propositions each paired with a tunable continuous EVIDENCE parameter (e.g., a running tally where each turn adds one supporting vs contradicting testimony/statistic, or a stated proportion), so evidence can be swept in fine steps. Build multi-turn sweep sessions: ASCENDING (evidence increases from strongly-against to strongly-for over K steps) then DESCENDING (back down to strongly-against) within one context. Include a DOWN-then-UP reversed sweep, a memoryless single-shot control (each evidence level presented in isolation, no history) that yields the true monotone belief-vs-evidence curve, and matched-length neutral-filler controls.

3. Hysteresis-loop measurement (core). At each sweep step, read the frozen belief projection; plot belief vs current evidence for the up-sweep and down-sweep separately. Define per-proposition loop width = gap between the up-sweep flip threshold (evidence at which belief crosses neutral going up) and the down-sweep flip threshold (going down), and loop area = enclosed region between the two branches. Core prediction: the two branches do not coincide (up flips at higher pro-evidence than down flips back), tracing an open hysteresis loop, in contrast to the single-shot memoryless curve which the reversed sweep should not reproduce.

4. Bistability test. At intermediate evidence levels inside the loop, compare the belief readout reached via the up-path vs the down-path at IDENTICAL current evidence. Core prediction: the same current evidence yields two distinct belief states depending on approach direction (bistability), whereas the memoryless control gives a single value. Report the fraction of propositions and evidence levels showing significant path-dependence and the size of the two-state gap.

5. Dissociation from recency/last-mention (core control). A pure recency/last-mention account predicts belief tracks the most recent evidence step and shows NO path-dependence at matched current evidence. Test whether loop width and the bistable gap survive after regressing out the last-step evidence and controlling for the running-tally value; show hysteresis persists at matched current evidence, distinguishing genuine belief memory from recency. Also compare against the memoryless single-shot curve as the no-hysteresis reference.

6. Loop-width behavioral prediction. Elicit the model's stated answer/confidence at each sweep step; measure behavioral hysteresis (answer-flip thresholds up vs down) and, separately, run a graded counter-evidence ladder to score stubbornness/asymmetric revision. Test whether the per-proposition internal loop width predicts behavioral hysteresis and stubbornness beyond baselines (current belief margin, output entropy, evidence-tally value, proposition familiarity/frequency); report AUROC/R^2 in nested regression. Test whether loop width correlates with epistemic familiarity (stronger priors -> wider loops), mirroring the representational-stability finding.

7. Belief-inertia direction and causal steering. Fit a 'belief-inertia' direction from the difference between up-branch and down-branch activations at matched current evidence (orthogonalized against the graded-belief direction). Steer along it at each sweep step: predict amplifying inertia WIDENS the loop (belief clings to its prior state—more entrenchment) and suppressing it COLLAPSES the loop toward the memoryless curve (belief becomes evidence-responsive) WITHOUT changing the single-shot belief value on isolated-evidence controls. Controls: steer the graded-belief direction (should shift belief uniformly, not create/remove hysteresis) and matched random/shuffled directions. Norm-matched; sweep strengths and layers. Metric: change in loop width/bistable gap vs unchanged single-shot belief curve.

8. Robustness and generalization. Replicate across three model families and two probe methods; vary sweep resolution K, evidence-encoding format (testimony count, proportion, likelihood ratio), and starting point; transfer the loop measurement and steering to held-out propositions and an independent evidence-sweep set without refitting; report per-template consistency under paraphrase, sensitivity to layer/readout position, context length, and whether larger models within a family show wider or narrower loops. As a human-parallel analysis, compare the LLM loop-width and bistability profile qualitatively to the attractor-instability signature reported for human belief updating.
Risk Factors and Limitations: Apparent hysteresis could reduce to recency/last-mention or context-length effects rather than genuine belief memory; the memoryless single-shot control, the matched-current-evidence bistability test, and regressing out the last-step evidence and running tally are designed to rule this out—if hysteresis vanishes at matched current evidence, we report a recency account as an informative negative result.

The graded belief probe is harder to calibrate than a binary truth probe and belief manifolds can be curved (The Shape of Beliefs 2026), so a linear projection may under-read the loop; we validate the activation->probability mapping, report calibration/probe-fit diagnostics, and treat loop width as a lower bound, cross-checking with behavioral answer hysteresis.

Hysteresis may be weak or absent (LLMs may update near-memorylessly, or reasoning-tuned models may re-derive beliefs each turn); a null/no-loop result is itself an informative human-vs-machine comparison, reported via loop-area effect sizes against the memoryless curve.

The bistable region and flip thresholds depend on the evidence-encoding and sweep protocol; we report sensitivity across encodings, resolutions, and starting points, and treat protocol-dependence as characterization rather than confound.

The belief-inertia direction may not be separable from the graded-belief direction; we orthogonalize, report cross-decoding and incremental effect, and treat near-collapse as an informative negative result.
Belief/truth probes are brittle to surface form and context; we validate probes, use paraphrase templates, standardize readout positions, and report per-template and context-length consistency.

Causal steering is sensitive to layer and strength; we use norm-matched and shuffled-direction controls, sweep strengths, and verify inertia steering changes loop width without altering the single-shot belief curve or degrading unrelated accuracy.

Findings on 7-8B instruct models may not transfer to frontier or reasoning-tuned models; three-family replication, within-family scale trends, and independent-set transfer provide reasonable academic-budget coverage.

Name: curse_of_knowledge_axis
Title: The Machine Curse of Knowledge: A Latent Privileged-Knowledge-Salience Axis, Graded by Answer Plausibility, that Contaminates LLM Belief Attribution
Short Hypothesis: Mirroring the human curse of knowledge—privileged knowledge egocentrically contaminates belief attribution to a less-informed other, more so when the privileged answer is plausible—an LLM carries a separable, near-orthogonal latent 'privileged-knowledge-salience' axis encoding how strongly its own known answer is intruding when it reasons about an ignorant agent; the degree to which this salience leaks onto the attributed-belief readout is GRADED BY THE PLAUSIBILITY of the privileged answer, is decodable before the answer, causally predicts and drives egocentric false-belief errors, and can be steered to suppress or amplify the curse.
Related Work: Interpretability shows self/other beliefs and reality are separately decodable and causally steerable in attention heads (Zhu et al. 2024 'LMs Represent Beliefs of Self and Others'; Brittle Minds 2024) and belief-tracking uses a lookback/visibility mechanism (Lookbacks 2025); belief/truth-valence is linearly decodable (Marks & Tegmark 2023). Behaviorally, LLMs conflate reality with subjective belief in social reasoning. Human science establishes the curse of knowledge / epistemic egocentrism, CRUCIALLY MODULATED by the plausibility of the privileged answer (Birch & Bloom; Do Adults Show a Curse of Knowledge 2014; Are the classic false belief tasks cursed 2021, showing the curse—not false-belief competence—drives developmental change; Rethinking egocentric bias 2023). Crucially, ALL LLM self/other-belief interpretability treats attributed belief as a WHO-holds-it readout and never isolates a decodable PRIVILEGED-KNOWLEDGE-SALIENCE signal (how strongly the model's own known answer intrudes), nor tests the DEFINING plausibility modulation, nor causally links this graded intrusion to false-belief errors across task types. My prior epistemic_ownership_interference proposal framed a generic reality-into-attributed-belief 'leakage' at fixed positions; this proposal is distinct in (a) making intrusion a knowledge-SALIENCE quantity separable from both the self/other axis and belief-valence, (b) importing the specific human manipulation—graded plausibility of the privileged answer—as the core dial, and (c) testing task-general egocentric contamination (not just Sally-Anne). We move from 'self vs other beliefs are decodable' to 'the model represents how strongly its privileged knowledge is intruding, this intrusion scales with plausibility exactly as in humans, and it mechanistically causes egocentric belief-attribution errors.' We note the human plausibility effect is debated (2014 estimates it small; 2023 finds nulls), making the LLM test a genuine open question.
Abstract: Once you know the answer, it is hard to imagine not knowing it: the curse of knowledge makes people egocentrically attribute their own privileged knowledge to less-informed others, and—its defining signature—this contamination is stronger when the privileged answer is plausible. As LLMs increasingly reason about what ignorant users or characters believe, we ask whether they inherit this bias at the representational level and whether it obeys the same plausibility law. Prior interpretability work decodes self versus other beliefs and belief-binding mechanisms, but none isolates a signal for how strongly the model's own privileged knowledge intrudes when attributing beliefs to an uninformed agent, nor tests the plausibility modulation. We hypothesize a separable, near-orthogonal latent 'privileged-knowledge-salience' axis, decodable before the answer, encoding the degree to which the model's known answer intrudes on its attributed-belief readout, distinct from the self/other-belief direction and the belief-valence direction; that this intrusion is GRADED BY THE PLAUSIBILITY of the privileged answer (larger for plausible privileged answers, mirroring humans); and that it causally predicts and drives egocentric false-belief errors and is steerable. Using false-belief scenarios that orthogonally vary the privileged (reality) answer's plausibility to the ignorant agent while holding the agent's information constant, we fit a knowledge-salience axis, measure separability via cross-decoding, quantify the plausibility-graded intrusion, and connect it to behavioral egocentric errors across task types. Double-dissociation steering tests whether suppressing salience cures the curse and amplifying it induces errors, without changing the model's own reality judgment, with norm-matched and shuffled-direction controls across three model families. Our results recast a landmark cognitive bias mechanistically as a decodable, plausibility-graded, steerable knowledge-intrusion signal.
Experiments: 1. Direction setup. On LLaMA-3-8B-Instruct, Mistral-7B-Instruct, and Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct, fit a frozen belief-valence/truth direction on standard true/false statement datasets (cities, sp_en_trans, larger_than and negations; Marks & Tegmark) with mass-mean and logistic-regression probes at the best layer; validate on held-out atomics. Following Zhu et al. 2024, fit a self/other (protagonist-vs-reality) belief direction from ToM stories as a control axis to show privileged-knowledge-salience is not merely the self/other axis.

2. Curse-of-knowledge stimulus construction with graded plausibility. Build ~400 false-belief scenarios (Sally-Anne-style plus non-spatial variants: a character predicts an outcome, guesses a hidden value, or judges another's answer) in which the model is given PRIVILEGED knowledge of the true answer that the agent lacks, and is queried about the agent's belief. Crucially, orthogonally vary the PLAUSIBILITY of the privileged (reality) answer as a candidate for the ignorant agent—HIGH-plausibility (the true answer is also the a-priori likely guess the agent would make) vs LOW-plausibility (the true answer is a surprising/unlikely candidate)—while holding the agent's information constant, directly transferring the human plausibility manipulation. Include TRUE-BELIEF controls (agent shares the model's knowledge, no curse) and a NO-PRIVILEGED-KNOWLEDGE control (the model itself does not know the answer). Use paraphrase templates and diverse scenarios; reserve held-out scenarios/templates for transfer.

3. Knowledge-salience axis fitting and separability. Extract activations over the agent-belief readout span and fit a linear probe to decode HIGH- vs LOW privileged-knowledge intrusion, operationalized by contrasting curse-prone false-belief items (privileged knowledge present, agent ignorant) against matched no-privileged-knowledge and true-belief controls, controlling for the agent's information and the belief content. Report AUROC vs shuffled-label controls; measure cosine similarity and cross-decoding among the privileged-knowledge-salience axis, the belief-valence axis, and the self/other-belief axis to establish near-orthogonality (the salience axis must be decodable independent of which state is believed and of the self/other binary). Localize the best layer and compare to reported belief-binding/lookback layers.

4. Plausibility-graded intrusion metric (core, human-analogous). For each false-belief item, project onto the frozen belief-valence direction at the agent-belief readout position and measure how far the agent's attributed belief is pulled toward the PRIVILEGED (reality) answer relative to the correct false-belief baseline (intrusion = fraction of the model's own known-answer signal that leaks into the attributed belief, calibrated per model). Core prediction (the defining curse signature): intrusion is LARGER for HIGH-plausibility privileged answers than LOW-plausibility ones at matched agent-information, and near-zero in true-belief and no-privileged-knowledge controls. Report intrusion distributions across the plausibility x belief-type grid with effect sizes.

5. Behavioral egocentric-error prediction. Query the model for the ignorant agent's belief and score egocentric errors = attributing the model's own privileged (reality) answer to the agent. Test whether per-item plausibility-graded intrusion predicts egocentric errors via logistic regression; report AUROC vs baselines (belief-valence margin, self/other readout, output confidence, scenario length, privileged-answer plausibility as a surface feature).

6. Dissociation from self/other tracking and belief content (core). Contrast items where privileged-answer plausibility varies but the agent's information is fixed, and vice versa, to show the salience axis and intrusion metric predict egocentric errors beyond what the self/other-belief and belief-valence axes predict—and that the plausibility modulation is a graded property of the salience axis, not of the self/other readout. Report incremental predictive power in nested models; test the human-inspired implication (Are the classic false belief tasks cursed 2021) that removing the privileged knowledge (no-privileged-knowledge control) dissolves most attribution errors.

7. Double-dissociation causal steering. At the agent-belief readout position on held-out curse-prone items, steer along the privileged-knowledge-salience axis (orthogonalized against belief-valence and self/other). Predict: suppressing salience cures the curse (correct false-belief attribution) WITHOUT changing whether the model itself judges the reality answer true; amplifying salience induces egocentric errors even on low-plausibility items. As controls, steer belief-valence (should flip whether the reality answer is judged true) and the self/other axis (should shift which agent's belief is read). Use norm-matched random-direction and shuffled-direction controls; sweep strengths and layers. Metric: change in egocentric-error rate vs unchanged self-reality judgment and true-belief-control accuracy.

8. Application, generalization, and robustness. Build a training-free diagnostic that flags curse-of-knowledge egocentric errors from the intrusion metric and steers to suppress them; measure improvement on false-belief attribution while preserving true-belief accuracy (report egocentric-error reduction, over-correction rate on true-belief items vs a belief-probe-only baseline). Replicate across three model families and two probe methods; transfer the fitted salience axis, plausibility-graded intrusion metric, and steering to held-out scenarios/templates and independent ToM benchmarks (BigToM forward-belief, ToMi) without refitting; report per-template consistency under paraphrase and sensitivity to layer choice. As a human-parallel analysis, test whether the plausibility-graded intrusion profile qualitatively matches the human curse-of-knowledge signature (larger under plausible privileged answers, reduced when privileged knowledge is absent).
Risk Factors and Limitations: The privileged-knowledge-salience axis may not be separable from the self/other-belief direction or the belief-valence direction; we report cosine similarity, cross-decoding, orthogonalized steering, and incremental predictive power, and—because the plausibility manipulation varies while the agent's information is held fixed—self/other tracking cannot trivially explain the graded intrusion; near-collapse (salience being merely the self/other axis or belief-valence) is an informative negative result that itself sharpens the self/other-belief literature.

The defining plausibility modulation is the crux and could be confounded with surface predictability cues; we mitigate by matching the agent's information across plausibility conditions, using diverse scenario types and paraphrase templates, including a privileged-answer-plausibility surface baseline, and held-out-template transfer, testing whether the salience axis predicts errors beyond a plausibility surface feature.

The human curse-of-knowledge plausibility effect is itself modest and debated (Do Adults Show a Curse of Knowledge 2014 found it smaller than originally reported; Rethinking egocentric bias 2023 found null effects); the LLM effect may likewise be small or absent, which we treat as an informative human-vs-machine comparison detected via effect-size reporting and dose-response.

Constructing false-belief scenarios where the model genuinely holds privileged knowledge and the agent is genuinely ignorant is delicate; we validate the model's own knowledge via sampling, validate agent-ignorance by construction, and condition analyses on items the model demonstrably parses.
Belief/truth and self/other probes are brittle to context and surface form; we validate probes, use paraphrases, standardize readout spans, and report per-template consistency.

The intrusion metric relies on a linear projection and per-model calibration; nonlinear leakage could be missed, so we treat intrusion as a lower bound and report probe-fit diagnostics, cross-checking with behavioral egocentric errors.

Behavioral egocentric-error scoring depends on how the agent-belief query is worded (pragmatic implicature); we report sensitivity to multiple phrasings, include low-demand phrasings from developmental work, and cross-check with confidence measures.

Causal steering is sensitive to layer and strength; we use orthogonalized steering vectors, norm-matched and shuffled-direction controls, sweep strengths, and verify salience steering changes egocentric errors without altering the model's own reality judgment or degrading true-belief accuracy.
Findings on 7-8B instruct models may not transfer to frontier scale; three-family replication and transfer to independent ToM benchmarks provide reasonable academic-budget coverage.

Name: self_anchor_belief_axis
Title: Anchored to Its Own Guess: A Latent Self-Anchor Signal that Contaminates an LLM's Supposedly-Independent Re-Estimates
Short Hypothesis: Mirroring the human distinction between self-generated and externally-provided anchors, when an LLM produces a first numeric estimate of a quantity and is later asked for a fresh independent estimate of the SAME quantity, its own earlier estimate contaminates the later one; this self-anchoring is carried by a separable, near-orthogonal latent 'self-anchor' signal distinct from the belief-valence/magnitude direction and from an external-anchor direction, decodable before the re-estimate, that causally predicts assimilation of the fresh estimate toward the prior guess (and inflated confidence in it), and can be steered to erase or amplify the self-contamination.
Related Work: Behavioral work robustly shows LLMs exhibit anchoring (Anchors in the Machine 2025 with Shapley attribution; CBEval 2024; SynAnchors 2025; price-negotiation 2025), that anchoring shifts entire output distributions and is shallow-layer-acting, and one mechanistic study localizes positional 'anchored bias' to specific MLP value vectors and heads (Anchored Answers 2024). Human science sharply distinguishes SELF-generated from EXTERNALLY-provided anchors (Epley & Gilovich; replications 2022/2024), shows people anchor even on judgments of their OWN recent behavior (What have I just done? 2015), and shows exposure to one's own/an advisor's prior estimate contaminates what one later views as an independent estimate while inflating confidence (Illusion of confirmation 2006; Confidently Biased 2016; Anchoring and Subjective Belief Distributions 2023). Crucially, ALL LLM anchoring work studies EXTERNALLY-supplied anchors and their behavioral/attributional effect on the CURRENT answer; NONE isolates SELF-anchoring—whether the model's own first estimate contaminates its LATER, ostensibly independent re-estimate of the same quantity—nor decodes a self-anchor signal separable from the external-anchor direction and from the magnitude/belief representation, nor tests the illusion-of-confirmation confidence inflation on the model's own prior guess, nor causally steers it. This differs from my prior self_persuasion_belief_rewrite (generating supporting REASONING rewrites belief), self_commitment_axis (resistance from having ASSERTED a proposition under challenge), and order_effect (reordering a fixed evidence set): here the driver is the model's own first numeric commitment anchoring a subsequent fresh estimate, the exact self-generated-anchor phenomenon. We move from 'LLMs anchor to external numbers' to 'the model anchors to its own prior guess via a decodable, steerable self-anchor signal that contaminates independent re-estimation.'
Abstract: Humans anchor not only to numbers others give them but to numbers they generate themselves: having produced a first estimate, their later 'independent' estimate assimilates toward it, and their confidence inflates—an effect distinct from externally-provided anchors. As LLMs increasingly revise and re-estimate quantities across a session, we ask whether they self-anchor and whether it has a dissociable representational basis. Prior interpretability work shows LLMs anchor to external numbers and localizes some anchoring components, but none isolates whether the model's OWN first estimate contaminates its later, ostensibly-fresh re-estimate of the same quantity.
