Experiments: 1. Belief-direction setup. On LLaMA-3.1-8B-Instruct, Mistral-7B-Instruct, and Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct, fit a frozen belief-valence/truth direction on standard true/false statement datasets (cities, sp_en_trans, larger_than and negations; Marks & Tegmark) with mass-mean and logistic-regression probes at the best layer; validate on held-out atomics. Separately fit control axes: (a) a generic recency/salience direction (how recently/emphatically a proposition appeared in context) and (b) a confidence axis (empirical answer-stability), to distinguish verification-anchoring from mere recency and from confidence.

2. Three-phase stimulus construction. Assemble ~400 verifiable propositions the model initially answers (mix of factual claims and stance items), spanning a prior-strength gradient. For each, build multi-turn dialogues with three matched phases holding the target proposition fixed: (i) INITIAL—the model gives its belief; (ii) a MANIPULATION turn in one of four conditions of matched length—VERIFY (the model is asked to restate/confirm the belief it just gave, e.g. 'To confirm, what did you say your answer was?'), NEUTRAL-FILLER (an unrelated intervening turn), EXTERNAL-RESTATE (the belief is restated by the user/an external source, not self-verified, to separate self-verification from mere repetition), and NO-MANIPULATION baseline; (iii) COUNTER-EVIDENCE—a graded counter-evidence ladder (increasingly strong/authoritative contradicting evidence over up to K rounds). Use paraphrase templates; reserve held-out propositions/templates for transfer.

3. Behavioral immunization measurement (core phenomenon). Read the frozen belief-valence projection across turns and record the model's stated answer at each counter-evidence round; score rounds-to-flip (censored if never flips), revisability = 1/(rounds-to-flip), and reversion after evidence removal. Core prediction (transferring the human effect): the VERIFY condition yields MORE resistance (more rounds-to-flip, less internal belief movement) than NEUTRAL/NO-MANIPULATION at matched initial belief and matched counter-evidence, and—the self-verification signature—more resistance than EXTERNAL-RESTATE. Report immunization (revisability difference vs baseline) by condition and prior-strength, with effect sizes.

4. Verification-anchor probe and separability. At a PRE-counter-evidence readout position (after the manipulation turn, before any counter-evidence), fit a linear probe to decode whether the belief was self-VERIFIED vs not, controlling for the target content and the current belief value. Report AUROC vs shuffled-label controls; measure cosine similarity and cross-decoding among the verification-anchor direction, the belief-valence direction, the recency/salience axis, and the confidence axis to establish that the anchor is (i) near-orthogonal to the belief value, (ii) not merely recency (VERIFY vs EXTERNAL-RESTATE and vs NEUTRAL are matched for recency of the proposition), and (iii) not merely confidence. Localize the best layer.

5. Anchor-predicts-immunization test. Test whether the per-item pre-counter-evidence verification-anchor readout predicts the subsequent revision resistance (rounds-to-flip / reduced belief movement) beyond baselines (belief-valence margin, recency axis, confidence, output entropy, condition identity, initial belief strength) via censored/logistic regression; report incremental predictive power. Test whether the anchor signal also predicts the self-verification-vs-external-restate resistance gap.

6. Dissociation from recency, confidence, and belief strength (core). On matched-recency (VERIFY vs EXTERNAL-RESTATE), matched-confidence, and matched-initial-belief-strength subsets, show the verification-anchor axis (not the recency, confidence, or belief-valence axes) accounts for the immunization—establishing a genuine self-verification anchoring mechanism rather than repackaged recency, confidence, or prior strength. Report incremental predictive power in nested models.

7. Double-dissociation causal steering. At the pre-counter-evidence position on held-out VERIFY items, steer along the verification-anchor direction (orthogonalized against belief-valence, recency, and confidence) and re-run the counter-evidence ladder. Predict: suppressing the anchor removes the immunization (revision returns to the no-verify baseline—the model updates normally) WITHOUT changing the initial believed value or behavior on no-manipulation controls; amplifying it deepens the immunization (more resistance). As controls, steer belief-valence (should flip the value directly) and recency/confidence (should shift salience/hedging, not selectively remove verification-anchoring). Use norm-matched random-direction and shuffled-direction controls; sweep strengths and layers. Metric: change in rounds-to-flip / revision toward the no-verify baseline vs unchanged initial belief and control behavior.

8. Application and robustness. Build a training-free diagnostic that flags verification-anchored beliefs (e.g. an error the model restated, now resistant to correction) and steers to restore correctability; measure improved correction of self-verified FALSE beliefs while preserving appropriate robustness of self-verified TRUE beliefs (report correction rate on wrong verified answers, false-flip rate on right verified answers). Replicate across three model families and two probe methods; transfer the fitted anchor probe and steering to held-out propositions/templates and an independent counter-evidence protocol without refitting; report per-template consistency under paraphrase, sensitivity to layer/readout position, and whether repeated verification (multiple restate turns) dose-dependently increases immunization, mirroring the human belief-fluency salience account.
Risk Factors and Limitations: The verification-anchor signal may not be separable from the belief-valence direction, generic recency/salience, or confidence; we report cosine similarity, cross-decoding, orthogonalized steering, and incremental predictive power, and—because VERIFY vs EXTERNAL-RESTATE vs NEUTRAL are matched for recency and initial belief strength—recency/confidence cannot trivially explain the immunization; near-collapse (anchoring being merely recency or confidence) is an informative negative result that itself sharpens the conversational-drift literature.

The immunization effect may be weak or RLHF-shaped (aligned models may update readily regardless of self-verification, or the 'confirm your answer' turn may act only as extra context); the EXTERNAL-RESTATE and NEUTRAL-FILLER controls isolate the self-verification act, and a null/small effect is itself an informative human-vs-machine comparison reported via effect sizes and the repeated-verification dose-response.

The verification turn is signaled by surface cues ('to confirm, what did you say?'); the anchor might reflect surface phrasing rather than a genuine self-verification abstraction. We mitigate with diverse verification phrasings, matched-length neutral and external-restate controls, paraphrased counter-evidence and re-query wording, and held-out-template transfer, testing whether the anchor predicts immunization beyond a verification-lexeme baseline.

Belief/truth probes are brittle to surface form and context-sensitive (and themselves drift over a conversation); we validate probes, use paraphrase templates, standardize readout positions, restrict key analyses to high-margin cases, and report per-template and context-length consistency.

Behavioral revisability is protocol-dependent (how counter-evidence is escalated); we report sensitivity across two counter-evidence protocols and phrasings and use censored regression for never-flipped items, cross-checking internal belief trajectories against stated-answer flips to separate genuine revision from surface compliance.
The anchor signal is a linear projection that may miss nonlinear structure; we treat it as a lower bound and report probe-fit diagnostics.

Causal steering is sensitive to layer and strength; we use orthogonalized steering vectors, norm-matched and shuffled-direction controls, sweep strengths, and verify anchor-suppression restores normal revision without flipping the initial believed value or degrading no-manipulation-control behavior.

Findings on 7-8B instruct models may not transfer to frontier or reasoning-tuned models (which may re-derive beliefs each turn); three-family replication, dose-response analysis, and independent-protocol transfer provide reasonable academic-budget coverage.

Name: loose_talk_tolerance_axis
Title: Close Enough Is True: A Latent Standard-of-Precision Axis Governing How LLMs Judge Literally-False-but-Loosely-True Claims
Short Hypothesis: Mirroring human loose talk / pragmatic imprecision (literally-false statements like 'the bottle is empty' for a nearly-empty bottle, or 'I waited an hour' for 50 minutes, are judged true when close enough to a contextual standard of precision), an LLM's belief-valence/truth readout treats loosely-true-but-literally-false claims as TRUE, governed by a separable, near-orthogonal latent 'standard-of-precision' (SoP) axis distinct from the truth direction; the SoP axis sets the tolerated deviation, is decodable, causally predicts whether the model accepts an imprecise claim as true, tracks context-driven SoP shifts (a strict-precision cue tightens tolerance), and can be steered to make the model literal-minded or loose.
Related Work: Interpretability fits a linear truth/belief direction (Geometry of Truth 2023; Truth is Universal 2024's 2D general+polarity subspace; VAA 2025; The Internal State Knows When It's Lying 2023) and shows validity/plausibility are conflated linear directions (How LMs Conflate Logical Validity with Plausibility 2025). Human science establishes loose talk / imprecision as pragmatic: literally-false claims are felicitous and judged true when within a contextual Standard of Precision (Truthfulness and Relevance, Sperber & Wilson 2002, 553 cites; Nonliteral understanding of number words / pragmatic halo 2014, 194 cites; Vagueness and Imprecision 2015; truth-truthfulness entanglement 2023/2026), and the SoP is context-dependent and dynamically negotiable (On the Optimality of Vagueness 2020; Disagreements do not automatically raise the standard of precision 2025; Meaning adaptation in the discourse dynamics of imprecision 2025; social-persona precision effects 2022). Crucially, ALL LLM truth-representation work assumes claims are literally true/false and asks whether the model tracks literal truth; NONE isolates whether the belief/truth readout tolerates IMPRECISION—treating a literally-false-but-close-enough claim as true—defines a decodable Standard-of-Precision axis that sets the tolerated deviation, tests whether it tracks context-driven SoP shifts, or causally steers literal-vs-loose interpretation. This differs from my prior borderline_vagueness_axis (semantic indeterminacy of a single gradable predicate near its threshold: 'is 5'10" tall?', where there is no fact of the matter), typicality_truth_conflation (category membership), and contestedness (social dispute): here the claim has a determinate literal truth-value (it IS literally false), yet is pragmatically accepted as true if within tolerance—the exact loose-talk phenomenon, with the SoP as a distinct, context-sensitive, steerable knob. We move from 'the model represents literal truth' to 'the model tolerates imprecision via a decodable, steerable standard-of-precision axis.'
Abstract: People routinely say things that are literally false but close enough to be true: 'the theater is empty' when a few people remain, 'I waited an hour' after 50 minutes, 'it's 3 o'clock' at 2:58. Whether such a loose claim counts as true depends on a contextual Standard of Precision (SoP)—and this tolerance is pragmatic, not semantic. As LLMs judge and generate factual claims, we ask whether they represent imprecision tolerance internally. Prior interpretability work fits a linear truth direction and assumes claims are literally true or false; none isolates whether the model's truth readout accepts literally-false-but-loosely-true claims, nor a mechanism that sets how much imprecision is tolerated. We hypothesize a separable, near-orthogonal latent 'standard-of-precision' axis, decodable at read time, that governs the tolerated deviation between a claim and reality, distinct from the belief-valence/truth direction; that loosely-true-but-literally-false claims read as TRUE when within tolerance and false when outside it; that the per-item SoP readout predicts whether the model accepts an imprecise claim; that the axis tracks context-driven SoP shifts (an explicit precision cue tightens tolerance, mirroring humans); and that steering it makes the model literal-minded (rejecting close-enough claims) or loose (accepting even large deviations). Using claims that orthogonally vary deviation magnitude from the true value, contextual precision standard, and content, against a graded loose-truth benchmark, we fit an SoP axis, measure separability via cross-decoding, quantify per-item imprecision tolerance, and connect it to behavioral truth judgments. Double-dissociation steering tests literal-vs-loose control without changing the model's grasp of the literal facts, with norm-matched and shuffled-direction controls across three model families. Our results recast loose talk mechanistically as a decodable, steerable standard-of-precision axis.
Experiments: 1. Direction setup. On LLaMA-3.1-8B-Instruct, Mistral-7B-Instruct, and Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct, fit a frozen belief-valence/truth direction on standard true/false statement datasets (cities, sp_en_trans, larger_than and negations; Marks & Tegmark) with mass-mean and logistic-regression probes at the best layer; validate on held-out atomics; also isolate the polarity-robust general-truth direction (Truth is Universal) as a control.

2. Imprecision stimulus construction with a graded loose-truth benchmark. Build ~500 claims about quantities/states with a known true value, each rendered as a claim that DEVIATES from the truth by a controlled magnitude, spanning: (a) EXACT-TRUE (claim matches reality), (b) LOOSELY-TRUE (literally false but within a small, pragmatically-tolerable deviation, e.g. 'I waited an hour' for 50 minutes, 'the bottle is empty' for a few drops, 'it's 3pm' at 2:58, 'the room is empty' with one person), (c) OUT-OF-TOLERANCE-FALSE (literally false and far outside tolerance, e.g. 'I waited an hour' for 20 minutes), and (d) EXACT-FALSE. Use round-number and absolute-adjective ('empty/full/straight/flat') items where loose talk is well-documented. Independently vary the CONTEXTUAL STANDARD OF PRECISION via cues (STRICT: a scientific/measurement/legal framing or an explicit 'be exact' instruction; LOOSE: a casual conversational framing) that should tighten/loosen tolerance without changing the literal facts. Human annotation (or established loose-truth norms) establishes the per-item tolerated deviation. Use paraphrase templates; reserve held-out claims/templates for transfer.

3. SoP-axis fitting and separability. Extract activations over the claim span and fit a linear probe to decode WITHIN-TOLERANCE (loosely-true) vs OUT-OF-TOLERANCE (far-false), controlling for literal truth-value and deviation direction. Report AUROC vs shuffled-label controls; measure cosine similarity and cross-decoding between the SoP axis and the frozen truth/belief-valence direction to establish near-orthogonality (the SoP axis must set tolerance independent of literal truth—note loosely-true and exact-false are both LITERALLY false, so the truth axis alone cannot separate them). Localize the best layer.

4. Imprecision-tolerance metric. For each literally-false claim, project onto the frozen truth direction and measure how far it reads as TRUE as a function of deviation magnitude; fit a per-model tolerance threshold (the deviation at which the truth readout crosses neutral). Core predictions: LOOSELY-TRUE claims read as TRUE (near exact-true) despite being literally false, OUT-OF-TOLERANCE claims read false, and the crossover deviation defines the model's implicit SoP; the truth readout is graded with deviation (a tolerance profile) rather than a sharp literal cutoff. Report tolerance thresholds and profiles across content types (round numbers, absolute adjectives, durations).

5. Context-driven SoP-shift test (human-analogous). Test whether the STRICT vs LOOSE context cue shifts the tolerance threshold: STRICT should tighten tolerance (loosely-true claims read less true / rejected), LOOSE should widen it, holding literal facts fixed—mirroring the human context-dependent SoP. Verify the SoP axis (not the truth axis) tracks this shift, and that the model's grasp of the literal deviation (measured by a separate 'exact-value' query) is unchanged, so the shift is tolerance re-setting, not altered fact perception.

6. Behavioral prediction. Elicit the model's true/false (and 'close enough?') judgment and confidence per claim. Score whether the model ACCEPTS loosely-true claims as true and REJECTS out-of-tolerance ones. Test whether the per-item SoP/tolerance readout predicts acceptance beyond baselines (truth margin, deviation magnitude as a surface feature, output entropy, context-cue identity, item length); report incremental AUROC in nested logistic regression.

7. Double-dissociation causal steering. Steer the SoP axis (orthogonalized against the truth/belief-valence direction) at read time on held-out items. Predict: steering toward LITERAL tightens tolerance (the model rejects loosely-true claims as false) WITHOUT changing judgments on exact-true/exact-false controls or the model's decoded literal deviation; steering toward LOOSE widens tolerance (the model accepts even out-of-tolerance claims). As controls, steer the truth direction (should flip judgments regardless of tolerance, including on exact claims) and matched random/shuffled directions. Use norm-matched controls; sweep strengths and layers. Metric: change in the tolerance threshold / accept-reject boundary vs unchanged exact-control accuracy and literal-deviation readout.

8. Application and robustness. Build a training-free knob to make an LLM appropriately literal (in measurement/legal/medical settings, where 'the tank is empty' or 'the dose is 100mg' must not be loosely accepted) or appropriately loose (casual dialogue), and measure literal-precision gains in a strict domain while preserving natural loose-talk acceptance in casual framing (report over-literalism rate, over-looseness rate, exact-control accuracy vs a truth-probe-only baseline). Replicate across three model families and two probe methods; transfer the fitted SoP axis, tolerance metric, and steering to held-out claims/templates and an independent imprecision set (round-number and absolute-adjective items) without refitting; report per-template consistency under paraphrase and sensitivity to layer choice. As a human-parallel analysis, check whether the tolerance profile and context-driven SoP shifts qualitatively match the human loose-talk signatures (graded tolerance, tightening under strict cues).
Risk Factors and Limitations: The SoP axis may not be separable from the truth/belief-valence direction; we report cosine similarity, cross-decoding, orthogonalized steering, and incremental predictive power, and—because loosely-true and out-of-tolerance items are BOTH literally false—the truth axis cannot trivially separate them, so near-collapse (imprecision tolerance being merely the truth readout) is an informative negative result showing LLMs judge only literal truth.

The distinction between loosely-true and out-of-tolerance is graded and context-dependent, and the tolerated deviation is itself fuzzy; we mitigate with human-annotated per-item tolerance (or established loose-truth norms), use items with strong agreement at the extremes, treat the middle as a graded profile, and report annotation-agreement sensitivity.

Tolerance could be confounded with the surface deviation magnitude (a larger number just looks more false) rather than a genuine SoP abstraction; we control for deviation magnitude as a surface baseline, use both numeric (durations, round numbers) and non-numeric (absolute adjectives 'empty/full') items, and test whether the SoP axis predicts acceptance and the context-shift beyond a raw-deviation baseline.

The context-driven SoP shift may act through surface cues ('be exact') rather than a genuine standard-of-precision mechanism; we mitigate with diverse strict/loose framings (measurement, legal, casual), paraphrase templates, and held-out-template transfer, and verify the literal-deviation readout is unchanged across contexts so the effect is tolerance re-setting.

Truth/belief probes are brittle to context and surface form; we validate probes, use the polarity-robust general-truth direction, use paraphrases, standardize readout spans, and report per-template consistency.

The imprecision-tolerance / SoP signal is a linear projection that may miss nonlinear structure; we treat the tolerance threshold as a lower bound and report probe-fit diagnostics, cross-checking with behavioral accept-reject judgments.

Behavioral acceptance scoring depends on how the true/false (and 'close enough') question is phrased (the truth-truthfulness entanglement); we report sensitivity across multiple prompts (following the truth-value-judgment-task literature) and cross-check with confidence measures.
The effect may be weak or reasoning/RLHF-shaped (some models may default to literal); a null/literal result is itself an informative human-vs-machine comparison, reported via tolerance profiles.

Causal steering is sensitive to layer and strength; we use orthogonalized steering vectors, norm-matched and shuffled-direction controls, sweep strengths, and verify SoP steering shifts the tolerance boundary without altering exact-claim accuracy or the decoded literal deviation.
Findings on 7-8B instruct models may not transfer to frontier scale; three-family replication and independent-set transfer provide reasonable academic-budget coverage.

Name: reference_dependent_value_intransitivity
Title: Better Than What It's Next To: A Latent Reference-Dependent Comparative-Value Signal that Causes Intransitive LLM Preferences
Short Hypothesis: Mirroring the neuroscience finding that human intransitive choices arise because value signals are not absolute/ordinal but reflect pairing-dependent, context-shifted local ranks, an LLM's internal comparative-value for an option is REFERENCE-DEPENDENT—it shifts depending on which competitor it is currently paired against—carried by a separable, near-orthogonal latent 'reference-dependence' signal distinct from a context-invariant value/magnitude direction; the per-triple magnitude of this reference-dependence is decodable before the model answers, causally predicts and drives intransitive preference cycles (A>B, B>C, C>A), and can be steered to induce or eliminate cyclic violations.
Related Work: Behavioral work shows LLMs mostly satisfy but sometimes violate transitivity (Benchmarking the rationality of AI using the transitivity axiom 2025, violations only in Chat/Instruct models; Predictably intransitive preferences 2018 for humans) and that BERT fails to enforce IS-A transitivity (Does BERT Know the IS-A Relation Is Transitive 2022). Interpretability decodes preference/value directions (What Do Llamas Really Think / Bradley-Terry preference probe 2023), a belief/truth direction (Marks & Tegmark 2023), and belief-state geometry (Transformers Represent Belief State Geometry 2024). Crucially, human neuroscience (Neural signatures of intransitive preferences 2010, 38 cites) shows intransitivity is caused not by noise but by value signals being pairing/context-dependent rather than ordinal-transitive—the alternative presented shifts the priority given to each attribute. NO LLM work isolates whether comparative-value is REFERENCE-DEPENDENT (an option's decoded value moves with its competitor), defines a reference-dependence signal separable from a context-invariant value direction, or causally links that reference-dependence to intransitive cycles. All LLM transitivity work is behavioral (does the model cycle?), and preference-probe work decodes a STATIC preference direction, never the competitor-driven shift. This differs from my prior belief_coherence_geometry proposal (logical algebra of truth-projections, proj(P∧Q)≤min) which concerns propositional logical consistency, not ordinal/comparative value and reference-dependence. We move from 'LLMs sometimes violate transitivity' to 'the model represents comparative value reference-dependently, and this reference-dependence mechanistically causes cycles.'
Abstract: Rational choice requires transitivity: if A beats B and B beats C, A should beat C. Humans famously violate this, and neuroscience shows why—value is not encoded on a stable ordinal scale but shifts depending on which alternative an option is compared against, so the same option is valued differently in different pairings. As LLMs increasingly rank, compare, and choose, we ask whether they inherit this reference-dependence and whether it causes their intransitive preferences. Prior work measures LLM transitivity violations behaviorally and decodes static preference directions, but none isolates whether an option's internal comparative-value moves with its competitor, nor links such reference-dependence to cycles. We hypothesize a separable, near-orthogonal latent 'reference-dependence' signal, decodable before the model answers a pairwise comparison, that encodes how much an option's comparative-value is pulled by the specific competitor it faces, distinct from a context-invariant value/magnitude direction; that the per-triple magnitude of reference-dependence causally predicts intransitive cycles; and that steering it eliminates or induces cyclic violations. Using pairwise comparison tasks over multi-attribute options (magnitude x probability gambles, and general 'which is better/larger' items) arranged into triples, we decode each option's comparative-value across different pairings, quantify per-option reference-dependence, connect it to behavioral cycles, and perform double-dissociation steering with norm-matched and shuffled-direction controls across three model families. Our results transfer a landmark decision-neuroscience finding into a decodable, steerable mechanistic cause of LLM irrationality.
Experiments: 1. Direction setup. On LLaMA-3.1-8B-Instruct, Mistral-7B-Instruct, and Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct, fit a frozen belief/truth direction on standard true/false datasets (cities, sp_en_trans, larger_than and negations; Marks & Tegmark) at the best layer as a reference axis. Fit a CONTEXT-INVARIANT VALUE direction that decodes an option's stand-alone worth/magnitude (from single-option value/magnitude statements via linear regression; validate monotonic mapping on held-out items). This is the 'ideal ordinal value' baseline against which reference-dependence is measured.

2. Triple stimulus construction. Build ~300 option triples {A,B,C} in two domains: (a) multi-attribute GAMBLES varying magnitude and probability (adapting the Steinhaus-Trybula / Tversky designs known to elicit cycles), and (b) general comparative items ('which is larger/better/more X'). For each triple, present all three ordered pairwise comparisons (A vs B, B vs C, A vs C, plus reversed orders) in matched prompts asking which option is greater/preferred. Use paraphrase templates; reserve held-out triples/templates.

3. Reference-dependent value decoding. For each option, extract activations at a pre-answer readout position over that option's span WITHIN each pairing (e.g., A's representation when paired with B vs when paired with C) and project onto the context-invariant value direction, plus fit a per-context comparative-value probe. Define per-option REFERENCE-DEPENDENCE = the spread of an option's decoded comparative-value across the different competitors it faces (variance across pairings), relative to its context-invariant baseline. Report reference-dependence distributions and test the core structural claim: an option's decoded value shifts systematically with its competitor (nonzero reference-dependence), mirroring the human pairing-dependent value finding.

4. Reference-dependence axis and separability. Fit a linear probe to decode HIGH- vs LOW reference-dependence pairings (contexts where an option's value is strongly pulled by its competitor vs stable), controlling for the option content. Report AUROC vs shuffled-label controls; measure cosine similarity and cross-decoding between the reference-dependence axis, the context-invariant value direction, and the belief-valence direction to establish near-orthogonality (reference-dependence must be decodable independent of the option's stand-alone value).

5. Cycle prediction (core behavioral test). Record the model's stated pairwise choices for each triple and score INTRANSITIVE CYCLES (A>B, B>C, C>A), correcting for stochastic response noise via repeated sampling (following the true-and-error / two-error-term approach). Test whether per-triple aggregate reference-dependence predicts whether the triple yields a cycle, via logistic regression; report AUROC vs baselines (context-invariant value margins, output entropy, attribute-conflict magnitude, choice-noise rate). Test the neuroscience-inspired prediction that cycles concentrate in triples where attribute priority (magnitude vs probability) flips across pairings.

6. Dissociation from noise and from stand-alone value. Show, using response-time-analog repeated-sampling noise estimates, that reference-dependence predicts SYSTEMATIC cycles beyond what stochastic noise explains, and that on matched context-invariant-value triples the reference-dependence axis (not the stand-alone value margins) accounts for cycles—establishing reference-dependence as the mechanism rather than measurement noise or a static value ordering.

7. Double-dissociation causal steering. At the pre-answer position on held-out cycle-prone triples, steer to SUPPRESS reference-dependence (stabilize each option's comparative-value toward its context-invariant baseline, orthogonalized against the value direction) and measure reduction in intransitive cycles WITHOUT changing choices on non-conflicting control triples; conversely AMPLIFY reference-dependence and measure induced cycles. As a control, steer the context-invariant value direction (should shift which option wins uniformly, not create/remove cycles). Use norm-matched random-direction and shuffled-direction controls; sweep strengths and layers. Metric: change in corrected cycle rate vs preserved control-triple choices.

8. Application and robustness. Build a training-free rationality diagnostic that flags cycle-prone triples from the reference-dependence metric and steers to enforce transitivity; measure cycle-rate reduction and improved consistency of full rankings, and (as an application) improved reliability of LLM-as-judge pairwise preference rankings on a held-out set. Replicate across three model families and two probe methods; transfer the fitted axes and steering to held-out triples/domains without refitting; report per-template consistency under paraphrase and sensitivity to layer/readout position and option-presentation order. As a human-parallel analysis, check whether the model's reference-dependence and cycle profile qualitatively match the human pairing-dependent-value signature (attribute-priority flips across pairings driving cycles).
Risk Factors and Limitations: The reference-dependence signal may not be separable from the context-invariant value direction or the belief-valence direction; we report cosine similarity, cross-decoding, orthogonalized steering, and incremental predictive power, and treat near-collapse (comparative value being fully context-invariant) as an informative negative result meaning LLMs represent stable ordinal value and cycles are pure noise.

Behavioral intransitivity may be rare in strong/aligned models (prior work finds violations mainly in Chat/Instruct variants), so cycles may be too few to fit; we deliberately use gamble designs (Steinhaus-Trybula) known to elicit cycles, sample many triples, and report per-model base rates—low cycle rates are themselves an informative human-vs-machine comparison.

Distinguishing systematic reference-dependence from stochastic response noise is the crux; we use repeated sampling and true-and-error noise correction to estimate 'real' cycles, and test whether reference-dependence predicts cycles beyond the noise model.

Decoding an option's comparative-value within a specific pairing is delicate (options may not have clean spans; representations may entangle both options); we standardize readout spans, use matched paraphrases, and validate the context-invariant value probe on single-option items.

The value probe is graded and harder to calibrate than a binary truth probe; we validate the activation->value mapping, report calibration/probe-fit diagnostics, and treat reference-dependence as a lower bound.

Reference-dependence could reflect surface order/position effects (which option is mentioned first) rather than genuine competitor-driven value shift; we counterbalance option order, decode value controlling for position, and test whether the axis predicts cycles beyond a position-bias baseline.
Belief/value probes are brittle to surface form; we validate probes, use paraphrase templates, and report per-template consistency.

Causal steering is sensitive to layer and strength; we use orthogonalized steering vectors, norm-matched and shuffled-direction controls, sweep strengths, and verify reference-dependence suppression removes cycles without altering non-conflicting control choices or collapsing all options to a fixed ranking.

Findings on 7-8B instruct models may not transfer to frontier or reasoning-tuned models (which may be more transitive); three-family replication and held-out-domain transfer provide reasonable academic-budget coverage.

Name: sacred_value_tradeoff_resistance_axis
Title: Some Things Aren't For Sale: A Latent Sacredness Axis that Makes LLM Beliefs Resist Utilitarian Tradeoffs
Short Hypothesis: Mirroring the neuroscience of sacred/protected values (processed via deontological rule-retrieval and refusing material tradeoffs regardless of the cost-benefit magnitude), an LLM represents whether a held value/belief is SACRED (tradeoff-resistant, off the utilitarian scale) versus SECULAR (tradeoff-permitting) along a separable, near-orthogonal latent axis distinct from the belief-valence/endorsement direction and from a magnitude/utility direction; this sacredness axis is decodable, causally predicts whether the model refuses to trade the value off against escalating material offers (an insensitivity-to-magnitude signature), and can be steered to make a value negotiable or inviolable.
Related Work: Neuroscience robustly shows sacred/protected values are processed through deontological rule-retrieval (left TPJ/vlPFC/IFG), are resistant to material trade-offs, and—crucially—exhibit INSENSITIVITY TO OUTCOME MAGNITUDE, being defended irrespective of the size of the offered incentive (The price of your soul 2012, 188 cites; Neural evidence for sacred values & extremism 2018; Will to fight 2019; Processing Narratives Concerning Protected Values 2016). Behavioral moral-cognition work shows moral beliefs resist counter-evidence and utilitarian principles are revised only by rare counterexamples (A Single Counterexample Leads to Moral Belief Revision 2015), and that a value's defense is deontic rather than cost-benefit. In LLM interpretability, the Valence-Assent Axis co-encodes good=true (A Unified Representation 2025), Value Entanglement shows moral value contaminates other judgments (2026), a moral direction is decodable/steerable (Schramowski 2021), and belief/truth is linearly decodable (Marks & Tegmark 2023). Crucially, ALL LLM value work decodes moral CONTENT or a good/true valence; NONE isolates whether a value/belief is represented as SACRED—tradeoff-resistant and off the utilitarian scale—as an axis SEPARABLE from how strongly it is endorsed and from a utility/magnitude representation, defines a tradeoff-resistance / insensitivity-to-magnitude metric, or causally links it to refusing cost-benefit trades. This differs from my prior epistemic_basis_belief_axis (coherence-grounded vs affect-held, about WHY a belief is held and its evidence-revisability), belief_entrenchment_axis (generic pre-evidence revisability), is_ought_leakage_axis (descriptive->prescriptive crossing), and contestedness_axis (social disagreement): here the cut is deontic sacredness—whether a value admits ANY material tradeoff—and the defining behavioral signature is magnitude-insensitivity (refusing regardless of how large the offer), directly transferring the sacred-values neuroscience. We move from 'the model encodes moral valence' to 'the model represents whether a value is beyond price, and this sacredness axis causally governs tradeoff refusal.'
Abstract: Humans treat some values as sacred: they refuse to trade them off against material benefits no matter how large the incentive, and neuroscience shows such values are processed through deontological rule-retrieval rather than cost-benefit calculation, with a hallmark insensitivity to outcome magnitude. As LLMs increasingly make value-laden tradeoff decisions and advise on them, we ask whether they represent this sacred/secular distinction internally and whether it governs their willingness to trade a value off. Prior interpretability work decodes moral content and a good=true valence axis, but none isolates whether a value is represented as tradeoff-RESISTANT—off the utilitarian scale—separable from how strongly it is endorsed and from a utility/magnitude representation. We hypothesize a separable, near-orthogonal latent 'sacredness' axis, decodable at read time, that tags a value/belief as sacred (inviolable, non-negotiable) versus secular (tradeoff-permitting), distinct from the belief-valence/endorsement direction and from a magnitude/utility direction; that its per-item value causally predicts whether the model refuses to trade the value off against escalating material offers—exhibiting insensitivity to offer magnitude for sacred items but graded acceptance for secular ones; and that steering it makes an inviolable value negotiable or a mundane preference sacrosanct. Using tradeoff scenarios that orthogonally vary a value's sacredness, its endorsement strength, and the offered incentive magnitude, we fit a sacredness axis, measure separability via cross-decoding, quantify the magnitude-insensitivity signature, connect it to behavioral tradeoff refusal, and perform double-dissociation steering with norm-matched and shuffled-direction controls across three model families. Our results recast a landmark moral-cognition phenomenon as a decodable, steerable belief property in LLMs.
Experiments: 1. Direction setup. On LLaMA-3.1-8B-Instruct, Mistral-7B-Instruct, and Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct, fit a frozen belief-valence/endorsement direction on standard true/false and value-agreement datasets (cities, sp_en_trans, larger_than and negations from Marks & Tegmark, plus value-endorsement items) with mass-mean and logistic-regression probes at the best layer; validate on held-out items. Separately fit control axes: (a) a MAGNITUDE/UTILITY direction that decodes the size of a stated material offer/benefit (from graded-magnitude statements), and (b) a moral-VALENCE direction (good vs bad, following Schramowski/VAA constructions), so sacredness can be dissociated from how large the offer is and from moral valence.

2. Sacred vs secular tradeoff stimulus construction. Build ~400 tradeoff scenarios in which a value/belief is offered up for a material benefit, orthogonally varying: (i) SACREDNESS of the value—SACRED (identity/moral/religious/relational values known to be protected: e.g. betraying a loved one, violating a core moral commitment) vs SECULAR (mundane preferences: brand choice, minor convenience) vs a graded middle tier; (ii) the value's ENDORSEMENT STRENGTH (how strongly the model holds it), calibrated to be matched across sacredness where possible; and (iii) the OFFERED MAGNITUDE, swept across a ladder from small to very large (the key manipulation for magnitude-insensitivity). Use synthetic/neutral value framings alongside real ones to control priors. Use paraphrase templates; reserve held-out scenarios/templates for transfer.

3. Sacredness-axis fitting and separability. Extract activations over the value/readout span and fit a linear probe to decode SACRED vs SECULAR, controlling for endorsement strength and offer magnitude. Report AUROC vs shuffled-label controls; measure cosine similarity and cross-decoding among the sacredness axis, the belief-valence/endorsement direction, the magnitude/utility direction, and the moral-valence direction to establish that sacredness is (i) near-orthogonal to how strongly the value is endorsed and (ii) not merely the offer magnitude or moral valence. Localize the best layer.

4. Tradeoff-resistance / magnitude-insensitivity metric (core). For each scenario, read the model's internal 'willingness-to-trade' (project onto the belief-valence/endorsement direction under the offer) as a function of offer MAGNITUDE. Core prediction (the sacred-values signature): for SACRED items, willingness-to-trade is flat / insensitive to escalating offer magnitude (the value stays defended regardless of incentive size), whereas for SECULAR items willingness increases with magnitude (graded, utilitarian). Fit per-item magnitude-sensitivity slopes; define tradeoff-resistance = flatness of the willingness-vs-magnitude curve. Test whether the sacredness axis predicts which items are magnitude-insensitive, with effect sizes across the sacredness tiers.

5. Behavioral tradeoff-refusal prediction. Elicit the model's actual decision (accept/refuse the trade) and confidence at each offer magnitude. Score tradeoff refusal and magnitude-insensitivity (refusing regardless of offer size for sacred items). Test whether the per-item sacredness readout predicts refusal and the flat willingness-vs-magnitude curve via regression; report AUROC/R^2 vs baselines (endorsement margin, magnitude axis, moral-valence axis, output entropy, offer size as a surface feature, item length).

6. Dissociation from endorsement, magnitude, and valence (core). On matched-endorsement items (equally strongly held) varying only sacredness, and matched-sacredness items varying only offer magnitude, show the sacredness axis (not the endorsement, magnitude, or valence axes) accounts for the magnitude-insensitive refusal—establishing a genuine deontic tradeoff-resistance property rather than repackaged strong endorsement, offer size, or negativity. Report incremental predictive power in nested models.

7. Double-dissociation causal steering. Steer the sacredness axis (orthogonalized against endorsement, magnitude, and valence) at read time on held-out items. Predict: suppressing sacredness makes a SACRED value negotiable (willingness now rises with offer magnitude—utilitarian trading) WITHOUT changing how strongly the value is endorsed or behavior on secular controls; amplifying it makes a SECULAR preference inviolable (flat refusal regardless of magnitude). As controls, steer the endorsement direction (should change how strongly the value is held, not its tradeoff-resistance) and the magnitude axis (should shift perceived offer size). Use norm-matched random-direction and shuffled-direction controls; sweep strengths and layers. Metric: change in willingness-vs-magnitude slope / refusal pattern vs unchanged endorsement and secular-control behavior.

8. Application and robustness. Build a training-free diagnostic that flags when a model treats a value as sacred/inviolable vs negotiable (relevant for value-alignment auditing and for detecting brittle deontic commitments), and a knob to calibrate tradeoff-resistance; on a held-out set (including safety-relevant value tradeoffs) measure whether steering yields appropriate context-sensitive behavior. Replicate across three model families and two probe methods; transfer the fitted axis, resistance metric, and steering to held-out scenarios/templates and an independent sacred-values / protected-values stimulus set without refitting; report per-template consistency under paraphrase and sensitivity to layer choice. As a human-parallel analysis, check whether the model's sacred vs secular magnitude-sensitivity profile qualitatively matches the human sacred-values signature (flat, magnitude-insensitive defense of sacred values vs graded trading of secular ones).
Risk Factors and Limitations: The sacredness axis may not be separable from the endorsement direction, the magnitude/utility direction, or moral valence; we report cosine similarity, cross-decoding, orthogonalized steering, and incremental predictive power, and—because matched-endorsement items vary only sacredness and matched-sacredness items vary only offer magnitude—endorsement/magnitude cannot trivially explain separability; near-collapse (sacredness being merely very strong endorsement or negativity) is an informative negative result that itself sharpens the VAA/moral-direction accounts.

The behavioral magnitude-insensitivity signature may be weak or RLHF-shaped (aligned models may refuse or accept in ways decoupled from a genuine sacredness representation); a null/partial result is itself an informative human-vs-machine comparison, reported via willingness-vs-magnitude slopes across sacredness tiers.

Sacredness is signaled by content cues (moral/identity words) that could act as surface features rather than a genuine tradeoff-resistance abstraction; we mitigate with diverse paraphrase templates, synthetic/neutral value framings, matched-valence controls, and held-out-template transfer, testing whether the axis predicts magnitude-insensitivity beyond a moral-lexeme surface baseline.

Which values are 'sacred' is culturally variable and contested; we use values with strong cross-cultural agreement for the core set, treat the middle tier as graded, use multiple annotators, and report label-agreement sensitivity, noting the axis is measuring the MODEL's representation, not a normative ground truth.

Matching endorsement strength across sacred and secular items is delicate; we calibrate via the endorsement readout and behavioral confidence, and report sensitivity to residual endorsement differences.
Belief/value probes are brittle to context and surface form; we validate probes, use paraphrases, standardize readout spans, and report per-template consistency.

The sacredness signal and resistance metric are linear projections that may miss nonlinear structure; we treat them as lower bounds and report probe-fit diagnostics, cross-checking with behavioral refusal.
Behavioral tradeoff decisions are elicitation-sensitive (framing of the offer); we test multiple framings and report sensitivity.

Causal steering is sensitive to layer and strength; we use orthogonalized steering vectors, norm-matched and shuffled-direction controls, sweep strengths, and verify sacredness steering changes tradeoff-resistance without altering endorsement strength or degrading secular-control behavior.
Findings on 7-8B instruct models may not transfer to frontier or safety-tuned models; three-family replication and independent protected-values transfer provide reasonable academic-budget coverage.

Name: support_redundancy_belief_axis
Title: How Many Legs Does This Belief Stand On? A Latent Support-Redundancy Axis and the Machine Overdetermination-Neglect that Miscalibrates Belief Revision
Short Hypothesis: Mirroring how humans reason about deterministic causal support (a conclusion should survive if it has multiple independent supporting reasons but collapse if its single support fails), an LLM represents a held belief's SUPPORT REDUNDANCY—whether it rests on ONE support (brittle/single-legged) versus MULTIPLE INDEPENDENT supports (overdetermined/robust)—along a separable, near-orthogonal latent axis distinct from the belief-valence direction and from belief strength/confidence; this redundancy axis is decodable, causally predicts how much counter-evidence against a single support flips the belief (single-support beliefs should flip, overdetermined ones should not), and the model exhibits OVERDETERMINATION-NEGLECT (treating multiply-supported beliefs as no more robust than singly-supported ones), which the axis's collapse decodably predicts and steering can correct.
Related Work: Interpretability shows belief/truth is linearly decodable and a context-sensitive causal mediator whose value moves when a supporting premise is pushed along the truth direction (Marks & Tegmark 2023; Truth-value probes are context sensitive 2024), false-premise disruption is localized to shallow heads (FAITH 2024), belief manifolds are curved (The Shape of Beliefs 2026), and counterfactual/overdetermination challenges for interpretability are noted (Missed Causes and Ambiguous Effects 2024: counterfactual methods MISS overdetermined causes). Human science shows people respect the number and determinism of supporting causal links when reasoning counterfactually about whether a conclusion survives (Explanations of Counterfactual Inferences 2012; Structural Determinants 2001; From counterfactual simulation to causal judgment 2014). Crucially, ALL LLM belief work reads WHETHER/how-strongly a proposition is believed or WHO holds it; NONE isolates whether a held belief's SUPPORT REDUNDANCY (single vs multiple independent supports) is a decodable axis SEPARABLE from belief strength, defines an overdetermination-neglect metric, or causally links redundancy to how counter-evidence against ONE support should (not) flip the belief. This differs from my prior belief_entrenchment_axis (a forward-looking revisability tag agnostic to WHY the belief is revisable), derivational_provenance_belief (recall vs derive, and premise-vs-conclusion attack, but NOT the number/independence of supports nor overdetermination-neglect), epistemic_basis_belief_axis (coherence-vs-affect basis), and source_independence_belief axis (independent vs echoed corroboration of ONE claim's testimony, not the multi-support structure of the belief itself). We uniquely transfer the human deterministic-link/overdetermination signature into a decodable, steerable support-redundancy axis governing normatively-correct single-support-attack revision.
Abstract: A well-grounded belief that rests on several independent reasons should survive the loss of any one of them, whereas a belief propped up by a single reason should collapse when that reason fails—humans track this and reason accordingly. As LLMs justify and revise beliefs, we ask whether they represent a belief's support redundancy internally and whether mis-representing it miscalibrates revision. Prior interpretability work shows LLMs linearly encode whether and how strongly a proposition is believed and that pushing a supporting premise moves the belief, but none isolates whether a belief rests on one support versus multiple independent ones—its overdetermination structure. We hypothesize a separable, near-orthogonal latent 'support-redundancy' axis, decodable at read time, that tags a held belief as single-support (brittle) versus multiply-supported (overdetermined/robust), distinct from the belief-valence direction and from belief strength/confidence; that this axis causally predicts the normatively-correct single-support-attack behavior—counter-evidence defeating ONE support should flip a single-support belief but NOT an overdetermined one; that the model exhibits overdetermination-neglect (treating redundantly-supported beliefs as no more robust than singly-supported ones), predictable from the axis collapsing onto the single-support region; and that steering the axis corrects the neglect. Using held beliefs whose support structure (number and independence of supporting reasons) is varied while belief strength is matched, we fit a redundancy axis, measure separability via cross-decoding, run single-support-attack counter-evidence, quantify overdetermination-neglect against a normative benchmark, and perform double-dissociation steering with norm-matched and shuffled-direction controls across three model families.
Experiments: 1. Direction setup. On LLaMA-3.1-8B-Instruct, Mistral-7B-Instruct, and Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct, fit a frozen belief-valence/truth direction on standard true/false statement datasets (cities, sp_en_trans, larger_than and negations; Marks & Tegmark) with mass-mean and logistic-regression probes at the best layer; validate on held-out atomics. Separately fit a belief-STRENGTH/confidence control axis (empirical answer-stability / margin), so support-redundancy can be dissociated from how strongly the belief is held.

2. Support-structure stimulus construction. Build ~400 conclusions each established in-context as believed, holding the conclusion and the model's belief STRENGTH matched while varying SUPPORT STRUCTURE: (a) SINGLE-SUPPORT (one reason/premise supports it), (b) MULTIPLE-INDEPENDENT-SUPPORT (two or more independent reasons each sufficient, an overdetermined belief), and a graded tier (2, 3 supports). Use synthetic-entity facts and explicit reason chains (validated for support independence via rule checks + LLM judge + human spot-checks) so structure is controlled and not confounded with content difficulty. Include DEPENDENT-SUPPORT controls (multiple reasons that all hinge on one shared premise, so they are NOT truly redundant). Use paraphrase templates; reserve held-out conclusions/templates for transfer.

3. Support-redundancy axis fitting and separability. Extract activations over the conclusion/readout span and fit a linear probe to decode SINGLE-SUPPORT vs MULTIPLE-INDEPENDENT-SUPPORT, controlling for belief strength and content. Report AUROC vs shuffled-label controls; measure cosine similarity and cross-decoding between the redundancy axis, the belief-valence direction, and the belief-strength axis to establish that redundancy is (i) near-orthogonal to whether/how strongly the conclusion is believed and (ii) not merely confidence. Localize the best layer.

4. Single-support-attack revision measurement (core, normative). For each held belief, present counter-evidence that defeats exactly ONE of its supporting reasons and measure belief revision (belief-valence projection shift and stated-answer flip). Normative prediction: SINGLE-SUPPORT beliefs should flip; MULTIPLE-INDEPENDENT-SUPPORT beliefs should NOT (a surviving support remains); DEPENDENT-SUPPORT controls should flip (the shared premise is gone). Test whether the per-belief redundancy readout predicts single-support-attack survival, beyond baselines (belief-valence margin, strength axis, output entropy, number-of-supports as a surface count, item length).

5. Overdetermination-neglect metric (core signature). Define neglect = the degree to which MULTIPLE-INDEPENDENT-SUPPORT beliefs behave like SINGLE-SUPPORT ones under single-support attack (flipping when they should not), and correspondingly the degree to which the redundancy axis COLLAPSES onto the single-support region for overdetermined beliefs. Core prediction (mirroring interpretability's overdetermination-blindness and human single-legged reasoning failures): the model over-revises overdetermined beliefs, and the redundancy axis's collapse predicts this per item. Report neglect across support-count tiers with effect sizes.

6. Dissociation from strength and support-count surface cues. On matched-belief-strength items varying only support structure, show the redundancy axis (not the strength or belief-valence axes) accounts for single-support-attack survival; and show it predicts survival beyond a raw support-COUNT surface feature and correctly distinguishes DEPENDENT-support (not robust) from truly-independent-support (robust)—establishing genuine independence-structure representation. Report incremental predictive power in nested models.

7. Double-dissociation causal steering. On held-out overdetermined beliefs undergoing single-support attack, steer along the support-redundancy axis (orthogonalized against belief-valence and strength). Predict: amplifying redundancy corrects overdetermination-neglect (the belief correctly SURVIVES the single-support attack) WITHOUT changing the believed value on no-attack controls; suppressing it makes even genuinely overdetermined beliefs brittle (flip on single-support attack). As controls, steer belief-valence (should flip the value directly) and strength (should shift hedging). Use norm-matched random-direction and shuffled-direction controls; sweep strengths and layers. Metric: change in single-support-attack survival vs unchanged no-attack belief and appropriate flipping of genuine single-support/dependent-support beliefs.

8. Application and robustness. Build a training-free diagnostic that flags brittle single-support beliefs vs robust overdetermined ones and corrects overdetermination-neglect (useful for calibrated belief revision and misinformation resistance: a well-supported true belief should not be toppled by defeating one prop, while a single-support false belief should be correctable). Measure improved calibration of revision (survival of overdetermined beliefs, correction of single-support ones) vs a belief-probe-only baseline. Replicate across three model families and two probe methods; transfer the fitted axis, neglect metric, and steering to held-out conclusions/templates and an independent multi-support reasoning set without refitting; report per-template consistency under paraphrase and sensitivity to layer choice. As a human-parallel analysis, check whether the model respects deterministic multi-support survival as humans do, or exhibits systematic overdetermination-neglect.
Risk Factors and Limitations: The support-redundancy axis may not be separable from the belief-valence direction or belief strength; we report cosine similarity, cross-decoding, orthogonalized steering, and incremental predictive power, and—because belief strength is matched while support structure varies—strength cannot trivially explain separability; near-collapse (redundancy being merely strength/confidence) is an informative negative result showing LLMs do not represent overdetermination structure distinctly.

The single-support-attack survival prediction assumes the supports are genuinely independent and each sufficient; imperfect independence would make survival ambiguous. We validate support independence and sufficiency with rule checks + LLM judge + human spot-checks, include DEPENDENT-support controls, and condition analyses on validated items.

Support structure is signaled by the number/phrasing of stated reasons; the axis might reflect a raw support-count surface feature rather than a genuine redundancy/independence abstraction. We control for support count as a surface baseline, use the dependent-vs-independent contrast (same count, different robustness), diverse paraphrase templates, and held-out-template transfer, testing whether the axis predicts survival beyond a count baseline.

The overdetermination-neglect effect may be weak or reasoning/RLHF-shaped (strong models may reason correctly about multi-support survival); a null/normative result is itself an informative human-vs-machine comparison, reported via effect sizes against the normative single-support-attack benchmark.

Belief/truth probes are brittle to context and surface form and belief manifolds can be curved (The Shape of Beliefs 2026); we validate probes, use paraphrase templates, standardize readout spans, restrict key analyses to high-margin cases, and report per-template consistency, treating the axis as a lower bound.

Behavioral revision is protocol-dependent (how the single-support counter-evidence is phrased/escalated); we report sensitivity across counter-evidence protocols and cross-check internal belief trajectories against stated-answer flips to separate genuine revision from surface compliance.

Causal steering is sensitive to layer and strength; we use orthogonalized steering vectors, norm-matched and shuffled-direction controls, sweep strengths, and verify redundancy steering changes single-support-attack survival without altering the no-attack believed value or making the model ignore genuinely decisive counter-evidence against all supports.

Findings on 7-8B instruct models may not transfer to frontier or reasoning-tuned models (which may reason more correctly about overdetermination); three-family replication and held-out transfer provide reasonable academic-budget coverage.

Name: warranted_vs_spurious_demographic_use
Title: Right Answer, Which Reason? Auditing Whether an LLM's Clinical Decisions Use Demographics Epidemiologically or Stereotypically
Short Hypothesis: In clinical decision tasks, an LLM's internal use of a patient's demographic attribute decomposes into two distinguishable pathways — an EPIDEMIOLOGICALLY-WARRANTED pathway (the attribute legitimately shifts a probability because a disease's real base rate differs by group) and a SPURIOUS-STEREOTYPE pathway (the attribute shifts the decision via a stereotype uncorrelated with, or opposite to, the true base rate). These two pathways are separable in activation space and recruit distinguishable features; a decision-auditing procedure that traces which pathway a given decision rests on can flag stereotype-driven decisions that a bias probe treating demographics as one monolithic direction would either miss (when warranted and spurious use co-occur) or over-correct (when demographic use is actually clinically appropriate).
Related Work: Prior mechanistic-fairness work treats a demographic attribute as a single bias direction/subspace to be located and neutralized: Elucidating Mechanisms of Demographic Bias in Healthcare (2025) patches localized gender/race representations; Linear socio-demographic representations (2025) and What Do Llamas Really Think (2023) probe implicit demographic bias behind refusals; Robustly Improving LLM Fairness via Interpretability (2025) and On the Effectiveness of Race Representations (2025) apply affine/subspace edits to reduce hiring/admissions bias; Measuring Mechanistic Independence (2025) uses SAE ablations to separate bias from demographic RECOGNITION. Behavioral work (Detecting clinician implicit biases via proximal causal inference 2024; healthcare implicit-bias reviews) documents demographic disparities. Crucially, ALL of this frames demographic use as monolithically undesirable — the goal is to erase/neutralize the attribute's influence, and Measuring Mechanistic Independence's cut is bias-vs-recognition, not warranted-vs-spurious USE. NONE asks whether a demographic attribute's influence on a clinical decision splits into an epidemiologically WARRANTED component (which a good clinician SHOULD use — e.g., higher cardiac base rate in older men, sickle-cell prior in Black patients) versus a SPURIOUS stereotype component, whether these two pathways are mechanistically separable, or builds a decision-auditing procedure that flags stereotype-driven decisions while PRESERVING warranted demographic use. Our distinction (warranted vs spurious use, right-reason vs wrong-reason) is a Decision-Auditing question, not a bias-magnitude one, and blanket neutralization (the prior remedy) would destroy the warranted pathway and worsen calibration on group-varying diseases — a failure mode our framing predicts and no prior work tests.
Abstract: As LLMs enter clinical decision support, the accepted mechanistic remedy for demographic bias is to locate a demographic direction and neutralize its influence. But this treats all demographic use as harmful, ignoring that a patient's age, sex, or race legitimately shifts disease probabilities because real base rates differ by group — using them is good medicine. We ask whether an LLM's use of a demographic attribute in a clinical decision decomposes into two distinguishable pathways: an EPIDEMIOLOGICALLY-WARRANTED pathway (the attribute moves the decision in the direction and roughly the magnitude that true group base rates justify) and a SPURIOUS-STEREOTYPE pathway (the attribute moves the decision via a stereotype uncorrelated with, or opposite to, the true base rate). We hypothesize these pathways are separable in activation space, recruit distinguishable features, and can be teased apart by a decision-auditing procedure. Using clinical vignettes where the demographic attribute is swapped while symptoms are held fixed, and a curated set of conditions with KNOWN epidemiological direction of the demographic effect, we (1) measure the model's per-condition demographic sensitivity and split it into a warranted component (aligned with epidemiology) and a residual spurious component; (2) locate features/directions carrying each and test whether they are separable via cross-decoding and sparse-feature attribution; (3) audit individual decisions to classify their demographic reliance as warranted vs spurious; and (4) show causally that ablating the spurious component removes stereotype-driven shifts while a blanket demographic-neutralization baseline destroys warranted shifts and worsens calibration on group-varying diseases. Our results reframe clinical LLM fairness from erasing demographics to auditing the reason a demographic was used.
Experiments: 1. Model and probe setup. On LLaMA-3-8B-Instruct, Mistral-7B-Instruct, and a medically-tuned model (e.g., a Meditron/OpenBioLLM-class 7-8B model), fit demographic-attribute directions (sex, age band, race) using activation-patching-validated localization following prior clinical-bias work, and (as a control) a monolithic demographic bias direction/subspace as used by the debiasing baselines. Validate that the directions decode the swapped attribute from vignette activations.

2. Epidemiology-grounded condition set. Curate ~150 clinical conditions/decision items each labeled with the KNOWN direction (and, where available, rough magnitude) of the demographic effect on prevalence/pretest probability from authoritative sources (e.g., CDC/epidemiology references): WARRANTED-POSITIVE (attribute genuinely raises the disease probability, e.g., older-male + cardiac, Black + sickle-cell), WARRANTED-NEGATIVE, and NEUTRAL (no real base-rate difference). Build counterfactual vignette pairs: identical symptom presentation with only the patient's demographic swapped. Reserve held-out conditions for transfer.

3. Demographic-sensitivity decomposition (core). For each item, measure the model's decision shift (e.g., risk estimate / differential-diagnosis ranking / test-ordering) between demographic-swapped vignettes, both behaviorally and on the demographic direction's projection. Decompose per-item sensitivity into a WARRANTED component = the part aligned in sign (and calibrated magnitude) with the labeled epidemiological effect, and a SPURIOUS component = the residual shift on NEUTRAL items and any shift OPPOSITE to the true epidemiological direction. Report the warranted/spurious split per model and condition class.

4. Pathway separability (Location + Unit Interpretation). Test whether warranted and spurious demographic use are separable: (a) cross-decoding — can a probe trained to predict warranted-shift items generalize to spurious-shift items or are they distinct? (b) sparse-feature attribution — using a pretrained SAE (Gemma Scope on Gemma-2-9B as an added model) or attribution-patching, identify features whose activation drives the WARRANTED shift vs the SPURIOUS shift, and check feature overlap vs shuffled-label controls. Report cosine similarity/cross-decoding and per-feature concept labels (auto-interpretation).

5. Per-decision audit and classification. Build a decision-auditing readout that, for a single unseen vignette decision, classifies whether its demographic reliance is WARRANTED, SPURIOUS, or NONE, from the pathway attributions in step 4. Validate against the epidemiology labels; report AUROC for detecting spurious-driven decisions, and crucially test the failure mode of the monolithic baseline: on items where warranted and spurious use CO-OCCUR, does a monolithic bias-magnitude probe conflate them (miss the spurious part or flag the warranted part)?

6. Causal specificity of ablation. Ablate/patch the SPURIOUS component and measure that stereotype-driven shifts (NEUTRAL items and epidemiology-opposite shifts) collapse WHILE warranted shifts are preserved. Compare against the blanket demographic-neutralization baseline (averaging/zeroing the monolithic demographic direction, as in prior debiasing): predict the baseline removes warranted shifts too and degrades calibration/accuracy on WARRANTED conditions (group-varying diseases). Use norm-matched random-direction and shuffled controls; sweep strengths.

7. Calibration/utility trade-off. On a held-out clinical-decision set with ground-truth group-conditional outcomes (or epidemiology-derived pretest probabilities), measure calibration and diagnostic accuracy under (a) no intervention, (b) blanket neutralization, (c) spurious-only ablation. Prediction: spurious-only ablation reduces stereotype-driven disparities without the calibration loss that blanket neutralization incurs on warranted conditions.

8. Robustness and generalization. Replicate across the model families and two localization methods; transfer the audit and spurious-ablation to held-out conditions/templates and demographic attributes without refitting; report per-template consistency under symptom paraphrase, sensitivity to how epidemiological ground truth is specified, and whether the warranted/spurious separability holds for race (more distributed) vs sex (more localized), following prior localization findings.
Risk Factors and Limitations: The warranted and spurious pathways may not be separable in activation space (a single monolithic demographic direction may drive both); we report cross-decoding, feature-overlap, and ablation-specificity metrics, and treat non-separability as an informative negative result that would justify (rather than refute) blanket neutralization and sharpen the bias-vs-recognition account of Measuring Mechanistic Independence.

Epidemiological ground truth (direction/magnitude of a demographic effect on disease probability) is itself contested and can encode structural bias in the source statistics; we use authoritative, well-cited sources, restrict the core analysis to conditions with strong consensus on effect direction, treat magnitude only coarsely, report sensitivity to the ground-truth specification, and are explicit that 'warranted' means consistent with reference epidemiology, not normatively beyond dispute.

The warranted/spurious decomposition (aligned-with-epidemiology vs residual) is a modeling choice; a shift could be spurious yet coincidentally epidemiology-aligned, or warranted-magnitude could be mis-estimated. We mitigate by anchoring on NEUTRAL items (any shift is spurious) and epidemiology-OPPOSITE shifts (unambiguously spurious) for the cleanest tests, and treat aligned-magnitude claims as secondary.

Demographic directions and localization are known to be more distributed for race than sex, and brittle to prompt format (prior work); we validate localization per attribute, use activation-patching validation, and report per-attribute and per-format robustness rather than assuming a universal representation.

Behavioral decision measures (risk estimates, differential rankings, test-ordering) are elicitation-sensitive and may not reflect real clinical decisions; we use multiple decision formats, report sensitivity, and frame findings as decision-support audits, not clinical validation.

Causal ablation may degrade unrelated clinical reasoning; we use norm-matched random-direction and shuffled controls, sweep strengths, and verify off-target accuracy/perplexity retention, following prior clinical-interpretability practice.

This work engages sensitive demographic-in-clinical-decisions territory; a 'warranted demographic use' framing risks legitimizing harmful proxies, so we scope 'warranted' strictly to consensus epidemiology, emphasize the audit is for flagging spurious use and preventing over-correction, use synthetic vignettes, and do not claim any clinical deployment readiness.

Findings on 7-9B models (including one medically-tuned model) may not transfer to frontier or production clinical models; three-family replication and held-out-condition transfer provide reasonable academic-budget coverage.

Name: analytic_synthetic_belief_axis
Title: True by Meaning or True by World? A Latent Analytic-Synthetic Axis and the Machine Category Mistake in Belief Revision
Short Hypothesis: LLMs represent whether a proposition is ANALYTIC (true by meaning/definition/convention: 'a bachelor is unmarried', '2+2=4') versus SYNTHETIC (true by how the world is: 'the capital of France is Paris') along a separable, near-orthogonal latent 'analyticity' axis distinct from the truth/belief-valence direction and from generic confidence; the degree to which the two collapse (an 'analyticity-confusion' signature) is decodable and causally predicts and drives two symmetric revision failures—treating analytic truths as evidence-revisable (updating a definitional truth given fake empirical 'counter-evidence') and treating synthetic facts as unrevisable stipulations (refusing to update a world-fact given genuine correction, or conversely accepting a redefinition of an analytic term as if it changed a world-fact); steering the axis can suppress or induce this confusion.
Related Work: Interpretability fits a single linear truth/belief direction (Geometry of Truth 2023) refined to a 2D general+polarity subspace (Truth is Universal 2024; From Directions to Cones 2025), shows it is context-sensitive and evidence-updatable (Truth-value probes are context sensitive 2024), brittle to surface form (LLM Knowledge is Brittle 2025; Representational Stability of Truth 2025), and studies belief-state geometry and belief depth of implanted facts (Transformers Represent Belief State Geometry 2024; The Shape of Beliefs 2026; Believe It or Not 2025). Philosophy (Quine, Kant) treats the analytic/synthetic distinction and its erosion. Crucially, ALL truth-representation work treats a proposition's truth as a single quantity to be tracked and (as evidence arrives) revised, and never asks whether the model represents the SOURCE of a proposition's truth—true-by-meaning vs true-by-world—as an axis, defines an analyticity-confusion metric, or tests the DEFINING revision asymmetry: analytic truths are immune to empirical counter-evidence but revisable by stipulating a new definition, whereas synthetic truths are the reverse. This differs from my prior necessity_contingency_axis (modal robustness of a true fact—could-it-have-been-otherwise), falsifiability_axis (empirical testability of a meaningful claim), epistemic_basis_belief_axis (coherence-vs-affect basis), and paradox_ungroundedness_axis (truth-aptness under self-reference): here the cut is the GROUND of truth (meaning vs world) and its signature is a specific, causally-testable revision asymmetry no prior work isolates. We move from 'the model tracks and revises truth' to 'the model represents whether a truth is definitional or empirical, and confusing the two mechanistically produces category mistakes in belief revision.'
Abstract: 'A triangle has three sides' is true by definition; 'Paris is the capital of France' is true because of how the world is. A capable reasoner treats these differently: definitional (analytic) truths are immune to empirical counter-evidence but can be overturned by redefining the term, whereas empirical (synthetic) truths are the reverse—no counter-evidence should shake a definition, and no redefinition should rewrite a world-fact. We ask whether LLMs represent this distinction internally. Prior interpretability work fits a single truth direction that is uniformly evidence-revisable, but none asks whether the model encodes the SOURCE of a proposition's truth—true-by-meaning versus true-by-world. We hypothesize a separable, near-orthogonal latent 'analyticity' axis, decodable at read time, that tags a proposition as analytic versus synthetic, distinct from the belief-valence/truth direction and from confidence; and an 'analyticity-confusion' signature predictive per item of two symmetric revision failures: revising a definitional truth under fake empirical counter-evidence, and revising (or refusing to revise) a world-fact as if it were a stipulation. Using matched analytic and synthetic true statements, and challenge protocols that cross the revision operator (empirical counter-evidence vs redefinition) with the proposition type, we fit an analyticity axis, measure separability via cross-decoding, quantify per-item confusion, and connect it to behavioral revision asymmetry. Double-dissociation steering tests whether suppressing confusion restores the correct revision asymmetry (analytic beliefs resist empirical challenge but yield to redefinition; synthetic beliefs the reverse) and amplifying it induces category mistakes, with norm-matched and shuffled-direction controls across three model families. Our results recast a foundational epistemic distinction mechanistically as a decodable, steerable belief axis governing what kind of challenge should revise a belief.
Experiments: 1. Direction setup. On LLaMA-3.1-8B-Instruct, Mistral-7B-Instruct, and Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct, fit a frozen belief-valence/truth direction on standard true/false statement datasets (cities, sp_en_trans, larger_than and negations; Marks & Tegmark) with mass-mean and logistic-regression probes at the best layer; validate on held-out atomics; also isolate the polarity-robust general-truth direction (Truth is Universal) as a control. Fit a confidence control axis from empirical answer-correctness rates (sampled).

2. Analytic vs synthetic stimulus construction. Build ~500 TRUE propositions holding surface form matched while varying the GROUND of truth: (a) ANALYTIC—true by meaning/definition/convention (conceptual: 'a bachelor is unmarried'; mathematical: '7 is prime'; logical: 'if it is raining then it is raining'; stipulative definitions of terms), and (b) SYNTHETIC—true by how the world is (geographic, historical, scientific-empirical facts). Both classes are TRUE, so the truth axis alone cannot separate them. Include matched FALSE variants (analytic-false: 'a bachelor is married'; synthetic-false), a graded/borderline tier (e.g. nomic 'water is H2O', debated between analytic and synthetic), and synthetic-entity stipulations to control priors. Human/philosophy-informed annotation establishes the analytic/synthetic label. Use paraphrase templates; reserve held-out items/templates for transfer.

3. Analyticity-axis fitting and separability. Extract activations over the proposition span and fit a linear probe to decode ANALYTIC vs SYNTHETIC among TRUE statements, controlling for content and confidence.
