Operationalizing 'interrupted vs completed goal' cleanly is delicate (partial completion is graded, and the interruption text differs from the completion text); we control the interruption point, use content-matched interrupted/completed pairs, treat completion as graded where needed, and report sensitivity to the interruption position.

Belief/task-identity probes are brittle to context and surface form and drift over long contexts; we validate probes, use paraphrase templates, standardize the pre-resumption readout position, restrict key analyses to high-margin cases, and report per-template and context-length consistency.

The unfinished-goal signal is a linear projection that may miss nonlinear structure; we treat persistence/leakage as lower bounds and report probe-fit diagnostics, cross-checking with behavioral resumption.
Behavioral resumption and leakage scoring depend on how the resumption cue and intervening probes are phrased; we test multiple framings and report sensitivity.

Causal steering is sensitive to layer and strength; we use orthogonalized steering vectors, norm-matched and shuffled-direction controls, sweep strengths, and verify unfinished-goal steering changes resumption/persistence without altering task identity or degrading unrelated-control behavior.

Findings on 7-8B instruct models may not transfer to frontier or agent-tuned models (which may manage interruptions via explicit scratchpads); three-family replication, a within-family scale/reasoning-tuning trend, an agentic application, and held-out transfer provide reasonable academic-budget coverage.

Name: causal_transparency_evidence_integration
Title: Opaque Numbers, Neglected Base Rates: A Latent Causal-Transparency Axis that Gates How Fully an LLM Integrates Evidence
Short Hypothesis: Mirroring the human finding that base-rate neglect and conservatism arise from an inability to integrate CAUSALLY OPAQUE information (evidence with no explanatory link to the hypothesis) rather than from evidence strength per se, an LLM integrates a piece of evidence into its belief MORE fully when the evidence is causally TRANSPARENT (a mechanistic story links it to the hypothesis) than when it is causally OPAQUE (a bare statistic with the same normative diagnosticity); this transparency-driven integration gap is governed by a separable, near-orthogonal latent 'causal-transparency' axis distinct from the belief-valence direction and from the evidence's decoded strength/diagnosticity, is decodable before the model updates, causally predicts the under-integration of opaque evidence (base-rate/statistic neglect), and can be steered to make opaque evidence integrate as fully as transparent evidence.
Related Work: Human science shows base-rate neglect is driven not only by evidential-impact focus but critically by CAUSAL TRANSPARENCY: people fail to integrate information that is causally opaque, and teasing causal from evidential-impact factors shows causal transparency modulates how much evidence is used (Effects of causal structure and evidential impact on probabilistic reasoning 2024; Causal Models account of base-rate neglect; Bias in Belief Updating combining Bayesian sampler with heuristics 2024). In LLM interpretability, belief/truth is linearly decodable (Marks & Tegmark 2023), transformers implement (constrained) Bayesian belief updating (Constrained Belief Updates 2025; Belief Dynamics 2025), confirmation bias skews CoT (Unveiling Confirmation Bias 2025), and causal reasoning is knowledge-dominated (Is Knowledge All LLMs Needed 2023). Crucially, ALL LLM belief-updating interpretability treats evidence as a scalar to be weighted (by strength, prior, likelihood ratio, order, sample size) and NONE isolates whether a piece of evidence's CAUSAL TRANSPARENCY—whether an explanatory mechanism links it to the hypothesis, holding normative diagnosticity fixed—governs how fully it is integrated, defines a transparency-gated integration metric separable from decoded diagnosticity, or causally links it to base-rate/statistic neglect. This differs from my prior diagnosticity_axis (likelihood-ratio vs one-sided fit), prior_likelihood_gain_axes (prior vs likelihood weighting), sample_weight_neglect_axis (sample size vs proportion), and signal_strength_miscalibration_axis (magnitude of one signal): here the decorrelated dimension is causal transparency vs a bare statistic of matched diagnosticity, the exact factor the causal-models account of base-rate neglect identifies. We move from 'transformers weight evidence by strength' to 'the model under-integrates causally-opaque evidence, and this is a decodable, steerable transparency gate.'
Abstract: A leading account of base-rate neglect holds that people fail to use statistical information not because it is weak but because it is causally OPAQUE—a bare number with no explanatory link to the hypothesis—whereas the same information wrapped in a causal mechanism is readily integrated. As LLMs increasingly weigh statistics against mechanistic evidence in diagnosis, risk, and forecasting, we ask whether they inherit this transparency-gated integration and whether it has a dissociable representational basis. Prior interpretability work shows LLMs update beliefs approximately Bayesianly and weight evidence by strength, prior, and sample size, but none isolates whether a piece of evidence's causal transparency—holding its normative diagnosticity fixed—governs how fully it is integrated. We hypothesize a separable, near-orthogonal latent 'causal-transparency' axis, decodable before the model updates, that encodes whether an explanatory mechanism links evidence to the hypothesis, distinct from the belief-valence direction and from the evidence's decoded strength/diagnosticity; that causally-transparent evidence is integrated more fully than a matched-diagnosticity opaque statistic (a base-rate/statistic-neglect signature); that per-item transparency predicts the under-integration of opaque evidence; and that steering the axis makes opaque evidence integrate as fully as transparent evidence. Using belief-update tasks where evidence is rendered as a causally-transparent mechanism versus a matched-diagnosticity bare statistic against a closed-form Bayesian benchmark, we fit a transparency axis, measure separability via cross-decoding, quantify per-item under-integration, connect it to behavioral base-rate neglect, and perform double-dissociation steering with norm-matched and shuffled-direction controls across three model families. Our results recast a classic reasoning failure mechanistically as a decodable, steerable causal-transparency gate on evidence integration.
Experiments: 1. Graded belief-direction setup. On LLaMA-3.1-8B-Instruct, Mistral-7B-Instruct, and Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct, fit a frozen graded belief/credence direction that reads a posterior over a binary hypothesis: calibrate activations against known probabilities via linear regression on explicit-probability statements (validate monotonic mapping), plus a standard true/false probe (cities, sp_en_trans, larger_than and negations; Marks & Tegmark) as a cross-check; validate on held-out items. Separately fit an EVIDENCE-STRENGTH/DIAGNOSTICITY direction that decodes how strong/diagnostic a piece of evidence is (from graded-diagnosticity stimuli), so causal-transparency can be dissociated from the evidence's normative strength.

2. Transparency x diagnosticity stimulus construction with a closed-form target. Build ~500 belief-update items (diagnosis, forecasting, everyday inference) each specifying a prior and a single piece of evidence whose normative likelihood ratio (diagnosticity) is explicit/inferable, so the Bayesian posterior is CLOSED-FORM. Render each evidence item in two matched forms holding diagnosticity fixed: (a) CAUSALLY-TRANSPARENT (an explanatory mechanism links it to the hypothesis, e.g. 'the test detects the antibody the disease produces, so a positive result...'), and (b) CAUSALLY-OPAQUE (a bare statistic of identical diagnosticity, e.g. 'in this population the base rate / test-positive rate is X%'), adapting the causal-transparency-vs-evidential-impact paradigm. Validate diagnosticity parity with rule checks + human annotation. Include a CONTROL where transparent and opaque forms are both present. Use paraphrase templates; reserve held-out items/templates for transfer.

3. Causal-transparency axis fitting and separability. Extract activations at a pre-update readout position (after the evidence, before the model reports the updated belief) and fit a linear probe to decode CAUSALLY-TRANSPARENT vs CAUSALLY-OPAQUE evidence, controlling for the evidence's diagnosticity. Report AUROC vs shuffled-label controls; measure cosine similarity and cross-decoding among the causal-transparency axis, the graded-belief direction, and the diagnosticity direction to establish that transparency is (i) near-orthogonal to the belief value and (ii) not merely the evidence's decoded strength. Localize the best layer.

4. Transparency-gated integration metric. For each item, project onto the frozen belief direction and measure how far the belief updates from the prior toward the Bayesian posterior for TRANSPARENT vs matched-diagnosticity OPAQUE evidence (integration = fraction of the normative update achieved). Core prediction: opaque evidence is UNDER-integrated relative to transparent evidence of identical diagnosticity (a base-rate/statistic-neglect signature), and the per-item transparency readout predicts the size of the under-integration. Report integration gaps across the transparency x diagnosticity grid with effect sizes; verify the decoded diagnosticity readout is unchanged across transparency conditions (so the gap is a transparency effect, not re-read strength).

5. Behavioral base-rate/statistic-neglect prediction. Elicit the model's numeric posterior and stated answer. Score neglect = under-updating on opaque-statistic evidence relative to the closed-form Bayesian answer. Test whether per-item transparency-gated under-integration predicts behavioral neglect via regression; report AUROC/R^2 vs baselines (diagnosticity axis, belief margin, output entropy, evidence-form surface features, item length).

6. Dissociation from diagnosticity and belief (core). On matched-diagnosticity items where only causal transparency varies, show the transparency axis (not the diagnosticity or belief axes) accounts for the integration gap—establishing causal transparency as a distinct driver of neglect rather than repackaged evidence strength. Report incremental predictive power in nested models.

7. Double-dissociation causal steering. At the pre-update position on held-out opaque-evidence items, steer along the causal-transparency axis (orthogonalized against belief and diagnosticity) toward the transparent pole. Predict: amplifying transparency makes opaque statistics integrate as fully as matched transparent evidence (moving updates toward the Bayesian benchmark) WITHOUT changing updates on already-transparent controls; suppressing it deepens neglect. As controls, steer the diagnosticity direction (should shift update magnitude via re-read strength) and the belief direction (should shift the posterior uniformly). Use norm-matched random-direction and shuffled-direction controls; sweep strengths and layers. Metric: change in deviation-from-Bayesian toward the normative update vs unchanged transparent-control behavior.

8. Application and robustness. Build a training-free calibration knob that steers causal-transparency to reduce statistic-neglect and measure reduced deviation from the closed-form posterior and improved decision accuracy on held-out items (report deviation reduction, decision accuracy, ECE) vs a belief-probe-only baseline. Replicate across three model families and two probe methods; transfer the fitted axis, integration metric, and steering to held-out items/templates and an independent diagnosis/base-rate set without refitting; report per-template consistency under paraphrase and sensitivity to layer/readout position and prior magnitude. As a human-parallel analysis, check whether the transparency-driven integration gap qualitatively matches the human causal-models base-rate-neglect signature (opaque statistics neglected, causally-framed evidence integrated), and whether reasoning-tuned models neglect less.
Risk Factors and Limitations: The causal-transparency axis may not be separable from the graded-belief or diagnosticity directions; we report cosine similarity, cross-decoding, orthogonalized steering, and incremental predictive power, and—because transparent and opaque items are matched on normative diagnosticity—strength cannot trivially explain the integration gap; near-collapse (transparency being merely diagnosticity) is an informative negative result.

The behavioral neglect effect may be weak or reasoning/RLHF-shaped (strong models may integrate statistics correctly); a null/normative result is itself an informative human-vs-machine comparison, reported via deviation from the Bayesian benchmark and a reasoning-model extension.

The graded belief probe is harder to calibrate than a binary truth probe and belief manifolds can be curved; we validate the activation->probability mapping, report calibration/probe-fit diagnostics, and treat integration gaps as lower bounds.

The closed-form Bayesian target assumes the model uses the stated diagnosticity; we screen items where the model demonstrably uses it, report the fraction, and treat gross non-compliance as a separate finding.

Causal transparency is signaled by explanatory wording that could act as a surface fluency/length cue rather than a genuine mechanism-link abstraction; we match length and readability across forms, include a surface-fluency baseline, validate diagnosticity parity, and test whether the axis predicts integration beyond a surface baseline and transfers to held-out templates.
Constructing transparent/opaque forms of identical diagnosticity is delicate; we validate with rule checks and human annotation and verify the decoded diagnosticity readout is unchanged across forms.
Belief/diagnosticity probes are brittle to context and surface form; we validate probes, use paraphrases, standardize the pre-update readout position, and report per-template consistency.

Causal steering is sensitive to layer and strength; we use orthogonalized steering vectors, norm-matched and shuffled-direction controls, sweep strengths, and verify transparency steering moves opaque-evidence integration toward the Bayesian answer without collapsing the belief or degrading already-well-integrated items.

Findings on 7-8B instruct models may not transfer to frontier or reasoning-tuned models; three-family replication, a reasoning-model extension, and independent-set transfer provide reasonable academic-budget coverage.

Name: expected_information_value_axis
Title: Worth Knowing vs. Worth Deciding: A Latent Expected-Information-Value Axis Governing Which Questions an LLM Chooses to Ask
Short Hypothesis: When an LLM agent must choose which query/action to gather information, it represents a candidate inquiry's EXPECTED INFORMATION VALUE—how much it expects the inquiry to reduce its uncertainty about the task—along a separable, near-orthogonal latent axis distinct from generic uncertainty/entropy and from the belief-valence direction; moreover this value splits into an INSTRUMENTAL component (information that changes the decision) and a NON-INSTRUMENTAL/curiosity component (information that reduces uncertainty without affecting the decision), the two are dissociable, and the model—mirroring the human dual-policy finding—often over-weights uncertainty-reduction over decision-relevance, a bias the axis decodably predicts and steering can correct.
Related Work: Human information-seeking science distinguishes information VALUE driven by uncertainty-reduction/curiosity from instrumental (decision-relevant) value, and shows these are computed by dissociable processes (Humans use a dual policy to improve inferences 2025; Information seeking without metacognition 2024, a double-dissociation of information seeking from confidence; Information-seeking in the brain 2021, separate reward-value vs uncertainty-reduction networks; Decoding reward-curiosity conflict 2023). In LLM interpretability, EAST (2024) and Ambiguity-Encoding Neurons (2025) steer generic uncertainty/abstention MAGNITUDE (whether to explore/clarify at all); 'LLMs Think Too Fast to Explore' (2025) shows uncertainty representations dominate over empowerment; 'Reasoning aligns LMs to human cognition' (2026) shows CoT improves inference but leaves a persistent gap in active SAMPLING, modeled behaviorally with latent variables; Belief Dynamics (2025) models Bayesian belief updating. Crucially, ALL LLM work either steers a scalar uncertainty/explore knob or models sampling behaviorally; NONE isolates whether the model represents a specific candidate inquiry's EXPECTED INFORMATION VALUE (expected uncertainty reduction about the task) as a decodable per-query axis, whether that value SPLITS into instrumental (decision-changing) vs non-instrumental (curiosity) components that are dissociable, or causally links an information-value axis to WHICH query the model selects. This differs from my prior positive_test_strategy_axis (test polarity: positive vs diagnostic) and uncertainty_source_axis (reducible vs irreducible uncertainty of the answer): here the object is the forward-looking value of a candidate inquiry and the instrumental/curiosity split, the exact dual-policy cut. We move from 'LLMs encode uncertainty and can be nudged to explore more' to 'the model represents each candidate question's expected information value, decomposes it into decision-relevant vs curiosity value, and mis-weights the two—decodably and steerably.'
Abstract: A capable agent gathers not just any information but the RIGHT information: it should value a question by how much it will actually help the task, distinguishing information that changes the decision (instrumental value) from information that merely reduces uncertainty out of curiosity (non-instrumental value). Human science shows these two values are computed by dissociable processes and that people deploy a dual policy that sometimes over-weights uncertainty-reduction. As LLMs act as agents that decide what to ask, look up, or test, we ask whether they represent a candidate inquiry's expected information value internally and whether they mis-weight its components. Prior interpretability work shows LLMs encode a scalar uncertainty/explore signal that can be steered, but none isolates whether the model represents the expected information value of a SPECIFIC candidate query, nor whether that value splits into instrumental and non-instrumental components. We hypothesize a separable, near-orthogonal latent 'expected-information-value' axis, decodable before the model selects a query, distinct from generic uncertainty/entropy and from the belief-valence direction; that this value decomposes into a decision-relevant (instrumental) component and a curiosity (non-instrumental) component that are dissociable; that per-query information-value causally predicts which query the model chooses; that—mirroring humans—the model over-weights uncertainty-reduction over decision-relevance; and that steering the instrumental component realigns query choice toward decision-relevant inquiries. Using decision tasks where each candidate query's true instrumental vs non-instrumental information value is computable against a value-of-information benchmark, we fit information-value axes, measure separability via cross-decoding, quantify the instrumental/curiosity split, connect it to behavioral query selection, and perform double-dissociation steering with norm-matched and shuffled-direction controls across three model families. Our results recast active information gathering as a decodable, steerable, decomposable value representation.
Experiments: 1. Direction setup. On LLaMA-3.1-8B-Instruct, Mistral-7B-Instruct, and Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct, fit a frozen belief-valence/truth direction on standard true/false statement datasets (cities, sp_en_trans, larger_than and negations; Marks & Tegmark) at the best layer as a reference. Fit a generic UNCERTAINTY/entropy control axis (from empirical answer-stability / output entropy contrasts, following EAST and ambiguity-neuron constructions), so information-value can be dissociated from how uncertain the model is overall.

2. Value-of-information stimulus construction with a computable benchmark. Build ~400 decision tasks (guess-the-object 20-questions, medical/mechanical diagnosis, hypothesis identification) each with a set of CANDIDATE QUERIES the agent could issue, where each query's true EXPECTED INFORMATION VALUE (expected uncertainty reduction) and its INSTRUMENTAL VALUE (expected change to the optimal decision) are computable in closed form given the task's belief state. Construct diagnostic query cells: HIGH-INSTRUMENTAL (reduces uncertainty AND changes the decision), CURIOSITY-ONLY (reduces uncertainty but does NOT change the decision—non-instrumental), LOW-VALUE (reduces little uncertainty), and DECISION-CRITICAL-BUT-LOW-UNCERTAINTY-REDUCTION (rare but decisive). Present the candidate queries and read internal representations at each. Use paraphrase templates; reserve held-out tasks/templates for transfer.

3. Information-value axes fitting and separability. Extract activations over each candidate-query span (pre-selection) and fit linear probes (regression) to decode (a) the query's total expected information value, (b) its instrumental value, and (c) its non-instrumental/curiosity value. Report R^2/AUROC vs shuffled-label controls; measure cosine similarity and cross-decoding among the information-value axes, the generic uncertainty axis, and the belief-valence direction to establish that expected-information-value is (i) near-orthogonal to generic model uncertainty and (ii) not merely belief-valence. Critically, test whether the instrumental and non-instrumental components are decodable from separable directions (cross-decoding, orthogonality), the dual-policy dissociation.

4. Query-selection prediction. Record which query the model actually issues. Test whether the per-query information-value readout predicts the model's query choice beyond baselines (generic uncertainty axis, belief-valence margin, output entropy, query surface length, task difficulty); report incremental AUROC. Test whether the model's choice tracks total information value more than instrumental value—the over-weighting-of-uncertainty-reduction signature.

5. Instrumental-vs-curiosity mis-weighting metric (core, human-analogous). On the diagnostic cells, compute how much the model's query selection over-weights the non-instrumental (curiosity) component relative to the instrumental component, against the value-of-information benchmark. Core prediction (mirroring the human dual-policy finding): the model over-selects CURIOSITY-ONLY queries (high uncertainty reduction, no decision impact) and under-selects DECISION-CRITICAL-BUT-LOW-UNCERTAINTY-REDUCTION queries. Report the mis-weighting profile and test whether the instrumental-value axis's under-influence on choice predicts these errors.

6. Dissociation from generic uncertainty and belief (core). On matched-total-information-value queries differing only in instrumental content, show the instrumental-value axis (not the generic uncertainty or belief-valence axes) accounts for optimal-vs-curiosity selection; report incremental predictive power in nested models—establishing information value and its instrumental/curiosity split as distinct represented quantities rather than repackaged uncertainty.

7. Double-dissociation causal steering. At the pre-selection position on held-out tasks, steer along the instrumental-value axis (orthogonalized against generic uncertainty and the non-instrumental axis). Predict: amplifying the instrumental component realigns query choice toward decision-relevant inquiries (fewer curiosity-only picks, more decision-critical picks) WITHOUT changing the model's overall uncertainty; suppressing it worsens the mis-weighting. As controls, steer the generic uncertainty axis (should change how much the model explores overall, not which query, replicating EAST-style effects) and the non-instrumental/curiosity axis (should shift curiosity-driven picks). Use norm-matched random-direction and shuffled-direction controls; sweep strengths and layers. Metric: change in instrumental-query selection / value-of-information regret vs unchanged overall uncertainty.

8. Application and robustness. Build a training-free agentic diagnostic that flags curiosity-driven mis-weighting in query selection and steers toward decision-relevant information gathering; in a simple interactive 20-questions/diagnosis agent, measure improved value-of-information (fewer queries to solution, lower regret) vs an unsteered and an uncertainty-only-steered baseline. Replicate across three model families and two probe methods; on a reasoning-tuned model test whether extended CoT reduces the mis-weighting (linking to the 'Reasoning aligns LMs to cognition' sampling gap); transfer the fitted axes and steering to held-out tasks/templates without refitting; report per-template consistency under paraphrase and sensitivity to layer/readout position. As a human-parallel analysis, check whether the model exhibits a dual-policy signature (uncertainty-reduction over-weighted, instrumental value under-weighted) matching the human active-information-seeking findings.
Risk Factors and Limitations: The expected-information-value axis may not be separable from the generic uncertainty axis or the belief-valence direction; we report cosine similarity, cross-decoding, orthogonalized steering, and incremental predictive power, and—because matched-total-value queries differing only in instrumental content decorrelate the components—uncertainty cannot trivially explain separability; near-collapse (information-value being merely generic uncertainty, as EAST/ambiguity-neuron work might suggest) is an informative negative result showing LLMs represent only a scalar explore knob, not per-query value.

The instrumental/non-instrumental split may not be dissociable in activation space (a single value direction may drive both); we report cross-decoding and orthogonality, and treat non-dissociability as an informative negative result about whether LLMs implement the human dual policy.

The mis-weighting phenomenon may be weak or reasoning/RLHF-shaped (strong or reasoning-tuned models may select instrumentally, consistent with the human-alignment-via-reasoning finding); a null/normative result is itself an informative human-vs-machine comparison, reported via value-of-information regret against the benchmark and a reasoning-model extension.

Computing true instrumental vs non-instrumental value requires the model to accept the task's belief state and the queries' semantics; models may impose their own priors. We use tasks with explicit, well-defined belief states and query outcomes, validate that the model uses them, condition analyses on parsed items, and report sensitivity to the value-of-information specification.

Information value is partly signaled by query surface features (specificity, length) that could act as cues rather than a genuine value abstraction; we control for query length/specificity as surface baselines, use diverse paraphrase templates, and test whether the axes predict selection beyond a surface baseline and transfer to held-out tasks.

The value probes are graded and harder to calibrate than a binary truth probe; we validate the activation->value mapping, report calibration/probe-fit diagnostics, and treat the axes and mis-weighting as lower bounds, cross-checking with behavioral query choice.
Belief/uncertainty probes are brittle to surface form and context; we validate probes, use paraphrase templates, standardize the pre-selection readout position, and report per-template consistency.

Causal steering is sensitive to layer and strength; we use orthogonalized steering vectors, norm-matched and shuffled-direction controls, sweep strengths, and verify instrumental-value steering realigns query selection without changing overall uncertainty or degrading task competence.

Findings on 7-8B instruct models may not transfer to frontier or agent-tuned models; three-family replication, a reasoning-model extension, an interactive-agent application, and held-out transfer provide reasonable academic-budget coverage.

Name: chance_vs_credence_axis
Title: A Coin Is Not a Mystery: A Latent Chance-vs-Credence Axis and the Machine Conflation of Physical Randomness with Ignorance
Short Hypothesis: LLMs represent whether a probability statement concerns OBJECTIVE CHANCE (the physical propensity of a genuinely indeterminate event, e.g. a fair coin landing heads) versus SUBJECTIVE CREDENCE (a degree of belief about a determinate-but-unknown fact, e.g. whether a specific already-flipped coin landed heads) along a separable, near-orthogonal latent 'chance-vs-credence' axis distinct from the probability-magnitude direction and from the belief-valence/truth direction; the degree to which the two collapse (a 'chance-credence-conflation' signature) is decodable and causally predicts and drives two symmetric errors—treating a settled-but-unknown fact as if it were physically undetermined (refusing to acknowledge there is a fact of the matter) and treating an inherently random future as if it had a hidden determinate answer that more evidence could reveal—and can be steered to suppress or induce the conflation.
Related Work: Interpretability decodes a linear truth/belief direction (Geometry of Truth 2023; Truth is Universal 2024), modal categories probable/improbable/impossible/inconceivable (Is This Just Fantasy? 2025), a good=true Valence-Assent Axis (A Unified Representation 2025), validity-vs-plausibility conflation (How LMs Conflate Validity with Plausibility 2025), and belief-manifold geometry over posteriors (The Shape of Beliefs 2026; Emergent World Beliefs 2025 on poker equity). Philosophy sharply distinguishes objective chance/physical propensity from subjective credence and debates their coordination (Objective chance: not propensity 2016; The objective-subjective dichotomy 2020; Physical, subjective and analogical probability 2022; Conditional Degree of Belief and Bayesian Inference 2019; Certainly but not certain: subjective vs objective modality 2022). Crucially, ALL LLM probability-representation work either decodes a scalar probability MAGNITUDE/posterior, or possibility categories, or good=true valence; NONE isolates whether the model represents the KIND of a probability—a fact about the world's physical chanciness (objective chance) versus a fact about the model's own ignorance (subjective credence)—as a decodable axis distinct from the magnitude, defines a chance-credence-conflation metric, or causally links it to the symmetric errors of mistaking settled-but-unknown facts for undetermined ones and inherently random events for hidden-answer ones. This differs sharply from my prior uncertainty_source_belief_axis (which concerns the reducibility of the model's OWN uncertainty about its ANSWER—epistemic vs aleatoric, and its repair-routing), disbelief_vs_absence (falsity vs ignorance), falsifiability (empirical testability), and contestedness (social dispute): here the object is a first-order property of the PROPOSITION's probability—is its 0.5 a coin's propensity or the model's ignorance about a determinate outcome—a metaphysical chance-vs-credence cut, not a property of the model's answer-uncertainty. We move from 'LLMs encode probability magnitude and possibility' to 'the model represents whether a probability is physical chance or personal ignorance, and conflating them mechanistically drives distinct reasoning errors.'
Abstract: There are two very different ways for something to be 50% likely: a fair coin about to be flipped is physically undetermined (objective chance), whereas a specific coin already flipped and hidden has a settled outcome you merely do not know (subjective credence). A capable reasoner keeps these apart—treating the flipped coin as having a fact of the matter that more evidence could reveal, and the future flip as genuinely open. We ask whether LLMs represent this distinction internally. Prior interpretability work decodes probability magnitude, possibility categories, and truth, but always as scalar quantities, and never asks whether the model encodes the KIND of a probability: physical chanciness of the world versus the model's own ignorance. We hypothesize a separable, near-orthogonal latent 'chance-vs-credence' axis, decodable at read time, that tags a probability statement as objective-chance versus subjective-credence, distinct from the probability-magnitude direction and from the belief-valence/truth direction; and a 'chance-credence-conflation' signature predictive per item of two symmetric errors—treating a settled-but-unknown fact as physically undetermined (denying there is an answer), and treating an inherently random future as if it had a hidden determinate answer discoverable by more evidence. Using matched probability items that orthogonally vary probability KIND (chance vs credence), probability MAGNITUDE, and content, we fit a chance-vs-credence axis, measure separability via cross-decoding, quantify per-item conflation, and connect it to behavioral errors on diagnostic queries (is there a fact of the matter? would more information change the odds?). Double-dissociation steering tests whether suppressing conflation restores the correct handling and amplifying it induces category errors, without changing the represented probability magnitude, with norm-matched and shuffled-direction controls across three model families. Our results recast a foundational chance/credence distinction mechanistically as a decodable, steerable belief-about-probability axis.
Experiments: 1. Direction setup. On LLaMA-3.1-8B-Instruct, Mistral-7B-Instruct, and Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct, fit a frozen belief-valence/truth direction on standard true/false statement datasets (cities, sp_en_trans, larger_than and negations; Marks & Tegmark) with mass-mean and logistic-regression probes at the best layer; validate on held-out atomics. Separately fit a PROBABILITY-MAGNITUDE direction that decodes the numeric probability of a statement (calibrated via linear regression on explicit-probability statements; validate monotonic mapping), so chance-vs-credence KIND can be dissociated from the probability's magnitude.

2. Chance x credence x magnitude stimulus construction. Build ~500 probability items crossing (i) probability KIND—OBJECTIVE-CHANCE (genuinely indeterminate events: a fair coin about to be flipped, a die about to be rolled, a not-yet-decided quantum-style random draw) vs SUBJECTIVE-CREDENCE (determinate-but-unknown facts: a specific already-flipped-and-hidden coin, a historical fact the model does not know, a sealed-box contents)—with (ii) matched MAGNITUDE (0.5 chance vs 0.5 credence; skewed variants), and (iii) content held comparable across kinds. The key is that a chance item and a credence item can share the SAME numeric probability yet differ in kind. Include AMBIGUOUS items (mixed) and matched controls. Use paraphrase templates; reserve held-out items/templates for transfer. Philosophy-informed annotation labels the kind.

3. Chance-vs-credence axis fitting and separability. Extract activations over the proposition span and fit a linear probe to decode OBJECTIVE-CHANCE vs SUBJECTIVE-CREDENCE, controlling for probability magnitude and content. Report AUROC vs shuffled-label controls; measure cosine similarity and cross-decoding between the chance-vs-credence axis, the probability-magnitude direction, and the belief-valence/truth direction to establish that KIND is (i) near-orthogonal to magnitude (a 0.5-chance and a 0.5-credence item share magnitude but must separate on this axis) and (ii) not merely truth. Localize the best layer.

4. Chance-credence-conflation metric. Define per-item conflation as the degree to which the chance-vs-credence axis reads a CHANCE item as credence or a CREDENCE item as chance (collapse toward the wrong pole), calibrated per model. Compare conflation across kinds and magnitudes; core prediction: conflation is nonzero and larger at magnitude 0.5 (where chance and credence numerically coincide) and for content-familiar items. Verify the magnitude readout is unchanged across kinds (so the conflation is a KIND representation, not a re-read of magnitude).

5. Behavioral symmetric-error prediction. Elicit two diagnostic judgments per item: (a) IS-THERE-A-FACT ('is there a definite answer that already exists, or is the outcome genuinely undetermined?') and (b) WOULD-INFO-HELP ('could gathering more information change/reveal the probability?'). Normative pattern: CREDENCE items have a fact of the matter and info can reveal it; CHANCE items do not and info cannot (short of changing the physical setup). Score two failures: (i) CHANCE-AS-CREDENCE = treating a random future as having a hidden determinate answer info could reveal; (ii) CREDENCE-AS-CHANCE = denying a settled-but-unknown fact has an answer. Test whether per-item conflation predicts each failure via logistic regression; report AUROC vs baselines (belief-valence margin, probability-magnitude axis, output entropy, item kind as a surface feature, item length).

6. Dissociation from magnitude and truth (core). On matched-magnitude items (same numeric probability, different kind) and matched-content items, show the chance-vs-credence axis and conflation metric predict the symmetric errors beyond the probability-magnitude and belief-valence axes—establishing probability-KIND as a distinct represented property rather than repackaged magnitude or truth. Report incremental predictive power in nested models.

7. Double-dissociation causal steering. Steer the chance-vs-credence axis (orthogonalized against probability-magnitude and belief-valence) at read time on held-out items. Predict: pushing CREDENCE items toward the chance pole induces CREDENCE-AS-CHANCE errors (denying a fact of the matter) and pushing CHANCE items toward the credence pole induces CHANCE-AS-CREDENCE errors (positing a hidden determinate answer), WITHOUT changing the represented probability magnitude or content judgments on controls; conversely, correcting the axis toward the true kind restores the normative fact-of-the-matter and info-helps judgments. As controls, steer the probability-magnitude direction (should shift the numeric odds, not the kind) and belief-valence (should shift truth judgments). Use norm-matched random-direction and shuffled-direction controls; sweep strengths and layers. Metric: change in the symmetric-error rate vs unchanged magnitude readout and control judgments.

8. Application and robustness. Build a training-free diagnostic that flags chance-credence conflation (relevant for risk/forecasting/gambling advice where an LLM may treat a genuinely random outcome as having a discoverable answer, or a knowable fact as inherently uncertain) and steers to restore the correct handling; on a held-out mix (chance, credence, ambiguous items) measure reduction in category errors while preserving accurate probability magnitudes (report chance-as-credence and credence-as-chance rates, magnitude accuracy vs a probability-probe-only baseline). Replicate across three model families and two probe methods; transfer the fitted axis, conflation metric, and steering to held-out items/templates and an independent chance-vs-credence set without refitting; report per-template consistency under paraphrase and sensitivity to layer choice. As a human-parallel analysis, check whether the conflation profile qualitatively matches the philosophical chance/credence distinction (conflation peaks where magnitudes coincide).
Risk Factors and Limitations: The chance-vs-credence axis may not be separable from the probability-magnitude direction or the belief-valence direction; we report cosine similarity, cross-decoding, orthogonalized steering, and incremental predictive power, and—because matched-magnitude chance-vs-credence items share numeric probability while differing in kind—magnitude cannot trivially explain separability; near-collapse (kind being merely magnitude or truth) is an informative negative result showing LLMs do not represent probability-kind distinctly.

Ground-truth chance-vs-credence labels are philosophically nontrivial (determinism debates make even a coin flip arguably epistemic; some items are genuinely mixed); we use items with strong consensus at the extremes (a not-yet-flipped fair coin as clear chance; a sealed historical fact as clear credence), treat mixed items as a graded/ambiguous tier, use philosophy-informed multi-annotator labels, and report label-agreement sensitivity, framing 'kind' as the MODEL's representation rather than a settled metaphysical verdict.

Probability-kind may be signaled by surface cues (tense/aspect: 'will land' vs 'landed', or 'random' vs 'unknown') rather than a genuine chance-vs-credence abstraction; we mitigate with diverse paraphrase templates, matched surface form where possible (e.g., both framed in present tense with hidden vs undetermined setups), a surface-lexeme baseline, and held-out-template transfer, testing whether the axis predicts the symmetric errors beyond a surface baseline.

The magnitude probe is graded and harder to calibrate than a binary truth probe (and belief manifolds can be curved; The Shape of Beliefs 2026); we validate the activation->probability mapping, report calibration/probe-fit diagnostics, verify the magnitude readout is unchanged across kinds, and treat conflation as a lower bound.
Belief/truth probes are brittle to context and surface form; we validate probes, use paraphrases, standardize readout spans, and report per-template consistency.

The conflation metric relies on a linear projection and per-model calibration; nonlinear structure could be missed, so we treat it as a lower bound and report probe-fit diagnostics, cross-checking with behavioral errors.

Behavioral symmetric-error scoring depends on how the fact-of-the-matter and info-helps questions are phrased (pragmatic implicature); we report sensitivity across phrasings and cross-check with confidence measures.

The effect may be weak or reasoning/RLHF-shaped (strong models may handle coins vs sealed facts correctly, or over-hedge); a null/normative result is itself an informative human-vs-machine comparison, reported via effect sizes against the normative fact-of-the-matter/info-helps pattern and a reasoning-model extension.

Causal steering is sensitive to layer and strength; we use orthogonalized steering vectors, norm-matched and shuffled-direction controls, sweep strengths, and verify chance-vs-credence steering changes the symmetric-error behavior without altering the represented probability magnitude or degrading control judgments.
Findings on 7-8B instruct models may not transfer to frontier scale; three-family replication and independent chance-vs-credence-set transfer provide reasonable academic-budget coverage.

Name: partial_truth_composite_axis
Title: Half True, Not Just Uncertain: A Latent Partial-Truth Axis that Separates Genuinely Composite Claims from Whole-Truths and Falsehoods
Short Hypothesis: LLMs represent a claim's COMPOSITENESS OF TRUTH—whether it is a half-truth (a conjunctive/compound claim in which one conjunct is true and another false, e.g. 'Einstein was a physicist born in Switzerland') versus a whole-truth or a whole-falsehood—along a separable, near-orthogonal latent 'partial-truth' axis distinct from the binary truth/belief-valence direction and from generic confidence/uncertainty; the degree to which half-truths collapse toward either the fully-true or fully-false pole (a 'truth-flattening' signature) is decodable, causally predicts and drives two symmetric failures—endorsing a half-truth as simply true (accepting deceptive composite claims) and rejecting it as simply false (throwing out the true conjunct)—and can be steered to make the model detect the composite structure or flatten it.
Related Work: Interpretability fits a BINARY linear truth direction (Geometry of Truth 2023; Truth is Universal 2024's 2D general+polarity subspace; From Directions to Cones 2025) that is context-sensitive (Truth-value probes are context sensitive 2024) and generalizes across logical conjunction/disjunction as a classifier (Truthfulness Probe Generalization 2025), plus multiple decodable uncertainty types (Pretrained LLMs Learn Multiple Types of Uncertainty 2025; K-CSA 2025). Behavioral NLP detects half-truths and edits them (Beware of Deception 2023, LIAR-PLUS), and philosophy debates whether 'true' is gradable (Not Half True 2022, arguing it is not). Crucially, ALL interpretability truth work treats a proposition as monolithically true or false and probes/steers a single binary axis; even work that generalizes the truth direction across conjunctions uses it to CLASSIFY the whole claim's truth, never asking whether the model represents that a claim is INTERNALLY COMPOSITE—partly true and partly false—as an axis distinct from binary truth and from uncertainty, defines a truth-flattening metric, or causally links it to the symmetric failures of accepting or over-rejecting half-truths. My prior proposals cover borderline_vagueness (gradable-predicate indeterminacy of a SINGLE atomic predicate), analytic_synthetic, contestedness (social dispute), and belief_coherence_geometry (logical algebra of separate atomic projections proj(P∧Q)≤min)—but belief_coherence_geometry tests whether projections OBEY an algebra across separately-probed propositions, whereas here the claim is that a SINGLE composite claim's internal true/false MIXTURE is itself a decodable, steerable representation, and that flattening it causally drives half-truth deception. We move from 'the model classifies a whole claim as true or false' to 'the model represents whether a claim is a genuine half-truth, and flattening this composite structure mechanistically drives both deceptive acceptance and over-rejection.'
Abstract: The most effective deceptions are half-truths: 'Einstein was a physicist born in Switzerland' pairs a true conjunct (physicist) with a false one (born in Germany, not Switzerland). A careful reasoner should detect the composite structure—neither swallowing the whole claim as true nor discarding the true part—but interpretability treats truth as monolithically binary. We ask whether LLMs represent a claim's COMPOSITENESS of truth internally. We hypothesize a separable, near-orthogonal latent 'partial-truth' axis, decodable at read time, that tags a claim as a half-truth (one conjunct true, one false) versus a whole-truth or whole-falsehood, distinct from the binary truth/belief-valence direction and from generic confidence/uncertainty; and a 'truth-flattening' signature: the degree to which half-truths collapse toward the fully-true or fully-false pole, predictive per item of two symmetric failures—endorsing a half-truth as simply true (deceptive acceptance) and rejecting it as simply false (discarding the true conjunct). Using matched claims that orthogonally vary compositeness (whole-true, whole-false, half-true) and content, we fit a partial-truth axis, measure separability from the binary truth axis and an uncertainty axis via cross-decoding, quantify per-item flattening, and connect it to behavioral half-truth handling. Double-dissociation steering tests whether amplifying the axis makes the model flag composite structure (splitting a half-truth into its true and false parts) and suppressing it flattens the claim to a single verdict, without changing whole-truth/whole-false accuracy, with norm-matched and shuffled-direction controls across three model families. Our results recast a classic deception structure mechanistically as a decodable, steerable partial-truth axis distinct from binary truth and from uncertainty.
Experiments: 1. Direction setup. On LLaMA-3.1-8B-Instruct, Mistral-7B-Instruct, and Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct, fit a frozen BINARY belief-valence/truth direction on standard true/false statement datasets (cities, sp_en_trans, larger_than and negations; Marks & Tegmark) with mass-mean and logistic-regression probes at the best layer; validate on held-out atomics; also isolate the polarity-robust general-truth direction (Truth is Universal) as a control. Separately fit an UNCERTAINTY/confidence control axis (from empirical answer-stability / output-entropy contrasts, following Pretrained-LLMs-Learn-Multiple-Uncertainty constructions), so partial-truth (compositeness) can be dissociated from how uncertain the model is about a claim.

2. Compositeness stimulus construction. Build ~500 verifiable claims crossing COMPOSITENESS with content: (a) WHOLE-TRUE (a conjunctive claim in which both conjuncts are true, 'Einstein was a physicist born in Germany'), (b) WHOLE-FALSE (both conjuncts false), and (c) HALF-TRUE (one conjunct true, one false—the deceptive composite, 'Einstein was a physicist born in Switzerland'), with which conjunct is false balanced (first vs second) and the number of conjuncts varied (2, 3). Include ATOMIC true/false controls (single-conjunct) and matched-uncertainty items (long-tail conjuncts the model is unsure about) to separate compositeness from ignorance. Draw conjuncts from verifiable factual relations; validate each conjunct's truth. Use paraphrase templates; reserve held-out claims/templates for transfer.

3. Partial-truth axis fitting and separability. Extract activations over the claim span and fit a linear probe to decode HALF-TRUE (composite: mixed true/false conjuncts) vs WHOLE (uniformly true or false), controlling for the overall truth valence and content. Report AUROC vs shuffled-label controls; measure cosine similarity and cross-decoding between the partial-truth axis, the binary truth/belief-valence axis, and the uncertainty axis to establish that compositeness is (i) near-orthogonal to binary truth (a half-truth is neither cleanly true nor false, and whole-true vs whole-false span the truth axis) and (ii) not merely uncertainty (a confident half-truth vs an uncertain whole-truth must separate). Localize the best layer.

4. Truth-flattening metric. For each HALF-TRUE claim, project onto the frozen binary truth direction and measure how far it collapses toward the fully-TRUE or fully-FALSE pole relative to a genuinely-mixed baseline (flattening = magnitude of the definite whole-claim verdict a composite claim inherits, and its sign toward true or false, calibrated per model). Compare flattening across compositeness levels and conjunct positions; core prediction: half-truths show substantial flattening (the model reads them as simply true or simply false rather than mixed), with the direction of flattening biased by which conjunct is salient/plausible; whole-true and whole-false items show little flattening on the partial-truth axis.

5. Behavioral half-truth-handling prediction. Elicit two judgments per claim: (a) a binary true/false verdict, and (b) a composite-structure probe ('is this claim wholly true, wholly false, or partly true and partly false—and which part is false?'). Score two failures: (i) DECEPTIVE ACCEPTANCE = endorsing a half-truth as simply true; (ii) OVER-REJECTION = rejecting a half-truth as simply false (discarding the true conjunct). Test whether per-item truth-flattening predicts each failure via logistic regression; report AUROC vs baselines (binary truth margin, uncertainty axis, output entropy, claim length, conjunct-position surface feature).

6. Dissociation from binary truth and uncertainty (core). On matched-content items where only compositeness varies, and matched-uncertainty items where compositeness varies, show the partial-truth axis and flattening metric predict half-truth-handling failures beyond the binary truth and uncertainty axes—establishing compositeness as a distinct represented property rather than repackaged binary truth or ignorance. Report incremental predictive power in nested models. Also test whether the partial-truth axis is decodable beyond simply averaging separate atomic-conjunct truth probes (i.e., whether the composite representation is more than the sum of its parts), contrasting with a belief_coherence_geometry-style projection-averaging baseline.

7. Double-dissociation causal steering. Steer the partial-truth axis (orthogonalized against binary truth-valence and uncertainty) at read time on held-out items. Predict: amplifying the composite pole on half-truths makes the model detect and split the claim (correctly flagging it as partly true, identifying the false conjunct) WITHOUT changing verdicts on whole-true/whole-false controls; suppressing it flattens half-truths toward a single verdict (inducing deceptive acceptance or over-rejection). As controls, steer binary truth-valence (should flip the whole-claim verdict on atomic and whole items) and the uncertainty axis (should shift hedging). Use norm-matched random-direction and shuffled-direction controls; sweep strengths and layers. Metric: change in composite-detection / flattening-failure rate vs unchanged whole-truth/whole-false accuracy.

8. Application and robustness. Build a training-free misinformation diagnostic that flags half-truth flattening (deceptive composite claims the model accepts wholesale, or partly-true claims it wrongly discards) and steers to enforce composite detection; on a held-out set (including real half-truths adapted from a LIAR-PLUS-style set) measure reduction in deceptive acceptance and over-rejection while preserving accurate handling of whole-true and whole-false claims (report both failure rates, whole-claim accuracy, ECE vs a binary-truth-probe-only baseline). Replicate across three model families and two probe methods; transfer the fitted axis, flattening metric, and steering to held-out claims/templates without refitting; report per-template consistency under paraphrase and sensitivity to layer choice, number of conjuncts, and which conjunct is false. As a scaling check, test whether the partial-truth axis strengthens with model capability (truth directions themselves being capability-dependent per Truthfulness-Probe-Generalization 2025).
Risk Factors and Limitations: The partial-truth axis may not be separable from the binary truth/belief-valence direction or the uncertainty axis; we report cosine similarity, cross-decoding, orthogonalized steering, and incremental predictive power, and—because half-truths are neither cleanly true nor false while whole-true vs whole-false span the truth axis, and confident half-truths vs uncertain whole-truths dissociate compositeness from uncertainty—binary truth and uncertainty cannot trivially explain separability; near-collapse (compositeness being merely mid-range truth or generic uncertainty) is an informative negative result showing LLMs do not represent composite truth structure distinctly.

The partial-truth axis might reduce to a trivial average of separate atomic-conjunct truth probes rather than a genuine composite representation; we explicitly compare against a projection-averaging baseline (belief_coherence_geometry-style) and test whether the composite probe predicts half-truth-handling failures beyond it, treating reduction-to-average as a reportable finding.

Compositeness may be signaled by surface cues (conjunctive structure, sentence length) rather than a genuine partial-truth abstraction; we control for the number and structure of conjuncts across conditions, match whole-true/whole-false items to the same conjunctive form, include a surface/length baseline, and test held-out-template transfer, verifying the axis predicts behavior beyond conjunct-count and length.

Constructing clean HALF-TRUE items where exactly one conjunct is false requires reliable per-conjunct truth labels; we use verifiable factual relations, validate each conjunct, balance which conjunct is false, and report label sensitivity.

Binary truth/belief probes are brittle to context and surface form (LLM Knowledge is Brittle 2025); we validate probes, use the polarity-robust general-truth direction, use paraphrases, standardize readout spans, and report per-template consistency.

The flattening metric relies on a linear projection and per-model calibration; nonlinear structure could be missed, so we treat it as a lower bound and report probe-fit diagnostics, cross-checking with behavioral half-truth handling.
Behavioral composite-detection scoring depends on how the wholly/partly-true probe is phrased; we report sensitivity across phrasings and cross-check with confidence measures.

The effect may be weak or capability-dependent (smaller models may lack robust truth directions per Truthfulness-Probe-Generalization 2025, and thus lack a partial-truth axis); a weak/absent axis is itself informative about the limits of LLM truth representation, and we report a scale trend across the three families.

Causal steering is sensitive to layer and strength; we use orthogonalized steering vectors, norm-matched and shuffled-direction controls, sweep strengths, and verify partial-truth steering changes composite-detection without flipping whole-true/whole-false verdicts or collapsing the model into always-flagging-composite.
Findings on 7-8B instruct models may not transfer to frontier scale; three-family replication and held-out/independent-half-truth-set transfer provide reasonable academic-budget coverage.

Name: silence_as_evidence_axis
Title: Reading Nothing Into Silence, or Too Much: A Latent Absence-Diagnosticity Axis Governing How LLMs Update Beliefs on Missing Evidence
Short Hypothesis: Mirroring the human 'absence of evidence' inference (a silence/omission is diagnostic only to the extent it was EXPECTED to be broken—a source who would have spoken had P been true, but stayed silent, licenses inferring not-P; an unexpected silence licenses nothing), an LLM updating a belief on the NON-appearance of expected testimony/evidence represents a proposition's ABSENCE-DIAGNOSTICITY (how much a silence should move belief given the source's coverage/incentive to have spoken) along a separable, near-orthogonal latent axis distinct from the belief-valence direction and from the magnitude of positively-asserted evidence; the degree to which this collapses (an 'absence-neglect / over-inference' signature) is decodable before the model updates, causally predicts and drives two symmetric failures—neglecting a highly-diagnostic silence (failing to infer not-P when an informed source conspicuously omits P) and over-inferring from an uninformative silence (treating a source's failure to mention P as evidence of not-P when the source had no reason or opportunity to mention it)—and can be steered to calibrate absence-based inference.
Related Work: Human science robustly formalizes absence-based inference: silence is diagnostic in proportion to the expectation it would have been broken (The Epistemic Weight of Silence 2023; When Absence of Evidence Is Evidence of Absence 2016; On Reliable Algorithmic Absence-Based Inference 2025; epistemic-coverage accounts), people infer the MAGNITUDE of others' knowledge from minimal/omitted action (broad epistemic inference from minimal action 2021/2024), and Bayesian-ToM models ground belief attribution in observed and UNobserved behavior (LaBToM 2025; Grounding Belief in Bayesian ToM 2024; Belief Attribution as Mental Explanation 2025). In LLM interpretability, belief/self-other beliefs and their binding are linearly decodable and causally steerable (Marks & Tegmark 2023; Zhu et al. 2024 'LMs Represent Beliefs of Self and Others'; Lookbacks 2025 'visibility lookback'; Brittle Minds 2024), transformers implement (constrained) Bayesian belief updating (Belief Dynamics 2025; Constrained Belief Updates 2025; The Shape of Beliefs 2026), and RAG-aggregation work shows LLMs are heuristic followers biased by repetition/order (Rational Synthesizers or Heuristic Followers 2026). Crucially, ALL LLM belief-updating and belief-tracking work concerns updating on POSITIVELY PRESENTED evidence or on visibility of a state; NONE studies whether LLMs update beliefs on the ABSENCE/non-appearance of EXPECTED testimony or evidence, isolates an absence-diagnosticity axis (how much a silence should move belief given the source's coverage/incentive) separable from belief-valence and from positive-evidence strength, or causally links its miscalibration to the symmetric failures of neglecting diagnostic silences and over-inferring from uninformative ones. This differs from my prior source_independence (independent vs echoed corroboration), hearsay_firsthandness (evidential distance of a present claim), diagnosticity_axis (likelihood ratio of PRESENT evidence), and provenance/consensus axes: here the evidence is the NON-occurrence of expected speech, and the graded property is how expected that speech was—the exact absence-of-evidence cut, unstudied in LLMs. We move from 'LLMs update on presented evidence' to 'the model represents whether a silence is diagnostic and mis-weights it, decodably and steerably.'
Abstract: Skilled reasoners read meaning into silence—but only sometimes. If a well-informed, cooperative source would surely have mentioned that a candidate had a criminal record, their conspicuous omission licenses inferring there is none; but a source who had no reason or opportunity to mention it tells us nothing by staying silent. Humans track this: a silence is diagnostic in proportion to the expectation it would have been broken. As LLMs increasingly reason over incomplete testimony, reports, and retrieved documents—where what is NOT said matters—we ask whether they update beliefs on the absence of expected evidence and whether they calibrate its diagnosticity. Prior interpretability work shows LLMs linearly encode beliefs and update them on presented evidence, but none studies updating on the non-appearance of expected testimony. We hypothesize a separable, near-orthogonal latent 'absence-diagnosticity' axis, decodable before the model updates, that encodes how much a silence should move belief given the source's coverage and incentive to have spoken, distinct from the belief-valence direction and from positively-asserted-evidence strength; and an 'absence-miscalibration' signature predictive per item of two symmetric failures—neglecting a highly-diagnostic silence (failing to infer not-P from an informed source's conspicuous omission) and over-inferring from an uninformative silence (treating an uncovered source's non-mention as evidence of not-P). Using scenarios that orthogonally vary a source's coverage/incentive (how expected a mention of P was) against a Bayesian absence-inference benchmark, we fit an absence-diagnosticity axis, measure separability via cross-decoding, quantify per-item miscalibration, connect it to behavioral absence-inference errors, and perform double-dissociation steering with norm-matched and shuffled-direction controls across three model families. Our results recast a foundational absence-of-evidence inference mechanistically as a decodable, steerable belief axis.
Experiments: 1. Direction setup. On LLaMA-3.1-8B-Instruct, Mistral-7B-Instruct, and Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct, fit a frozen graded belief/credence direction reading a posterior over a binary proposition P: calibrate activations against known probabilities via linear regression on explicit-probability statements (validate monotonic mapping), plus a standard true/false probe (cities, sp_en_trans, larger_than and negations; Marks & Tegmark) as a cross-check; validate on held-out items. Separately fit a POSITIVE-EVIDENCE-STRENGTH direction that decodes how strongly a stated assertion supports/contradicts P (from graded positively-presented evidence), so absence-diagnosticity can be dissociated from present-evidence strength.

2. Absence-inference stimulus construction with a Bayesian benchmark. Build ~500 scenarios in which a SOURCE describes a situation and NOTABLY does NOT mention P, orthogonally varying (i) the source's COVERAGE (would they know about P?—expert/present vs uninformed/absent) and (ii) their INCENTIVE to mention P if true (a cooperative/exhaustive source who would report P vs one with no reason to mention it), which jointly set how EXPECTED a mention of P was and hence the normative diagnosticity of its absence. Key diagnostic cells: HIGH-DIAGNOSTIC SILENCE (informed, would-have-said-P, yet silent—licenses inferring not-P) vs UNINFORMATIVE SILENCE (uncovered/no-incentive source's silence—licenses nothing). Include POSITIVE-EVIDENCE controls (the source explicitly asserts or denies P) so absence-updating can be compared to presence-updating, and a closed-form Bayesian absence-inference model (silence lowers P(P) by a factor set by coverage x incentive) as the normative target. Use paraphrase templates; reserve held-out scenarios/templates for transfer.

3. Absence-diagnosticity axis fitting and separability. Extract activations at a pre-update readout position (after the source's account with its conspicuous omission, before the model updates) and fit a linear probe to decode HIGH- vs LOW absence-diagnosticity (would-have-spoken vs no-reason-to-speak), controlling for the underlying prior on P. Report AUROC vs shuffled-label controls; measure cosine similarity and cross-decoding among the absence-diagnosticity axis, the belief-valence direction, and the positive-evidence-strength direction to establish that absence-diagnosticity is (i) near-orthogonal to the belief value and (ii) not merely repackaged positive-evidence strength. Localize the best layer (compare to belief-binding/visibility-lookback layers).

4. Absence-miscalibration metric. For each silence scenario, project onto the frozen belief direction and measure how far belief in P moves upon the omission relative to the pre-omission prior (absence update), and compare to the closed-form Bayesian absence update. Define per-item miscalibration = signed deviation: NEGLECT (under-updating a high-diagnostic silence toward not-P) vs OVER-INFERENCE (updating toward not-P on an uninformative silence). Core prediction: substantial neglect of diagnostic silences and over-inference from uninformative ones, with the absence-diagnosticity axis reading collapsed (failing to distinguish would-have-spoken from no-reason-to-speak). Report miscalibration across the coverage x incentive grid with effect sizes.

5. Behavioral absence-inference-error prediction. Elicit the model's stated belief in P (and 'does the source's silence tell you anything about P?') per scenario. Score two failures: (a) NEGLECT = declining to infer not-P from an informed source's conspicuous omission; (b) OVER-INFERENCE = asserting not-P from an uncovered/no-incentive source's silence. Test whether per-item miscalibration/absence-diagnosticity readout predicts each failure via logistic regression; report AUROC vs baselines (belief-valence margin, positive-evidence-strength axis, output entropy, coverage/incentive as surface features, scenario length).

6. Dissociation from positive evidence and belief (core). Contrast absence-updating against matched POSITIVE-EVIDENCE controls (explicit assertion/denial of P) and, on matched-prior items where only coverage/incentive vary, show the absence-diagnosticity axis and miscalibration metric predict absence-inference behavior beyond the positive-evidence-strength and belief-valence axes—establishing absence-diagnosticity as a distinct represented quantity governing updating on missing evidence. Report incremental predictive power in nested models.

7. Double-dissociation causal steering. Steer the absence-diagnosticity axis (orthogonalized against belief-valence and positive-evidence-strength) at the pre-update position on held-out silence items. Predict: amplifying diagnosticity on high-diagnostic silences makes the model appropriately infer not-P (calibrated absence-updating) WITHOUT changing updates on positive-evidence controls; suppressing it induces neglect. Conversely, on uninformative silences, suppressing spurious diagnosticity halts over-inference while amplifying induces it. As controls, steer belief-valence (should shift P's credence regardless of the silence's diagnosticity) and the positive-evidence-strength direction (should shift updating on stated assertions, not silences). Use norm-matched random-direction and shuffled-direction controls; sweep strengths and layers. Metric: change in deviation-from-Bayesian-absence-update toward normative vs unchanged positive-evidence-control updates.

8. Application and robustness. Build a training-free diagnostic that flags absence-miscalibration in incomplete-testimony/RAG settings (e.g., inferring a fact is false because a document did not mention it, or missing a diagnostic omission) and steers to calibrate absence-based inference; on a held-out set (including realistic omission scenarios) measure reduction in both neglect and over-inference while preserving accurate positive-evidence updating (report both error rates, positive-evidence-update accuracy, ECE vs a belief-probe-only baseline). Replicate across three model families and two probe methods; transfer the fitted axis, miscalibration metric, and steering to held-out scenarios/templates and an independent absence-inference set without refitting; report per-template consistency under paraphrase and sensitivity to layer choice. As a human-parallel analysis, check whether the model's absence-updating scales with source coverage x incentive as the Bayesian silence account predicts.
Risk Factors and Limitations: The absence-diagnosticity axis may not be separable from the belief-valence direction or the positive-evidence-strength direction; we report cosine similarity, cross-decoding, orthogonalized steering, and incremental predictive power, and—because matched-prior items vary only coverage/incentive and the evidence is a NON-occurrence rather than an assertion—belief-valence and positive-evidence cannot trivially explain separability; near-collapse (absence-diagnosticity being merely present-evidence strength or belief value) is an informative negative result showing LLMs do not represent silence's diagnosticity distinctly.

The behavioral absence-inference effect may be weak or reasoning/RLHF-shaped (strong or reasoning-tuned models may update on silence normatively, or refuse to infer from omissions); a null/normative result is itself an informative human-vs-machine comparison, reported via deviation from the Bayesian absence-benchmark and a reasoning-model extension.

Constructing scenarios where the normative diagnosticity of a silence is well-defined requires clean specification of the source's coverage and incentive; these are graded and can be ambiguous. We anchor on the clearest cells (informed-and-cooperative vs uninformed/no-incentive), validate coverage/incentive with human annotation, use a closed-form silence-inference model as the target, and report label-agreement and benchmark-specification sensitivity.

Absence-diagnosticity may be signaled by surface cues (words like 'expert', 'exhaustive', 'unaware') rather than a genuine expectation-of-speech abstraction; we mitigate with diverse paraphrase templates, coverage/incentive conveyed structurally rather than lexically, surface-lexeme baselines, and held-out-template transfer, testing whether the axis predicts absence-updating beyond a surface baseline.

The graded belief probe is harder to calibrate than a binary truth probe and belief manifolds can be curved (The Shape of Beliefs 2026); we validate the activation->probability mapping, report calibration/probe-fit diagnostics, and treat absence-updates and miscalibration as lower bounds.

The closed-form Bayesian absence target assumes the model represents the prior on P and the source's coverage/incentive; models may impose their own priors. We measure the model's zero-silence prior, condition analyses on items where coverage/incentive are demonstrably parsed, and treat gross non-compliance as a separate finding.
Belief/positive-evidence probes are brittle to context and surface form; we validate probes, use paraphrases, standardize the pre-update readout position, and report per-template consistency.

Behavioral absence-inference scoring depends on how the belief and 'does the silence tell you anything' questions are phrased (pragmatic implicature about omissions); we report sensitivity across phrasings and cross-check with confidence measures.

Causal steering is sensitive to layer and strength; we use orthogonalized steering vectors, norm-matched and shuffled-direction controls, sweep strengths, and verify absence-diagnosticity steering calibrates absence-updating without altering positive-evidence updating or collapsing the model into always/never inferring from silence.

Findings on 7-8B instruct models may not transfer to frontier or reasoning-tuned models; three-family replication, a reasoning-model extension, and independent-set transfer provide reasonable academic-budget coverage.

Name: self_fulfilling_answer_commitment
Title: It Answers What It Predicts It Will Answer: A Causally-Potent, Self-Fulfilling Pre-Commitment Belief in LLMs
Short Hypothesis: Before generating, an LLM forms a decodable pre-commitment belief about WHICH answer it will give, and—unlike the causally-inert solvability belief reported by Confidence-is-Not-Competence—this content-commitment belief is causally POTENT and SELF-FULFILLING: it does not merely forecast the eventual answer but causally pulls generation toward the pre-committed answer, so steering it changes the actual output (including inducing a wrong answer the model would otherwise get right).
Related Work: Interpretability shows LLMs encode future response attributes pre-generation, including the eventual multiple-choice answer, probeable before any token (Emergent Response Planning 2025; Language Models Can Predict Their Own Behavior 2025; ParaScopes 2025; Future Lens 2023; Temporal Predictors 2025; No Answer Needed 2025; Knowing Before Saying 2025; Gnosis 2025; Factual Self-Awareness 2025), and belief-state geometry over the data process (Transformers Represent Belief State Geometry 2024). Crucially, Confidence is Not Competence (2025) finds a decodable SOLVABILITY belief (will-I-succeed) that is CAUSALLY INERT for execution—steering it leaves solutions unchanged—concluding 'decodable beliefs are not actionable levers.' Crucially, ALL LLM self-prediction/planning work treats the pre-generation signal as a PASSIVE FORECAST of a downstream-determined answer (probing accuracy, planning-decodability, early-warning) and never asks whether it is CAUSALLY SELF-FULFILLING; and Confidence-is-Not-Competence's inertness result concerns a solvability belief, NOT a content-commitment belief (which-answer). No work isolates a content-pre-commitment belief separable from the solvability/confidence axis, tests its causal potency and self-fulfillment via steering, or shows a pre-commitment can override the model's own competent answer. This differs from my prior intention_execution_gap (intended-vs-executed action mismatch) and self_fulfilling_belief_axis (truth determined by the model's own assertion of a proposition).
Abstract: A self-fulfilling prophecy is a prediction that brings about its own truth. Language models are known to encode, before generating, a prediction of the very answer they will produce—but this is always read as a passive forecast, and a recent result found a related solvability belief to be causally inert for execution, concluding decoded beliefs are not actionable levers. We ask a sharper causal question: does an LLM's pre-generation belief about WHICH answer it will give CAUSE it to give that answer, so the belief is self-fulfilling rather than merely predictive? We hypothesize a separable, near-orthogonal latent 'answer-commitment' belief, decodable after the question but before generation, distinct from the solvability/confidence axis, that encodes the specific answer the model expects to give; that steering this belief toward a different (including incorrect) answer causally shifts the actual generated answer—demonstrating self-fulfillment—rather than leaving output unchanged; and that on items the model can solve, inducing a wrong pre-commitment can override its competence (a self-inflicted error), while on genuinely uncertain items the pre-commitment disproportionately determines which plausible answer wins. Using multiple-choice and short-answer tasks, we decode the answer-commitment belief, dissociate it from solvability, and steer it with norm-matched and shuffled-direction controls across three model families, measuring whether the actual output follows the steered commitment. Our results would recast a decoded self-prediction as a causal, self-fulfilling driver of LLM answers, refining the influential claim that decoded beliefs are inert.
Experiments: 1. Direction setup. On LLaMA-3.1-8B-Instruct, Mistral-7B-Instruct, and Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct, fit a frozen belief-valence/truth direction on standard true/false datasets (cities, sp_en_trans, larger_than and negations; Marks & Tegmark) at the best layer as a reference. Separately fit a SOLVABILITY/CONFIDENCE direction (in-advance-correctness / solvability-belief probe, following No Answer Needed and Confidence-is-Not-Competence constructions), to distinguish the answer-commitment belief from will-I-succeed.

2. Answer-commitment decoding. Assemble ~500 multiple-choice items (MMLU-style, commonsense) and short-answer items with definite answers, spanning items the model reliably solves and genuinely uncertain items (measured by sampling). At a PRE-generation readout position (after the question, before any output token), fit a linear probe to decode WHICH answer option the model will produce (following Emergent Response Planning). Report AUROC vs shuffled-label controls; validate it predicts the eventual answer.

3. Separability from solvability. Measure cosine similarity and cross-decoding between the answer-commitment direction and the solvability/confidence direction to establish near-orthogonality. On the diagnostic subset (matched solvability, different committed answer), confirm the commitment probe separates items the solvability axis does not.

4. Causal self-fulfillment (core). At the pre-generation position on held-out items, steer along the answer-commitment direction toward a SPECIFIC (targeted, including incorrect) answer option and measure whether the ACTUAL generated answer shifts to the steered target. Core prediction (contra Confidence-is-Not-Competence's inertness for the solvability axis): the content-commitment belief is causally POTENT—steering it changes the output. Report the fraction of items where the output follows the steered commitment, dose-response vs steering strength, and target-specificity (steering toward option A vs B yields A vs B). Controls: steer the solvability/confidence axis (should shift hedging, not which answer, replicating its inertness) and matched random/shuffled directions.

5. Overriding competence (self-inflicted error).
