On items the model reliably SOLVES, steer the pre-commitment toward a wrong option and measure the induced error rate while verifying steering-free accuracy is retained; contrast with genuinely UNCERTAIN items, where the pre-commitment should disproportionately determine which plausible answer wins. Report the competence-override rate vs unsteered baseline.

6. Forecast-vs-cause dissociation. Establish self-fulfillment (not passive forecasting) by showing that EARLY perturbation of the commitment belief (before the answer is determined) changes the outcome, distinguishing 'the belief predicts a downstream-determined answer' from 'the belief causes the answer.' Report incremental causal effect over the solvability axis in nested analyses.

7. Application and robustness. Build a training-free diagnostic that flags items where a mis-formed pre-commitment will self-fulfill a wrong answer (a hallucination/robustness vector), and test whether re-steering the commitment toward the correct answer rescues accuracy. Replicate across three model families and two probe methods; transfer the fitted commitment direction and steering to held-out items/templates without refitting; report per-template consistency under paraphrase, sensitivity to layer/readout position, whether self-fulfillment is stronger on uncertain than confident items, and (as a reasoning-model extension) whether the pre-commitment biases the eventual answer across long chains of thought.
Risk Factors and Limitations: The answer-commitment direction may not be separable from the solvability/confidence direction; we report cosine similarity, cross-decoding, and incremental causal effect, and—because the diagnostic subset matches solvability while varying the committed answer—solvability cannot trivially explain it; near-collapse is an informative negative result.

The central risk is that the pre-commitment is a passive forecast, not a cause (as Confidence-is-Not-Competence found for the solvability axis); if steering the commitment leaves the output unchanged, that reinforces the inertness view—an informative negative result. We mitigate the forecast-vs-cause confound with early perturbation (before the answer is determined), dose-response, and target-specificity (steering to A vs B).

A subtle confound is that steering the commitment direction could work merely by injecting the target answer token's embedding rather than a genuine belief; we control by orthogonalizing the commitment direction against the raw token/unembedding directions of the options and by requiring target-specificity to hold for semantically-equivalent paraphrased options.

Steering could degrade fluency or globally corrupt output rather than selectively redirect the answer; we use norm-matched and shuffled-direction controls, sweep strengths, verify off-target coherence, and require target-specific answer changes.
The competence-override result could reflect generic disruption; the target-specificity and preserved-accuracy-on-control-items checks guard against this.
The answer-commitment probe (predicting a discrete answer) is easier for multiple-choice than open-ended items; we focus MC for the clean causal test and report open-ended results as secondary.
Belief/commitment probes are brittle to surface form; we validate probes, use paraphrase templates, standardize the pre-generation readout position, and report per-template consistency.

Findings on 7-8B instruct models may not transfer to frontier or reasoning-tuned models; three-family replication, a reasoning-model extension, and held-out transfer provide reasonable academic-budget coverage.

Name: dilution_effect_irrelevance_gating
Title: Diluted by the Irrelevant: A Latent Irrelevance-Recognition Gate that Fails to Filter Non-Diagnostic Evidence in LLM Belief Updating
Short Hypothesis: Mirroring the human dilution effect (adding non-diagnostic, irrelevant information WEAKENS the pull of genuinely diagnostic evidence, dragging judgments toward the middle), an LLM's belief update is diluted when diagnostic evidence is padded with irrelevant filler of zero normative diagnosticity; this dilution is governed by a separable, near-orthogonal latent 'irrelevance-recognition' gate—distinct from the belief-valence direction and from the decoded strength of the diagnostic evidence—that SHOULD filter out non-diagnostic content but instead lets it blunt the update; the gate's per-item failure is decodable before the model updates, causally predicts the size of the dilution, and can be steered to make the model ignore irrelevant filler (restoring the full update) or to induce dilution.
Related Work: The dilution effect—non-diagnostic information weakening the implications of diagnostic information, dragging judgments toward the mean—is a robust, high-citation human finding (Nisbett, Zukier & Lemley 1981, 611 cites; Dilution and confirmation 2004; The Moral Dilution Effect 2025; perceptual-integration accounts, Hotaling/Busemeyer 2013/2015), attributed to representativeness-matching or to inferring missing evidence, and reduced by cognitive feedback (Restoration of Diluted Judgment 2008). In LLM interpretability, transformers implement (constrained) Bayesian belief updating with belief-state geometry (Belief Dynamics 2025; Constrained Belief Updates 2025; Transformers Represent Belief State Geometry 2024), belief/truth is linearly decodable (Marks & Tegmark 2023), RAG-aggregation shows LLMs are heuristic followers biased by repetition/order (Rational Synthesizers or Heuristic Followers 2026), and priming work shows new content leaks into unrelated contexts (How new data permeates 2025). Crucially, ALL LLM belief-updating interpretability treats evidence as a scalar to be weighted (by strength, prior, likelihood ratio, order, sample size) and NONE isolates whether ADDING NON-DIAGNOSTIC information dilutes the update, decodes an 'irrelevance-recognition' gate that should filter such content, defines a dilution metric against a closed-form Bayesian no-move benchmark, or causally links a decodable gate to the dilution. This differs sharply from my prior diagnosticity_axis proposal, whose core was pseudodiagnosticity (evaluating a single datum's likelihood-ratio vs one-sided fit) and which used dilution only as a secondary cross-check: here the phenomenon IS dilution—the corruption of a strong evidence's effect by appended irrelevant filler—and the mechanism is a gate that fails to zero out zero-diagnosticity content, not the mis-reading of a datum's discriminating power. It also differs from prior_likelihood_gain (prior vs likelihood weighting), sample_weight_neglect (sample size vs proportion), order_effect (non-commutativity), and causal_transparency (opaque statistic vs mechanistic framing of DIAGNOSTIC evidence). We move from 'transformers weight evidence' to 'the model fails to filter irrelevant evidence, which blunts diagnostic evidence via a decodable, steerable irrelevance gate.'
Abstract: A robust human bias, the dilution effect, is that mixing irrelevant, non-diagnostic information with genuinely diagnostic evidence weakens the diagnostic evidence's impact, pulling judgments back toward the middle—so a strong argument padded with trivia persuades less than the argument alone. As LLMs increasingly integrate mixed, noisy evidence (RAG passages, multi-source reports, padded prompts), we ask whether they inherit this dilution and whether it has a dissociable representational basis. Prior interpretability work shows LLMs update beliefs approximately Bayesianly and weight evidence by strength, prior, and order, but none isolates whether appending NON-DIAGNOSTIC information dilutes the update, nor a mechanism that should filter such irrelevant content but fails. We hypothesize a separable, near-orthogonal latent 'irrelevance-recognition' gate, decodable before the model updates, that encodes whether appended evidence is diagnostically relevant, distinct from the belief-valence direction and from the decoded strength of the diagnostic evidence; that the gate's failure to filter irrelevant filler causally dilutes the belief update (moving the posterior toward the prior/mean, against a closed-form Bayesian benchmark where zero-diagnosticity content should not move belief at all); that per-item gate-failure predicts the size of the dilution; and that steering the gate makes the model ignore filler (restoring the full update) or induces dilution. Using belief-update items where a fixed piece of diagnostic evidence is presented alone versus padded with matched amounts of non-diagnostic filler, we fit an irrelevance-recognition gate, measure separability via cross-decoding, quantify per-item dilution against the Bayesian benchmark, connect it to behavioral judgment attenuation, and perform double-dissociation steering with norm-matched and shuffled-direction controls across three model families. Our results recast a classic reasoning bias mechanistically as a decodable, steerable irrelevance-gating failure.
Experiments: 1. Graded belief-direction setup. On LLaMA-3.1-8B-Instruct, Mistral-7B-Instruct, and Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct, fit a frozen graded belief/credence direction reading a posterior over a binary hypothesis: calibrate activations against known probabilities via linear regression on explicit-probability statements (validate monotonic mapping), plus a standard true/false probe (cities, sp_en_trans, larger_than and negations; Marks & Tegmark) as a cross-check; validate on held-out items. Separately fit an EVIDENCE-STRENGTH/DIAGNOSTICITY direction decoding how strongly a stated piece of evidence supports/contradicts the hypothesis (from graded-diagnosticity stimuli), so the irrelevance gate can be dissociated from the diagnostic evidence's own strength.

2. Dilution stimulus construction with a closed-form benchmark. Build ~500 belief-update items (diagnosis, forecasting, everyday inference, person/product judgments—the classic dilution paradigm) each specifying a prior and a piece of DIAGNOSTIC evidence with an explicit/inferable likelihood ratio, so the Bayesian posterior is CLOSED-FORM. For each, create matched conditions holding the diagnostic evidence fixed: (a) DIAGNOSTIC-ALONE (only the diagnostic evidence), (b) DILUTED (the same diagnostic evidence plus one or more pieces of NON-DIAGNOSTIC filler with normative likelihood ratio ~1—true but irrelevant facts about the entity), and (c) a LENGTH-MATCHED-RELEVANT control (the diagnostic evidence plus additional genuinely diagnostic evidence of matched length, which SHOULD move belief further). Vary the amount of filler (dose) and the strength of the diagnostic evidence. Crucially, since the filler is LR~1, the Bayesian posterior is IDENTICAL for DIAGNOSTIC-ALONE and DILUTED. Validate filler non-diagnosticity with rule checks + human annotation. Use paraphrase templates; reserve held-out items/templates for transfer.

3. Irrelevance-recognition gate fitting and separability. Extract activations at a pre-update readout position (after the evidence, before the model reports the updated belief) and fit a linear probe to decode whether appended content is NON-DIAGNOSTIC filler vs additional diagnostic evidence (the irrelevance gate), controlling for the diagnostic evidence's strength. Report AUROC vs shuffled-label controls; measure cosine similarity and cross-decoding among the irrelevance-recognition gate, the graded-belief direction, and the evidence-strength direction to establish that irrelevance-recognition is (i) near-orthogonal to the belief value and (ii) not merely the diagnostic evidence's decoded strength. Localize the best layer. Critically, test whether the model CAN recognize the filler as irrelevant (the gate is decodable) even when it nonetheless dilutes—a detects-but-fails-to-filter signature.

4. Dilution metric. For each item, project onto the frozen belief direction and measure how far the belief moves from the prior toward the Bayesian posterior in DIAGNOSTIC-ALONE vs DILUTED, holding the diagnostic evidence and its normative posterior fixed. Define per-item dilution = the reduction in update magnitude (movement back toward the prior/mean) caused by appending non-diagnostic filler (which normatively should cause zero change). Core prediction: DILUTED conditions under-update relative to DIAGNOSTIC-ALONE (belief dragged toward the middle), dilution grows with the amount of filler (dose), and the LENGTH-MATCHED-RELEVANT control moves belief FURTHER (ruling out a pure length/context-dilution artifact). Report dilution across dose and diagnostic-strength with effect sizes.

5. Behavioral dilution prediction. Elicit the model's numeric posterior and stated judgment per condition. Score behavioral dilution = attenuated judgment when diagnostic evidence is padded with irrelevant filler. Test whether per-item gate-failure (the irrelevance gate reading filler as relevant, or a mismatch between gate-recognition and update behavior) predicts behavioral dilution via regression; report AUROC/R^2 vs baselines (evidence-strength axis, belief margin, output entropy, filler amount as a surface length feature, item length).

6. Dissociation from length, strength, and belief (core). Contrast DILUTED vs LENGTH-MATCHED-RELEVANT (same added length, different diagnosticity) to show dilution is driven by the added content's IRRELEVANCE, not mere context length; and on matched-diagnostic-strength items show the irrelevance gate (not the strength or belief axes) accounts for the dilution. Report incremental predictive power in nested models. Verify the decoded strength of the diagnostic evidence is unchanged across DIAGNOSTIC-ALONE vs DILUTED (so dilution is a gating failure, not a re-reading of the diagnostic evidence's strength).

7. Double-dissociation causal steering. At the pre-update position on held-out DILUTED items, steer along the irrelevance-recognition gate (orthogonalized against belief and evidence-strength) toward the 'irrelevant/filter-out' pole. Predict: amplifying the gate makes the model IGNORE the non-diagnostic filler, restoring the full DIAGNOSTIC-ALONE update (moving toward the Bayesian posterior) WITHOUT changing updates on the LENGTH-MATCHED-RELEVANT control (where the added content should count) or on DIAGNOSTIC-ALONE items; suppressing it deepens dilution. As controls, steer the evidence-strength direction (should shift update magnitude via re-read diagnostic strength) and the belief direction (should shift the posterior uniformly). Use norm-matched random-direction and shuffled-direction controls; sweep strengths and layers. Metric: change in dilution (deviation from the Bayesian no-dilution posterior) vs unchanged relevant-control behavior.

8. Application and robustness. Build a training-free calibration knob that amplifies irrelevance-recognition to filter non-diagnostic filler, and measure reduced deviation from the closed-form posterior and improved decision accuracy on held-out mixed-evidence items and a RAG-style setting where diagnostic passages are padded with irrelevant ones (report dilution reduction, decision accuracy, ECE) vs a belief-probe-only baseline. Replicate across three model families and two probe methods; transfer the fitted gate, dilution metric, and steering to held-out items/templates and an independent dilution set (adapting the classic person/product-judgment paradigm) without refitting; report per-template consistency under paraphrase and sensitivity to layer/readout position, dose, and prior magnitude. As a human-parallel analysis, check whether the dilution profile qualitatively matches the human dilution signature (judgments dragged toward the mean by irrelevant information, dose-dependent), and whether reasoning-tuned models dilute less (mirroring the cognitive-feedback-reduces-dilution finding).
Risk Factors and Limitations: The irrelevance-recognition gate may not be separable from the graded-belief or evidence-strength directions; we report cosine similarity, cross-decoding, orthogonalized steering, and incremental predictive power, and—because DILUTED and DIAGNOSTIC-ALONE share an identical Bayesian posterior and matched diagnostic evidence—belief and strength cannot trivially explain the dilution; near-collapse (the gate being merely evidence-strength or belief) is an informative negative result.

The behavioral dilution effect may be weak or reasoning/RLHF-shaped (strong or reasoning-tuned models may correctly ignore filler); a null/normative result is itself an informative human-vs-machine comparison, reported via deviation from the Bayesian benchmark, dose-response, and a reasoning-model extension.

The central confound is that appended filler adds context LENGTH, so dilution could be a generic context/length effect rather than an irrelevance-specific one; the LENGTH-MATCHED-RELEVANT control (same added length, genuinely diagnostic—should move belief FURTHER, not less) is the key test, and if dilution reduces to pure length that is a reportable finding.

An alternative human account is that dilution reflects inferring MISSING evidence from irrelevant content rather than a filtering failure; we distinguish these by testing whether the model treats filler as informative (an inference-of-missing-evidence signature) vs simply blunting the update, and report which account the gate corresponds to.

The graded belief probe is harder to calibrate than a binary truth probe and belief manifolds can be curved; we validate the activation->probability mapping, report calibration/probe-fit diagnostics, verify the diagnostic-evidence strength readout is unchanged across conditions, and treat dilution as a lower bound.

The closed-form Bayesian target assumes the model uses the stated likelihood ratio and treats filler as LR~1; models may impose their own relevance judgments on filler. We screen items where the model uses the diagnostic evidence, validate filler non-diagnosticity with human annotation, report the fraction, and treat gross non-compliance as a separate finding.

Filler content could inadvertently carry weak diagnosticity or valence; we validate LR~1 with rule checks and human annotation, balance filler valence, and include multiple filler types (neutral biographical/product trivia).
Belief/strength probes are brittle to context and surface form; we validate probes, use paraphrases, standardize the pre-update readout position, and report per-template consistency.

Causal steering is sensitive to layer and strength; we use orthogonalized steering vectors, norm-matched and shuffled-direction controls, sweep strengths, and verify gate steering restores the full update on diluted items without altering the length-matched-relevant control or degrading already-undiluted items.

Findings on 7-8B instruct models may not transfer to frontier or reasoning-tuned models; three-family replication, a reasoning-model extension, a RAG application, and independent-set transfer provide reasonable academic-budget coverage.
